creatures.name: Gan
creatures.excerpt: The Gan (also spelled Gaan or Ga'an) are sacred mountain spirit beings in Apache tradition, central to the spiritual and ceremonial life of the Western Apache, Chiricahua, and other Apache groups. The Creator, known as Usen, sent these powerful spirit beings to teach the Apache people how to live in harmony with the la

creatures.name: Gandharva (Celestial Musician)
creatures.excerpt: Gandharvas are a class of celestial beings in Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions who serve as divine musicians and singers in the courts of the gods. Originating in the Rigveda as a singular celestial being who watches over Soma, they evolved into a class of minor deities numbering 6,333 according to the Atharvaveda.

creatures.name: Ganesha
creatures.excerpt: Ganesha (Unknown). is a deity. Ganesha is the elephant-headed god of wisdom, prosperity, and obstacle removal in Hinduism. He is one of the most widely worshipped deities in the Hindu pantheon.. Source: Hindu scripture; widespread living tradition

creatures.name: Gangikozō
creatures.excerpt: Gangikozō is a yokai from Japanese folklore, known as a riverbank-dwelling water spirit that belongs to the broader kappa family of aquatic creatures. creatures.name: Gangsi
creatures.excerpt: The Gangsi is a river spirit from Korean folklore, particularly associated with the southern regions of the Korean Peninsula. creatures.name: Gara Yakka (Sinhalese Demon of Disease)
creatures.excerpt: Gara Yakka is a prominent demon in Sinhalese folklore, part of the Daha Ata Sanniya (the eighteen maladies) — a group of eighteen diseases believed to be caused by demonic possession. creatures.name: Garamantes (Ancient Desert Giants)
creatures.excerpt: The Garamantes are a legendary people of ancient Libya, described by Greco-Roman sources and Berber oral tradition as powerful desert warriors, often attributed with giant stature or superhuman abilities. creatures.excerpt: Garang is the first man in Dinka mythology of South Sudan, created alongside Abuk, the first woman, by the supreme creator Nhialic. creatures.name: Garcis (or Gartis)

creatures.name: Gardvord
creatures.excerpt: Gardvord (farm guardian) is the older, original Norwegian farm guardian spirit, predating the nisse in Norwegian folk tradition. creatures.name: Garuda
creatures.excerpt: Hindu divine eagle - King OF Birds, mount (vahana) of Vishnu. Sanskrit: 'Garuḍa' from 'gṛ' (to swallow/devour). Half-Brother of Aruna (sun's charioteer). creatures.name: Gashadokuro

creatures.name: Gast

creatures.name: Gatekeeper (Maya)

creatures.name: Gbahali
creatures.excerpt: The gbahali is a giant crocodile-like cryptid reported from the rivers, swamps and waterways of Liberia, part of local oral tradition and popular cryptozoology. creatures.name: Gbekre
creatures.excerpt: Gbekre is a powerful spirit-deity of the Baoulé people of Ivory Coast, often depicted as a baboon-like figure serving as a judge of souls and protector against evil forces. creatures.name: Geb (Earth God of Egypt)
creatures.excerpt: Geb is the Egyptian god of the earth, lying beneath his wife-sister Nut (sky). He was separated from her by their father Shu (air), who holds Nut aloft. creatures.name: Gesar of Ling
creatures.excerpt: Gesar of Ling is the culture-hero of the Tibetan epic: a warrior-prince born in humble guise who grows to unite the kingdom of Ling and slay demons across the Himalayan world. creatures.name: Geser Khan

creatures.name: Giants (Jætter)

creatures.name: Gikuyu

creatures.name: Giltinė
creatures.excerpt: Giltinė is the goddess of death in Lithuanian mythology, one of the oldest and most feared deities in the Baltic pantheon. creatures.name: Glooscap

creatures.name: Gloson
creatures.excerpt: Gloson (Glo-so, 'Glowing Sow') is a Swedish spectral boar with glowing eyes and a saw-toothed ridge along its back, charging at travelers on roads and running between their legs to split them open. creatures.name: Gluskabe

creatures.name: Gnefro

creatures.name: Goblin
creatures.excerpt: A goblin is a small, grotesque, mischievous spirit of English folklore, from the family of household and wilderness spirits that includes hobgoblins and boggarts. creatures.name: Golden Frog
creatures.excerpt: The Golden Frog is a being of Mongolian creation myth: the earth rests on a giant golden frog, and when the frog stirs, the land shakes. Sometimes shown with arrows or bolts pinning it in place, it symbolizes the fixed foundation of the world in Mongol and regional Central Asian cosmology.

creatures.name: Golem

creatures.name: Goreu
creatures.excerpt: Goreu fab Custennin is not a shapeshifting spirit but a hero of the Welsh tale Culhwch ac Olwen in the Mabinogion: son of Custennin the giant and cousin to Arthur, he joins Culhwch's quest and, at the story's end, beheads the giant chieftain Ysbaddaden, whose fortress and lands he receives. His name means 'best'.

creatures.name: Goubet Monster

creatures.name: Gramya Devata
creatures.excerpt: Gramya Devata or Gramadevata are village deities from Bengali and wider Hindu folk tradition, serving as local guardian spirits that protect specific hamlets, fields, water sources, and communities across the Indian subcontinent. creatures.name: Gravfrun
creatures.excerpt: Gravfrun (the grave lady) is a female guardian spirit of burial mounds, grave fields, and churchyards in Swedish folklore. creatures.name: Great Buzzard

creatures.name: Great Coyote (Mąʼiitoʼí Áłchíní)
creatures.excerpt: Great-Coyote-Who-Was-Formed-in-the-Water is a primordial Navajo trickster-creator of the First World. creatures.name: Great Horned Serpent

creatures.name: Great Spirit

creatures.name: Grizzly Bear Spirit

creatures.name: Grootslang

creatures.name: Gruvrået

creatures.name: Gryphon

creatures.excerpt: Gu is a spirit of the Guro people of central Ivory Coast, known as the wife of Zamble, the great mythical being of the Guro, from whom he learned how to appear to humans; her mask dances in Guro masquerades. The entry's attribution to the Mossi of Burkina Faso is mistaken; the attested tradition is Guro, not Mossi.

creatures.name: Gueno
creatures.excerpt: Gueno (also spelled Guéno) is the eternal creator god of the Fulani people, the supreme being who existed before all things. creatures.name: Gui
creatures.excerpt: Gui is the general Chinese term for ghosts or the spirits of the dead, particularly those who have died unnaturally or have unfinished business that prevents them from moving on to the afterlife. creatures.name: Guije
creatures.excerpt: Guije (Unknown). is a water-spirit. creatures.name: Gullah Frog

creatures.name: Hanako-san

Part of the huldrefolk (hidden people), she is known for her breathtaking beauty and seductive nature. creatures.name: Huldra Iceland
creatures.excerpt: Huldra Iceland (Unknown). is a forest-spirit. The Huldra is a seductive forest spirit from Norse and Scandinavian folklore. creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Icelandic tradition. 'Huldu-Elder' appears a modern invention elaborating on huldufólk ('hidden people') belief. creatures.name: Huldufolk
creatures.excerpt: Huldufolk (Unknown). is a nature-spirit. The Huldufólk ("hidden people") are elf-like beings in Icelandic folklore who live in rocks and hills. They are nearly identical to humans but invisible to most people, living parallel lives in the Ic. Source: Icelandic folklore; contemporary Icelandic tradition

creatures.name: Huldufólk
creatures.excerpt: In Iceland, huldufólk ('hidden people') are a parallel race believed to live in rocks and cliffs, largely invisible to humans. creatures.name: Huldufólk
creatures.excerpt: Huldufólk (the Hidden People) are the most pervasive supernatural beings in Faroese folklore — a parallel race living just beyond human sight. Unlike Icelandic hidden folk (often beautiful and slender), the Faroese version is consistently described as unusually large in build, with black hair and somber grey clothing.

creatures.name: Huli Jing
creatures.excerpt: Huli jing (狐精) is the fox spirit of Chinese folklore: a fox that cultivates spiritual power over centuries, gaining the ability to shapeshift, usually into a beautiful woman who seduces and drains men's vitality. It appears in tales from the Six Dynasties, including Liaozhai Zhiyi. After a thousand years it grows nine

creatures.name: Huma Bird
creatures.excerpt: The Huma Bird (also known as Homa or Homay) is a legendary mythical bird from Persian folklore and a common motif in Sufi poetry, symbolizing fortune, kingship, and spiritual transcendence. creatures.name: Humadapnon
creatures.excerpt: Humadapnon is the middle brother among three demigod heroes in the Hinilawod, the epic of the Suludnon people of Panay in the Philippines. Son of the goddess Alunsina and the mortal Datu Paubari, Humadapnon is characterized as a thoughtful strategist and skilled diplomat whose adventures balance his brother Labaw Dongg

creatures.name: Humans Denmark
creatures.excerpt: Humans Denmark (Unknown). is a spirit. Ordinary humans from Danish folklore and the Molbo stories whose common sense drives comic tales.. Source: Danish folklore — spirit/human figures documented in Danish oral tradition.

creatures.name: Humbaba

creatures.excerpt: Humbaba, originally known as Huwawa in Sumerian, is a fearsome giant and ogre-like figure from Mesopotamian mythology, best known as the divinely appointed guardian of the Cedar Forest in the Epic of Gilgamesh. Appointed by the god Enlil to protect the sacred cedars, Humbaba was a terrifying being whose voice was the D

creatures.name: Hunabal
creatures.excerpt: Hun Hunahpu (also spelled Hun-Hunahpu, meaning 'One Hunahpu') is a central figure in Maya mythology as recounted in the Popol Vuh, the sacred book of the K'iche' Maya. creatures.name: Hundred-Egg Children (Bách Việt)
creatures.excerpt: The Hundred-Egg Children (Bách Việt) are the mythical founding ancestors of the Vietnamese people, born from an egg sac laid by the mountain fairy Âu Cơ after her marriage to the dragon lord Lạc Long Quân. According to the creation myth, Âu Cơ gave birth to a sac containing one hundred eggs, which hatched into one hund

creatures.name: Huron Wendigo
creatures.excerpt: The wendigo (windigo, witiko) is a malevolent cannibal spirit of Algonquian peoples — Ojibwe, Cree, Innu, Naskapi, and Algonquin — not the Huron, whose traditions the entry wrongly implies. creatures.name: Huxhukw Kwakwaka Wakw
creatures.excerpt: Huxhukw is the supernatural crane-like cannibal bird of the Kwakwaka'wakw Hamatsa ceremony, a long-beaked attendant of the Man-Eater spirit. It cracks open the skulls of men to suck out their brains, and its masked dancer joins the crooked-beak and raven cannibal birds in the winter dance of the Cannibal Society.

creatures.name: Hydra
creatures.excerpt: The Hydra is a fearsome multi-headed serpent from Greek mythology, most famously known as the Lernaean Hydra that infested the swamps of Lerna in the Argolid. This monstrous water serpent was said to have nine heads, one of which was immortal. Its venom was so potent that even its breath or the scent of its tracks coul

creatures.name: Hyldemor
creatures.excerpt: Hyldemoren (the Elder Mother) is a Danish tree spirit who lives in elder trees (hyld). She appears as a small family of folk — men, women, and children — who emerge from the elder tree at night to help diligent housewives with their chores. They churn butter, spin wool, polish copper, and sweep floors, finishing all wo

creatures.name: Hyllemor
creatures.excerpt: Hyllemor (Elder Mother) is a protective spirit who lives in the elder tree (fläder). She appears on Christmas Eve, dressed in a green skirt and red bodice with a striped apron, watching over the tree and punishing those who disrespect it. Breaking branches from an elder tree without permission causes 'hylleskåll' — a p

creatures.name: Háldi
creatures.excerpt: Háldi (plural Háldit) are nature spirits in Sami animistic belief, the guardians and protectors of specific places, animals, and plants. creatures.name: Hóu-koô-pô
creatures.excerpt: Hóu-koô-pô (also known as Hóo-koo-pô, 'Tiger Aunt' or 'Tiger Grandma') is a terrifying figure from Taiwanese folklore — a tiger spirit from the mountains that transforms into an old woman to prey on children. The story is a classic cautionary tale used by Taiwanese parents to teach children about the dangers of trustin

creatures.name: Húlí Jīng
creatures.excerpt: Húlí Jīng (Fox Spirit) is a shapeshifting creature from Chinese mythology — a fox that gains supernatural powers through centuries of cultivation. These fox spirits are among the most complex and enduring figures in East Asian folklore, appearing in countless stories, novels, and operas across China, Korea, and Japan.

creatures.name: Hāmah
creatures.excerpt: Hāmah is a mythical creature from pre-Islamic Arabian folklore, described as a flying snake or a screech owl that emerges from the skull of a murdered person. creatures.name: Hızır
creatures.excerpt: Hızır (Khidr), the 'Green One,' is the mysterious immortal guide of Turkic and Islamic tradition, revered across Turkmen lands as the patron of travelers and the helper who appears when he is truly needed. On Hıdırellez, the sixth of May, he is honored as the renewer of spring and the bringer of good fortune.

creatures.name: Iara
creatures.excerpt: Brazilian water mermaid - 'Iara' from Old Tupi 'yîara' = 'water lady.' Origin: based on Tupi-Guarani. Early form: Ipupiara (carnivorous fish-man monster devouring fishermen). creatures.name: Iara da Praiana
creatures.excerpt: Iara da Praiana is a Brazilian coastal variant of the famous Iara legend, specifically associated with the seashores and coastal waters rather than the freshwater rivers of the Amazon. While the Amazonian Iara is a freshwater mermaid who lures fishermen, this saltwater variant sings to sailors and navigators along Braz

creatures.name: Iatiku (Life Bringer)
creatures.excerpt: Iatiku (Life Bringer) is one of the two creator sisters in Acoma Pueblo mythology. She and her sister Nautsiti were born underground at Shipapu and guided by Tsichtinako (Thought Woman). Given baskets containing seeds and animal figurines, Iatiku created the mountains, directions, plants, and animals. She created the C

creatures.name: Ibeji
creatures.excerpt: Ibeji are the sacred twin orishas of the Yoruba, representing the divine spirits of twins. The Yoruba have one of the highest twinning rates in the world, and twins are considered special beings with supernatural powers. The first-born twin is Taiwo ("the one who tastes the world") and the second is Kehinde ("the one w

creatures.name: Ibong Adarna (The Adarna Bird)
creatures.excerpt: The Ibong Adarna is a legendary magical bird from Philippine epic poetry whose song has the power to heal any sickness and whose droppings turn anyone they fall upon into stone. creatures.name: Ibonia
creatures.excerpt: Ibonia (Iboniamasiboniamanoro, 'He of the Clear and Captivating Glance') is the great epic hero of Madagascar. Conceived through divine intervention, he began speaking from his mother's womb, demanding betrothal to Iampelasoamananoro ('Girl of Grace'). After birth, Girl of Grace was abducted by Ravato ('Stone Man'). Ib

creatures.name: Icarus
creatures.excerpt: Icarus (Unknown). is a human. Icarus is a figure from Greek mythology who escaped the Labyrinth of Crete on wings made of feathers and wax by his father Daedalus. creatures.name: Ice Giant (Muisca)
creatures.excerpt: The Ice Giant is a mythical figure from Muisca mythology, the advanced pre-Columbian civilization of the Altiplano Cundiboyacense in the Colombian Andes. creatures.excerpt: Ice Maiden Denmark (Unknown). is a human. The Ice Maiden is from Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tale about a cold snow spirit who lures a young man to his death.. Source: Danish folklore — the Ice Maiden from Hans Christian Andersen and Danish oral tradition.

creatures.name: Ice-Maiden (Isjomfru)
creatures.excerpt: Isjomfru ('Ice Maiden') is a Danish winter spirit: pale, translucent skin, frost-haired, ice-gowned. Lures travelers with cold melody to freeze in snow. Inhabits frozen lakes and mountains. Vulnerable to fire, true love, spring sun. Parallels Snow Queen (Snedronningen); both stem from older winter-goddess motifs.

creatures.name: Iele
creatures.excerpt: The Iele are feminine mythical creatures in Romanian mythology, often described as faeries with great seductive power over men. creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in folklore literature. 'Ifriqiya' is the medieval Arabic name of the North African province (from the Roman Africa, named for the Berber goddess Ifri and the Afri people), not a serpent of Tunisian legend. creatures.name: Ifrit
creatures.excerpt: The ifrit is a powerful and malevolent class of jinn in Arab and Islamic tradition, famed for brute strength, cunning, and a rebellious nature. creatures.name: Ifrit (Powerful Fire Jinn)
creatures.excerpt: The Ifrit (plural: Afarit) is a powerful class of jinn in Algerian Islamic folklore, considered among the most dangerous and formidable of supernatural beings. creatures.name: Ifrit (ʿIfrīt)
creatures.excerpt: The ifrit, spelled variously ifrit and afrit, is a mighty class of rebellious fire-jinn renowned for guile and supernatural power. creatures.name: Ijapa

creatures.name: Ijimere
creatures.excerpt: Ijimere (Ethiopia). is a demon. malevolent shadow spirits from nigerian folklore who lure victims into the woods with mimicry. Source: Ethiopian folklore — Ijimere shadow demons documented in Ethiopian oral tradition.

creatures.name: Ikenga
creatures.excerpt: Ikenga is the Igbo alusi of achievement, success, strength, and the right hand. creatures.name: Iktomi
creatures.excerpt: Iktomi is the spider trickster of Lakota mythology, a complex figure who is both clever and foolish. creatures.name: Iktomi Lakota
creatures.excerpt: Iktomi is the spider trickster of the Lakota, Dakota, and Nakota peoples, a wily, foolish being whose schemes usually go wrong. creatures.name: Iku-Turso

creatures.name: Ilmarinen

creatures.name: Imehornets underjordiske

creatures.name: Imizimu
creatures.excerpt: Imizimu (Burundi). is a ancestor-spirit. Spirits of deceased relatives divided into friendly and harmful categories. Source: Burundian folklore — Imizimu ancestor spirits documented in Burundian oral tradition.

creatures.name: Impundulu

creatures.name: Ina
creatures.excerpt: A beautiful Cook Islands maiden who became the lover of the moon god Marama. Ina is the Cook Islands version of the pan-Polynesian Hina/Sina figure. creatures.name: Ina-Mita (Corn Spirit)
creatures.excerpt: Ina-Mita (Mother Corn) is the agricultural spirit of Timor-Leste who, according to Timorese tradition, sacrificed herself to provide corn (maize) to the people during a time of terrible drought. creatures.name: Inkanyamba
creatures.excerpt: Inkanyamba is a Zulu and Xhosa serpentine water spirit associated with Howick Falls (Umgeni River, KwaZulu-Natal). creatures.name: Inkarri
creatures.excerpt: The Inkarri myth is one of the most famous legends of the Inca. creatures.name: Inuarutligaks

creatures.name: Inyan
creatures.excerpt: Inyan is the primordial rock of Lakota creation, the first being who existed alongside Wakan Tanka before the world began. creatures.name: Ioi
creatures.excerpt: Ioi is the sister of Blue Jay in Chinook tradition. Taken as a wife into the land of the dead, she tried patiently to teach her brother the customs of the ghost people, but Blue Jay mocked and mishandled everything and her warnings went unheeded. Her story is a lesson in approaching the supernatural world with humility

creatures.name: Ioi Coast Salish
creatures.excerpt: Io'i is not a Coast Salish figure but the sister of Blue Jay, the trickster of Chinookan tales told at the lower Columbia River. Blue Jay and Io'i travel together in adventure stories in which Io'i repeatedly saves her foolish brother from the consequences of his boasting and meddling.

creatures.name: Ioskeha
creatures.excerpt: Ioskeha is the Good Twin and culture hero of Huron (Wyandot) tradition. creatures.name: Ira
creatures.excerpt: Ira are Bijago island ancestor spirits represented by wooden statuettes (iran) placed in family shrines (balobas), maintaining connections between living and ancestors.

creatures.name: Irrbloss
creatures.excerpt: Irrbloss, meaning "wandering blaze" in Swedish, are ghostly flickering lights seen at night in marshes, bogs, and ancient roads. creatures.name: Irrlicht

creatures.name: Isis (Goddess of Magic)
creatures.excerpt: Isis is the greatest goddess of Egyptian mythology, known as the goddess of magic, motherhood, healing, and protection. creatures.name: Isokelekel

creatures.name: Ista First Woman Nuxalk
creatures.excerpt: Ista is the First Woman of the Nuxalk (Bella Coola) origin account, who descended to the land at the beginning of the world and became mother of the people. Her story, told as a smayusta, explains the beginnings of human life and of Nuxalk society and belongs to the creation narratives of the Bella Coola.

creatures.name: Iwin
creatures.excerpt: Ìwin are a class of Yoruba spirits, often described as mischievous and elusive forest beings who guard the secrets of the bush and teach wisdom through riddles and illusions. creatures.name: J Tte
creatures.excerpt: J Tte (Unknown). is a spirit. Jatte Jattar are giants from Swedish and Nordic folklore, ancient beings who shaped the landscape with immense strength.. Source: Norwegian folklore — the Jøtte giant figure documented in Norwegian oral tradition.

creatures.name: Jack-o'-Lantern
creatures.excerpt: In African American folklore, Jack-o'-Lantern (also called Jacky-My-Lantern) is a wandering spirit who carries a flickering light through the swamps at night, luring travelers from the safety of the road into treacherous marshland. creatures.name: Jackalope
creatures.excerpt: The jackalope is a 'fearsome critter' of American tall-tale tradition: a jackrabbit with antelope horns, said to mimic human voices and be lured with whiskey. The attested figure is

creatures.name: Korkut Ata
creatures.excerpt: Korkut Ata is the legendary sage-musician of the Oghuz Turks, revered across Kazakhstan as a wise, artistic culture hero. His lament for the impermanence of the world is said to have given birth to the kobyz, the bowed Kazakh instrument, granting a kind of immortality through music and story. His legacy survives in the

creatures.name: Korkyt
creatures.excerpt: Korkyt is the legendary founding father of Kazakh music, a revered sage, composer, poet, and philosopher who is credited with creating the kobyz, an ancient Kazakh stringed instrument, as well as the dombra, the national instrument of Kazakhstan. According to tradition, Korkyt lived for three hundred years, traveling t

creatures.name: Kosen
creatures.excerpt: 'Kosen' garbles the attested yokai kosenjobi ('ancient battlefield fire'): ghost-flames rising over old killing grounds from the blood of fallen warriors and horses. creatures.name: Kosenjōbi
creatures.excerpt: Kosenjōbi are ghost-fires of Japanese folklore: will-o'-the-wisp flames that appear over old battlefields, said to be the spirits of soldiers and horses killed in war, rising from the ground at dusk. creatures.name: Koshari (sacred clowns)
creatures.excerpt: Koshari are the sacred clowns in Pueblo tradition, known for their role in ceremonial dances and rituals. Unlike ordinary entertainers, the Koshari serve a vital spiritual function by mocking pretension, exposing hypocrisy, and reinforcing social norms through humor. creatures.name: Kostroma
creatures.excerpt: Kostroma is an East Slavic spring-and-summer fertility figure of Russian folk ritual, honored during Semik as a straw effigy or a disguised girl who is first revered and then burned or drowned to end the season's rites. creatures.name: Koumen
creatures.excerpt: Koumen is the primordial shepherd of the Fulani, custodian of pastoral initiation, who appears as a child of three to eleven. With his wife Foroforondu he passes the secret knowledge of cattle to initiates (Sile); those who complete the cycle gain mastery of ritual speech as Silatigi. Documented in Griaule and Dieterle

creatures.name: Kowi Anukasha
creatures.excerpt: The Kowi Anukasha are the little people of the Choctaw, spirit dwellers of the forests whose name means 'forest dwellers.' creatures.name: Koyemshi (Mudhead clowns)
creatures.excerpt: The Koyemshi, or Mudhead clowns, are the sacred clowns of the Zuni. Their origin myth tells of a father who fathered nine children with his sister and, in remorse, rolled in the mud until his head was covered in bulbous welts; his children were born with the same knobs. creatures.name: Koyemsi
creatures.excerpt: Koyemsi, also known as the Mudhead or Kachina Clown, is a distinctive figure in Hopi and Puebloan spiritual traditions of the Southwestern United States. creatures.name: Krahang
creatures.excerpt: Krahang is a malevolent nocturnal spirit from Laotian and Thai folklore, a cursed ghost that takes the form of a shirtless man who flies through the night sky using traditional rice winnowing baskets as makeshift wings. This terrifying apparition is said to be the result of a curse placed upon a man who practiced forbi

creatures.name: Krahom
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in folklore literature. creatures.name: Kraken
creatures.excerpt: The Kraken is a legendary colossal sea monster said to dwell off the coasts of Norway and Greenland. Described as a giant octopus or squid-like creature, the Kraken was feared by Norwegian fishermen for its ability to drag entire ships and crews to the ocean depths. creatures.name: Krakonoš

creatures.name: Krishna
creatures.excerpt: Krishna is one of the most venerated deities of Hinduism: the eighth avatar of Vishnu and, in Vaishnavism, the Supreme Being in his own right. creatures.name: Kulmking
creatures.excerpt: A hostile forest spirit of Estonian tradition, the kulmking (linked to Estonian 'külm', cold) is a malevolent being of the woods, bogs and remote wilds, dreaded more than the neutral forest guardians of Estonian nature belief and associated with the unholy dead. It is said to waylay travelers who enter its territory.

creatures.name: Kulshedra

creatures.name: Kumbhakarna (Sleeping Giant)
creatures.excerpt: Kumbhakarna is a powerful rakshasa and the younger brother of Ravana from the Hindu epic Ramayana. creatures.name: Kupua

creatures.name: Kuutkh (Kutkh)

creatures.name: Loa

creatures.name: Lobisomem
creatures.excerpt: The lobisomem is the Portuguese werewolf, a person cursed to run out a fado (spell) at night as an animal — in the north a horse, in the south a donkey, dog, or pig. creatures.excerpt: The lobisón is the werewolf of Galician folklore, the regional form of the Iberian lobishome. creatures.name: Lohiau
creatures.excerpt: Lohiau was a handsome chief of Kauai loved by the volcano goddess Pele. When Pele saw Lohiau in a dream, she fell deeply in love. She sent her sister Hi'iaka to retrieve him. creatures.name: Long

creatures.name: Long-Ears
creatures.excerpt: Long-Ears is a monster of Seminole tradition, a four-footed, wolf-headed creature the size of a donkey with long, pointed ears and an insatiable hunger. It hunts people in the swamps and forests of Florida, and its great speed, cunning, and tracking ability make it one of the most feared beings in Seminole legend.

creatures.name: Lono

creatures.name: Loogaroo

creatures.name: Loon (Creation Bird)
creatures.excerpt: The loon, also called the golden or diving bird, is the creation bird of Altai mythology, small but infinitely courageous, diving into the infinite primordial ocean and risking its life to bring up the mud from which the earth is made. creatures.name: Lord of the Gobi

creatures.excerpt: The Lord of the Gobi is a desert spirit of southern Mongolia, described as a towering figure of sand and wind, sometimes a dust devil, that can also appear as an old man or a shimmering form in the heat haze. creatures.name: Lorelei

creatures.name: Los Ahuiillas
creatures.excerpt: Los Ahuiillas (or Ahuillas) are Peruvian Andean road spirits: ghosts of murdered travelers who appear at night near abandoned houses and mountain paths. They warn or terrify passersby, reflecting colonial-era dangers on highland routes. Documented in central/southern Peru oral tradition.

creatures.name: Los Chamos
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a folkloric goblin. 'Los Chamos' is a famous 1980s Venezuelan boy band; 'chamo' is Venezuelan slang for 'kid/guy.' creatures.name: Lost Little Ones (transformed children)
creatures.excerpt: The Lost Little Ones are the Zuni children who, crossing the sacred river in the care of the Beloved Twins, fell into the water and were transformed into frogs, lizards, turtles, and newts. creatures.name: Louhi

creatures.name: Luna

creatures.name: Makonde Witchcraft Spirits (Uchawi)
creatures.excerpt: Among the Makonde of northern Mozambique, witchcraft (uchawi) is a real and powerful tradition involving spirits deployed by malevolent practitioners and by healers. Belief distinguishes inherited witchcraft, learned sorcery, and spirit-chosen witchcraft; the power is used to harm or to protect, and accusations are adj

creatures.name: Malahas Nuu Chah Nulth
creatures.excerpt: Malahas, the Woman of the Woods in Nuu-chah-nulth tradition, lures children into the forest and is a standing threat to village families. In the myth cycle she steals the children of a woman of the lineage; the hero Andaokut, born from that woman's tears or mucus, later finds her and kills her, returning the children.

creatures.name: Malakas (The First Man)
creatures.excerpt: In Tagalog creation myth, Malakas (Strong) is the first human man, who together with Maganda (Beautiful), emerged from a split bamboo stalk. According to the myth, the world began as a vast emptiness with only the sky and the sea. A huge bird (believed to be the deity Amihan) grew tired of flying and stirred up the sea

creatures.name: Malin Kundang
creatures.excerpt: Malin Kundang is the tragic protagonist of West Sumatra's most famous folktale, a cautionary story about filial ingratitude. A poor boy from a fishing village, Malin Kundang leaves his widowed mother to seek fortune overseas. After years of hardship, he becomes a wealthy merchant, marries a princess, and returns home i

creatures.name: Malina
creatures.excerpt: Malina is the Sun goddess of Greenlandic Inuit tradition, sister of Aningaat the Moon. Fleeing her brother's pursuit after he wronged her, she cast seal-oil and soot into his face as she rose into the sky; she became the sun and he the moon, and he still chases her, his face darkened, so that the waxing moon and the ra

creatures.name: Malmkarlen
creatures.excerpt: Malmkarlen (the ore man) is a male mining spirit in Swedish folklore, the counterpart to the female Gruvrået. He appears as a small, gray-clad miner with a leather apron and a mining lamp on his cap. Malmkarlen dwells in the deepest shafts and most dangerous passages of iron and copper mines in Bergslagen. Unlike the o

creatures.name: Malsumis
creatures.excerpt: Malsumis is the evil twin brother of Gluskabe in Abenaki tradition, born from the divine dust of Tabaldak's hands alongside his brother. From birth, Malsumis resented his brother and plotted to destroy him. He created only evil — dangerous animals, thorns, and crooked rivers that flooded the land. He tricked the animal

creatures.name: Mama Cocha
creatures.excerpt: Mama Qucha (Mama Cocha, 'Mother Sea/Lake') is the Inca goddess of the sea, lakes, and all waters. Wife of Wiraqucha, mother of Inti (Sun) and Mama Killa (Moon). One of four Elemental Mothers with Pachamama, Mama Nina, Mama Wayra. Worshipped by coastal peoples for calm seas and good fishing; snip inland peoples honored

creatures.name: Mama D'Leau
creatures.excerpt: Mama D'Leau, also known as Mama Glo or Mama D'Lo, is the Mother of Water in Dominican and wider Caribbean folklore. She is the wife of Papa Bois and the fierce guardian of rivers, streams, and water creatures. Described as having a beautiful woman's upper body and the lower body of a massive serpent, she uses her encha

creatures.name: Mama D'Leau
creatures.excerpt: Mama D'Leau is the Mother of Water in Saint Lucian folklore — the wife of Papa Bois and the fierce guardian of the island's rivers and streams. Saint Lucia, like Dominica, is known for its abundant rivers, and Mama D'Leau is believed to watch over each one. She has the upper body of a beautiful woman with long flowing

creatures.name: Mama Djombo
creatures.excerpt: Mama Djombo of Guinea-Bissau is a restless forest spirit that maintains transnational connections through diaspora support and protective shrine worship.

creatures.name: Mama Dlo
creatures.excerpt: Mama Dlo (Mother of Waters) is the Saint Lucian water spirit, upper body a beautiful woman with long flowing hair perpetually combing, lower body serpentine. Inhabits mountain pools and streams. A Caribbean manifestation of the West African Mami Wata/Mama Wata tradition brought by enslaved Africans. Can grant wealth or

creatures.name: Mama Glo
creatures.excerpt: Mama Glo, also known as Mama D'Leau or Mama D'Lo, is the Mother of Water in Grenadian folklore. Of African origin, she is the wife of Papa Bois and the guardian of all rivers and water bodies on the island. She is described as having a beautiful woman's upper body with long hair and a golden comb, and the lower body of

creatures.name: Maman Brigitte (Queen of the Cemetery)
creatures.excerpt: Maman Brigitte is the powerful female lwa of death, cemeteries, and the underworld in Haitian Vodou. She is the wife of Baron Samedi, the master of the dead, and together they rule the Gede family of spirits. She is depicted as a pale-skinned woman with long red or black hair, dressed in black and purple mourning cloth

creatures.name: Mamba Muntu
creatures.excerpt: Mamba Muntu (or Mami Muntu, Dona Fish) is the Central African variant of Mami Wata — a mermaid-like water spirit/goddess venerated in Angola, DRC, and Congo. Traced to 15th-century European mermaid depictions, her iconography later absorbed the 1880s Hamburg snake-charmer lithograph of Nala Damajanti and Hindu imagery

creatures.name: Mambabarang
creatures.excerpt: Witchcraft has been present throughout the Philippines even before Spanish colonization, and is associated with indigenous Philippine folk religions, where Philippine shamans, who people come to for healing and rituals, are known to counter the magic of Philippine witches, who people fear. Its practice involves black m

creatures.name: Mame Coumba Bang
creatures.excerpt: Mame Coumba Bang (Unknown). is a human. Mame Coumba Bang is a legendary figure from Senegal, a beautiful princess associated with the Saint-Louis region. Her story is central to the oral traditions of the Wolof people.. Source: Wolof oral tradition; Senegalese folklore

creatures.name: Mami Wata
creatures.excerpt: Mami Wata of Liberia appears as a beautiful water spirit who grants wealth, beauty, and luck in exchange for offerings and sexual celibacy. Her cult blends indigenous water deities with Hindu, Islamic, and colonial European imagery, making her one of the most complex and widely recognized water spirits along the West A

creatures.name: Mami Wata
creatures.excerpt: Mami Wata of Nigeria manifests as a seductive mermaid goddess with long hair and a fish tail, believed to control the sea, storms, and fortune. Her devotees enter trance states and spirit marriage, and her cult is deeply tied to coastal communities, fishing economies, and trade along the Bight of Benin.

creatures.name: Mami Wata
creatures.excerpt: Mami Wata is a powerful West African water goddess of wealth and beauty who grants prosperity while demanding spiritual devotion and celibacy from her devotees.

creatures.name: Mami Wata
creatures.excerpt: Mami Wata of Senegal is a seductive mermaid goddess of wealth and the waters, representing both allure and dangerous power in Senegalese coastal communities.

creatures.name: Mami Wata
creatures.excerpt: Mami Wata of the Gambia is a beautiful mermaid water spirit who grants wealth, luck, and fertility in exchange for offerings and sexual celibacy. She appears in rivers and the sea, holds protective maritime powers, and her cult blends indigenous beliefs with colonial-era imagery along the Gambia coast.

creatures.name: Mami Wata
creatures.excerpt: Mami Wata of Senegal is a seductive water spirit with wealth-granting powers, reflecting historical tensions between tradition and material aspiration.

creatures.name: Mami Wata
creatures.excerpt: Mami Wata is a water spirit widely venerated along the Ivory Coast, appearing as a beautiful, seductive woman, often half fish or serpent, who grants wealth, success, and children in exchange for offerings, spirit marriage, and ritual devotion. Her cult blends local lagoon and river deities with imported imagery, makin

creatures.name: Mami Wata
creatures.excerpt: Mami Wata is a water spirit widely venerated in Benin, appearing as a beautiful, seductive woman, often half fish or serpent, who grants wealth, children, and fortune in exchange for offerings and ritual devotion. The cult thrives in coastal towns and blends Fon, Yoruba, and imported imagery, with temples serving as ce

creatures.name: Mami Wata
creatures.excerpt: Mami Wata is known in parts of Burkina Faso through the spread of the West African water-spirit cult along trade routes, where she appears as a beautiful, seductive woman granting wealth and children in exchange for offerings and celibacy. Her inland temples cluster near rivers and sacred pools of the Volta basin.

creatures.name: Mamlambo
creatures.excerpt: Mamlambo is a fearsome shapeshifting water deity of the Zulu and Xhosa peoples, often described as a giant serpent with a horse's head or a beautiful woman who lures men to their doom. She controls the waters, causing floods when angered and droughts when she withdraws. Those who seek her for wealth must make terrible

creatures.name: Mammoth (Great Underground Bull)
creatures.excerpt: In Yakut (Sakha) tradition the mammoth is the Great Underground Bull, a massive creature with huge tusks, thick shaggy fur, and a body that shakes the earth underground. Solitary and reclusive, it avoids sunlight; when it dies its body causes geological upheaval, and it is linked to tremors and mysterious giant bones.

creatures.name: Manananggal
creatures.excerpt: The manananggal is a vampiric creature of Philippine folklore, a woman by day who at night separates her upper torso, grows leathery wings, and flies out to hunt. She preys especially on pregnant women, extending a long tongue to suck the unborn child, and must rejoin her lower half before dawn. Her night flights warne

creatures.name: Manas
creatures.excerpt: Manas is the legendary hero who united the scattered Kyrgyz tribes and namesake of one of the world's longest epic poems. The Kyrgyz trilogy 'Manas, Semetey, Seytek,' inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List, tells of tribes united into one nation. Tellers of both sexes and all ages recite it, often after a prophetic

creatures.name: Manasa
creatures.excerpt: Manasa is the Hindu snake-goddess worshipped across Bengal for snakebite protection, fertility, prosperity. Daughter of Kashyapa (or Shiva in Mangalkavyas), sister of Vasuki, wife of Jaratkaru, mother of Astika. Central to Manasamangal Kavya (Bengali medieval epics). Worshipped via cactus branch, earthen pot, snake ima

creatures.name: Manasa
creatures.excerpt: Manasa is the Hindu snake-goddess worshipped across Bengal for snakebite protection, fertility, prosperity. Daughter of Kashyapa, sister of Vasuki, wife of Jaratkaru, mother of Astika. Central to Manasamangal Kavya (Bengali medieval epics). Worshipped via cactus branch, earthen pot, snake image; festival Nag Panchami.

creatures.name: Manco Cápac
creatures.excerpt: Manco Cápac (Manqu Qhapaq) is the legendary founder and first Sapa Inca of Cusco (c. 1200 CE). In the Ayar brothers legend, he emerges from Paqariq Tampu with a golden staff, disposes of his brothers, and founds Cusco. In the Inti legend, he is the son of Sun god Inti and Moon goddess Mama Killa, sent from Lake Titicac

creatures.name: Mandinka Forest Spirit
creatures.excerpt: The Mandinka Forest Spirit of Gambia tests travelers with tricks while protecting wilderness areas, teaching moral lessons through cunning encounters.

creatures.name: Mandukhai Khatun
creatures.excerpt: Mandukhai Khatun, 'Mandukhai the Wise,' is the legendary warrior-queen of 15th-century Mongolia, a noble queen in traditional headdress and armor who wields twin swords while riding horseback. A warrior who led armies into battle and a wise counselor in statecraft, she fought to reunify the Mongol nation alongside Daya

creatures.name: Mangadhai
creatures.excerpt: Mangadhai are the monstrous giants of the Mongolian steppe, destructive ogre-beings of superhuman strength and size who oppose the epic heroes. In tradition they can be countered through wit, strategic traps, and elders' knowledge. Mangadhai is essentially the same figure as the multi-headed mangas of Mongol epic (see

creatures.name: Mangus (Mangadhai)
creatures.excerpt: Mangus (Mangadhai) are the multi-headed chaos-monsters of Mongol epic tradition, gigantic ogre-like beings often bearing 15, 25, or even 100 heads, with iron bodies, fangs, and claws. They devour livestock and people and battle the epic heroes, yet their souls are hidden outside the body in an animal or object, making

creatures.name: Mannbjørn
creatures.excerpt: Mannbjørn (man-bear) is a werebear in Norwegian folklore — a human who can transform into a bear. In Norwegian tradition, the bear transformation was more common than the werewolf of continental European folklore. The mannbjørn could transform by putting on a bearskin, by drinking a magical potion, or through a family

creatures.name: Mannegishi
creatures.excerpt: The Mannegishi (also known as Awwakkule, Nirumbee) are the Little People of Crow and Cree folklore—small, bald humanoid beings with large bulging eyes and tiny tan bodies. They are tricksters who live in rocky areas, along riverbanks, and especially in the Pryor Mountains of Montana. These beings are known for playing

creatures.name: Manticore
creatures.excerpt: The Manticore is a man-eating beast of Persian legend recorded by Ctesias and Pliny: a lion's body, a human face, and a tail like a scorpion's stinger that fires poison spines; its three rows of teeth devour humans whole, leaving no bones. The name is the Persian mardkhor ('man-eater'). From Iran it passed into medieva

creatures.name: Manup
search_terms: manup papua new guinea agriculture hero
creatures.excerpt: Manup is a mythical culture hero from northeastern Papua New Guinea, the brother of Kilibob. While his brother Kilibob traveled along the northern coast, Manup took a southern route and brought agriculture, domesticated animals, and ceremonial practices to the people. Wherever he landed, he left behind different langua

creatures.name: Mapinguari
creatures.excerpt: The Mapinguari is a giant hairy cryptid of Brazilian Amazon folklore (Tupi-Guarani mbaé-pi-guari: 'thing with twisted feet'). Described as monkey-like, bipedal, with backwards feet, a single eye (forehead or belly), a vertical mouth from nose to stomach, and foul odor. Bulletproof except at navel. Devours human heads.

creatures.name: Mara
creatures.excerpt: Mara (Swedish: mara; Old Norse: mara) is a malicious female night-spirit in Germanic and Slavic folklore who 'rides' sleepers' chests, causing suffocating nightmares (Swedish: mardröm) and sleep paralysis. Attested in Ynglinga saga (13th c.) where King Vanlandi is killed by a mara sent by Finnish sorceress Huld.

creatures.name: Mara
creatures.excerpt: Mara (mora) is a Slavic night spirit who torments sleepers, pressing on their chests and causing nightmares and sleep paralysis. In Ukrainian folk belief she appears as a shadowy woman or animal and can be warded off with prayers, salt, or blessed objects; her name is linked to the crushing motion of the night and to t

creatures.name: Mara
creatures.excerpt: Mara (Icelandic). is a spirit. A malevolent spirit that causes suffocating nightmares by sitting on the sleeper's chest. Source: Icelandic folklore, Nordic mythology

creatures.name: Marabout
creatures.excerpt: Marabout is an Islamic saint figure venerated across the Sahel, serving as intermediaries between people and spiritual forces with protective amulets.

creatures.name: Marawa
creatures.excerpt: Marawa is a spider spirit and important figure in Banks Islands mythology of Vanuatu. He appears as the companion and sometimes antithesis of the creator god Qat. While Qat created humans from dracaena wood and brought them to life by playing drums, Marawa grew envious and attempted to imitate Qat's creation. He made h

creatures.name: Mare
creatures.excerpt: Maren (the Mare) is the Danish nightmare spirit — a female entity who sits on sleeping people's chests, pressing the air from their lungs and causing terrifying dreams. In Danish folklore, the Mare is a shape-shifter who can take the form of a cat, a dog, an owl, a horse, or even a straw. She is blamed for sleep paraly

creatures.name: Mare
creatures.excerpt: The Mare (Danish: Maren) is the Danish nightmare spirit, a female being who sits on sleepers' chests and presses the breath from them, causing the terror known as mareridt. creatures.name: Mare (Germanic)
creatures.excerpt: The Mare (Old High German mara, Old Norse mara, Old English mære) is a female nightmare spirit in Germanic and Slavic folklore. She 'rides' sleepers' chests, causing suffocation, sleep paralysis, and nightmares — the word 'nightmare' derives from her (Old English nihtmare, 'mare-ride').

creatures.name: Margyge
creatures.excerpt: Margyge (also margygr, from Old Norse marr = sea + gygr = ogress) is a grotesque female sea monster in Norwegian medieval literature, first described in Konungs skuggsjá (The King's Mirror, c. The margyge is a hideous sea creature that appears before storms and shipwrecks as a dire omen. Unlike beautiful mermaids of la

creatures.name: Mari
creatures.excerpt: Mari is the supreme goddess of Basque religion, a powerful spirit associated with caves, mountains, weather, and the cycles of nature. She appears as a beautiful woman or a terrible dragon and may bring blessing or destruction, rewarding respect and punishing violation of her taboos. She is the central figure of Basque

creatures.name: Maria Makiling (Mariang Makiling)
creatures.excerpt: Maria Makiling is the most famous diwata (nature spirit/goddess) in Philippine mythology, the guardian spirit of Mount Makiling in Laguna. She is a breathtakingly beautiful young woman with long black hair and radiant white clothing who protects the mountain's forests, wildlife, and the people who depend on them. Pre-c

creatures.name: Marid
creatures.excerpt: The Marid are the most powerful class of jinn in Arabian tradition — mighty, proud and rebellious spirits of smokeless fire, often bound to water and the sea. Blue-hued giants in the Thousand and One Nights, they can become invisible, shapeshift and grant wishes, but twist them maliciously; some serve as guardians of h

creatures.name: Maring
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a forest spirit of Papua New Guinea. The name 'Maring' belongs to a highlands ethnolinguistic group of the Jimi Valley, documented in Roy Rappaport's ethnography Pigs for the Ancestors, not to a spirit being; no source records a 'Maring' tree-spirit. The long-limbed forest being is likely

creatures.name: Marjatta
creatures.excerpt: Marjatta is the virgin maiden of Kalevala (runo 50) who conceives a son after eating a lingonberry. Her child is presented to Väinämöinen; when he orders the infant killed, the babe speaks and is crowned King of Karelia. Her story, compiled by Lönnrot from Karelian runic songs, marks the Christianized conclusion of the

creatures.name: Marmennil
creatures.excerpt: Marmennil (Marmennilin) is a mischievous merman from Faroese folklore who lives at the bottom of the sea near Elduvík on Eysturoy. creatures.name: Marmæle
creatures.excerpt: Marmæle (also called marmennil) is a small prophetic merman in Norwegian folklore, first described in Konungs skuggsjá (The King's Mirror, c. This child-sized, half-human half-fish creature was believed to dwell in the deep waters off the coast of Norway, particularly along the Vestlandet fjords. Fishermen who caught a

creatures.name: Marraco
creatures.excerpt: El Marraco is the dragon of Lleida in Catalan folklore, depicted as a wingless green dragon with sharp claws and, in older accounts, linked to the ancient Ilergetes, whose chieftains were said to descend from a dragon deity. Today it appears in the city's festive processions (bestiari), preserving a folk memory of pre-

creatures.name: Masalai
creatures.excerpt: Masalai are a class of supernatural place-spirits found throughout Papua New Guinea's diverse cultures. Margaret Mead defined them as supernatural beings inhabiting specific locations distinguished by notable natural features such as waterholes, waterfalls, river bends, cliffs, or marshes. They exercise limited jurisdi

creatures.name: Masauwu (Skeleton Man, Spirit of Death)
creatures.excerpt: Masauwu, called Skeleton Man, is the Hopi spirit of death, fire, and the underworld, and owner of the land of the Fourth World. creatures.name: Masca
creatures.excerpt: Masche are the witches of Piedmontese tradition, women who inherited supernatural powers across generations, able to change into animals, fly, and cast spells. creatures.name: Masewi (Twin War God)
creatures.excerpt: Masewi is one of the Twin War Gods in Pueblo (specifically Acoma) tradition, brother to Oyoyewi. These twins are among the most important heroic figures in Pueblo mythology. They were born to a virgin mother who conceived from the Sun. The twins are credited with creating the world and all living creatures, slaying the

creatures.name: Masmasalanicw (Four Carpenters)
creatures.excerpt: Masmasalanicw, the Four Carpenters, are the winged creators of Nuxalk (Bella Coola) tradition who worked in the House of Smayusta at the beginning of time. Led by the eldest, Yulm, they assisted the Creator Alhkw'ntam in fashioning the world; Yulm made Raven from a lump of charcoal, and each carpenter brought a special

creatures.name: Masmasalanicw Four Carpenters Nuxalk
creatures.excerpt: The Masmasalanicw, the Four Carpenters, are the supernatural craftsmen of Nuxalk (Bella Coola) creation who shaped the world under the direction of the Creator. They made the mountains, rivers, and forests, fashioned the first creatures, and established the pattern of the land that the Nuxalk people know.

creatures.name: Matau
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a named eel deity of Fijian folklore. While eels (waqawaqa, duna) are widely sacred in Fiji — Degei, the great serpent of Nakauvadra, and the guardian eel of Naqali pool being documented examples — no source records an eel spirit called 'Matau'. The entry appears to generalise the region's

creatures.name: Mate Bein (Ancestral Ghost)
creatures.excerpt: In Tetum cosmology of East Timor, Mate Bein are the ancestral ghosts who occupy a central role in the spiritual world. Unlike malevolent spirits, these ghosts are the transformed souls of the deceased who become agencies for life-affirming fertility after proper ritual action. The soul of a person (klamar mate) transit

creatures.name: Matlose Nuu Chah Nulth
creatures.excerpt: Matlose is a hobgoblin of Nuu-chah-nulth tradition, described in early accounts as a Caliban-like spirit of the woods. His head is said to be only half like a man's, his body horrid with black bristles, his teeth monstrous, and his hands armed with bear-like claws. His voice fells listeners, and a single stroke of his

creatures.name: Matsieng
creatures.excerpt: Matsieng is a powerful one-legged giant from Tswana tradition, considered the first ancestor of the Batswana people. According to legend, Matsieng emerged from a waterhole in southeastern Botswana, followed by his people, domestic animals, and wildlife, all sinking their feet into the soft, unformed early earth. Their

creatures.name: Matsya
creatures.excerpt: Matsya (Fish) is the first avatar of Vishnu in the Dashavatara. In Shatapatha Brahmana, a fish saves Manu from the great flood; later Puranas identify it as Vishnu. Matsya warns Manu, has him build a boat, tows it to Himalayas with Vedas, sages, seeds. In Bhagavata Purana, slays demon Hayagriva who stole the Vedas. Dep

creatures.name: Matsyendranath (Karunamaya)
creatures.excerpt: Matsyendranath, also known as Karunamaya ('the compassionate one') and Red Machindranath, is one of the most important deities in Nepali Buddhism and Hinduism, revered as the god of rain and compassion. The central legend tells of a devastating 12-year drought that struck the Kathmandu Valley, caused by the demon Bhasm

creatures.name: Matuku
creatures.excerpt: Matuku-tangotango is the giant man-eating bird of Māori tradition, a monstrous owl-like creature who swallowed the ancestress Whaitiri and devoured travellers. creatures.name: Maui
creatures.excerpt: In Hawaiian tradition, Māui is the trickster demigod and culture hero who fished up the islands with his enchanted fishhook (the constellation Māui's Fishhook), snared the sun to lengthen the day, and drew fire from the depths. The youngest and cleverest of brothers, he used cunning rather than strength to aid humanity

creatures.name: Maui
creatures.excerpt: In Māori tradition, Māui is the great demigod and trickster who fished up Te Ika-a-Māui, the North Island, from the sea with a hook made from the jawbone of his grandmother Murirangawhenua, his canoe becoming Te Waka a Māui, the South Island. He slowed the sun, stole fire from Mahuika, and sought immortality from Hine-

creatures.name: Maui (Polynesian)
creatures.excerpt: The great Polynesian trickster demigod and cultural hero whose exploits are celebrated across the Pacific. Maui performed many legendary feats: he fished up the North Island of New Zealand (Te Ika-a-Maui) using a magical fishhook made from his ancestor's jawbone; he slowed the sun to make days longer by capturing Taman

creatures.name: Maure the Briden
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Algerian folklore. Maure the Briden is described as a sea goddess of the Mediterranean who commands storms and shelters coastal villages, a water spirit bound to the shore and offended by pollution of the sea. The garbled name suggests a modern invention conflating the classic siren type w

creatures.name: Mauve Sorciere
creatures.excerpt: The mauve sorcière is a witch figure of French folklore identified by Claude Lecouteux, whose name refers to the purple-tinged assemblies of witches, perhaps tied to the Devil's Sabbath. These gatherings at crossroads and isolated places mark the color mauve as the hue of the witches' supernatural realm. The figure con

creatures.name: Mavka
creatures.excerpt: Mavka (plural mavky) are Ukrainian forest spirits, the souls of unbaptized or drowned maidens, who dance in the fields and lure young men into the woods. In Ukrainian folklore and literature they are both beautiful and deadly, vanishing at dawn; the name is linked to the Slavic root for the dead.

creatures.name: Mawu
creatures.excerpt: Mawu is the supreme creator goddess of the Fon (Dahomey) and Ewe peoples of Benin and Togo. She is the goddess of the moon, night, fertility, and motherhood. Often paired with Lisa, the sun god, they form the dual-sexed creator deity Mawu-Lisa. Mawu created the cosmos, the earth, and humanity. According to Fon cosmolog

creatures.name: May and Gilan
creatures.excerpt: Mayy and Ghīlān are the legendary founding couple of Qatari tradition — a beloved hikâya told for generations about a heroic pair whose story is celebrated as a foundational myth of the peninsula. Cast as brave, protective figures of courage and unity, they embody the protector spirit of the Qatari people in oral story

creatures.name: Maya Mriga (Golden Deer)
creatures.excerpt: The Maya Mriga (Golden Deer) is a pivotal illusionary creature from the Ramayana, created by the rakshasa Maricha at Ravana's command. To enable Ravana's abduction of Sita, Maricha transformed himself into a mesmerizing golden deer with silver spots and jewel-like horns that appeared to be made of precious metals and g

creatures.name: Mayohiga
creatures.excerpt: Mayohiga (迷い家) is a phantom house of Japanese mountain folklore, recorded in Yanagita Kunio's 1910 Tōno Monogatari. It appears at dusk on remote paths and in deep valleys; those who enter may take food or goods, and some return wealthy, while others who stay too long are never seen again. It is a supernatural dwelling

creatures.name: Mazimu
creatures.excerpt: Mazimu are ancestral spirits of the Tumbuka people (Malawi, eastern Zambia, Tanzania). They dwell near family graves, monitoring descendants, offering protection or punishment. creatures.name: Mba-Katrè
creatures.excerpt: Mba-Katrè is the hyena of Mossi (Moose) folktales in Burkina Faso, the gluttonous, foolish trickster outwitted at every turn by the cunning hare Mba-Soamba. creatures.name: Mba-Soêmba
creatures.excerpt: Mba-Soêmba is the clever hare trickster figure in Mossi folklore of Burkina Faso, the wise and cunning counterpart to the foolish hyena Mba-Katrè. creatures.name: Mbatian
creatures.excerpt: Mbatian was the most powerful laibon (spiritual leader/prophet) in Maasai history, a legendary figure of the late 19th century descended from the sacred Inkindongi clan (Oloiboni clan). His prophetic powers were unrivaled -- he could predict droughts, locate lost cattle, communicate directly with Enkai, and control the

creatures.name: Mbe (Tortoise)
creatures.excerpt: Mbe the Tortoise is the cunning trickster of Igbo folklore, a small creature who uses his intelligence to overcome larger, stronger animals — and often his own greed leads to his downfall. In the most famous Igbo story, Mbe was once a bird with a beautiful shell who borrowed feathers to fly to a heavenly feast. Through

creatures.name: Mbenga (or Mokèlé-mbèmbé)
creatures.excerpt: Mokèlé-mbèmbé ('one who stops the flow of rivers') is a cryptid of the Congo Basin reported since 1913 by German Captain von Stein. Described as a long-necked, herbivorous, elephant-sized creature with smooth skin, it supposedly lives in riverbank caves and attacks canoes.

creatures.name: Mbidi Kiluwe
creatures.excerpt: Mbidi Kiluwe is the legendary culture hero and founding father of Luba sacred kingship (bulopwe). According to Luba oral tradition, Mbidi Kiluwe was a mysterious prince from the east, distinguished by his refined, dignified manners. He arrived at the court of King Nkongolo Mwamba, the crude and violent red-skinned rule

creatures.name: Mbona
creatures.excerpt: Mbona is a legendary rain-bringing prophet and martyr from Chewa and Mang'anja mythology of Malawi. Unlike purely mythical figures, Mbona may be based on a historical figure who lived around the 16th century. According to tradition, Mbona possessed extraordinary magic powers: he could bring rain during droughts, create

creatures.name: Mboreví
creatures.excerpt: Mboreví (Mborevi) are miniature forest-dwelling nature spirits in Guaraní tradition (Paraguay, NE Argentina, S Brazil). Described as small protective people who guard the forest and its creatures. They punish those who harm nature and can be appeased with offerings. Closely related to Pombero and Kurupi in the Guaraní

creatures.name: Mbwiri
creatures.excerpt: In Gabon (Fang and related groups), Mbwiri is a possessing spirit that inhabits individuals, manifesting through trance, song, and epileptic-like fits. A shaman builds a hut where the patient and assistants dance to flute and drum for ten days to two weeks; Mbwiri 'abhors good living' and is driven out by the ordeal.

creatures.name: Meandash
creatures.excerpt: Meandash is the mythic wild reindeer of eastern Sami (Kola Peninsula) tradition, a shapeshifter who is human inside his hut and a reindeer outside. He is the central culture hero of the Ter and Kildin Sami, credited with teaching humans the art of hunting and gifting them the bow. Nearly 30 stories about Meandash have

creatures.name: Mechanical Bird Denmark
creatures.excerpt: Mechanical Bird Denmark (Unknown). is a bird. The mechanical bird is from Hans Christian Andersen's The Nightingale, a bejeweled artificial nightingale.. Source: Danish folklore — mechanical figures documented in Danish oral tradition.

creatures.name: Medicine Man
creatures.excerpt: The Medicine Man is a recurring human hero figure in Arapaho mythology. In the story of How Medicine Man Resurrected Buffalo, a powerful medicine man saved his starving people by seeking a vision, receiving instructions from the Earth Spirit, and opening a passage to the underground buffalo world. He demonstrates the p

creatures.name: Medusa
creatures.excerpt: Medusa is the most famous of the three Gorgon sisters of Greek myth, a winged being with living serpents for hair whose gaze turned all who met it to stone. Once a beautiful maiden punished by Athena, she was beheaded by Perseus, and from her neck sprang Pegasus and Chrysaor. Her severed head, the gorgoneion, became an

creatures.name: Meiga
creatures.excerpt: Meigas are the wise women of Galician folklore, healers and practitioners who communicate with nature and the supernatural and who can cure or harm. Unlike the malevolent witch stereotype, they were knowledgeable community figures consulted for healing and divination. The tradition is recorded in Galician oral traditio

creatures.name: Melatha
creatures.excerpt: Melatha is the male lightning spirit of Choctaw tradition, mate of Heloha the thunder bird. Dressed in lightning and rainbows, he races across the sky above the vault of heaven at incredible speed, leaving trails of sparks that flash as lightning, while Heloha's eggs rumble to produce thunder.

creatures.name: Mellyng (Mellified Man)
creatures.excerpt: The mellified man (miren, 'honey person') is a legendary Arabian medicinal preparation recorded by Li Shizhen in the Bencao Gangmu (16th century): a very old man, fed only honey until death, sealed in a honey-filled stone coffin, and after a century sold in pieces as a remedy for broken bones and wounds. It is folk-med

creatures.name: Mellyng (Mellified Man)
creatures.excerpt: The mellified man (mellified mummy) is a legendary remedy from Arabic and Chinese sources, famously recorded by Li Shizhen in the Bencao Gangmu, in which willing elderly men were steeped in honey until their bodies dissolved into a curative confection. Though almost certainly fanciful, the tale circulated along the Sil

creatures.name: Melqart
keywords: melqart, tyrian god, phoenician deity, tyre lebanon, melqart heracles, phoenician colonization
creatures.excerpt: Melqart was the tutelary god of the Phoenician city-state of Tyre (in modern Lebanon) and one of the most important deities in the Phoenician and Punic pantheons. His name means 'King of the City' in Phoenician. Melqart was a complex deity embodying multiple roles: sea god and protector of navigation, a dying-and-risin

creatures.name: Melusine
creatures.excerpt: Melusine is a fresh-water spirit of French folklore, often a woman who becomes a serpent or mermaid below the waist, sometimes winged. In the medieval romance she married Raymondin of Lusignan, provided he never saw her on Saturdays; when he broke the oath she fled as a serpent. She is the legendary ancestress of the L

creatures.name: Mendiss
creatures.excerpt: Mendiss is a female Serer water spirit who guards the Fatick region coast, controlling tides and protecting maritime communities with guardianship powers.

creatures.name: Menehune
creatures.excerpt: The Menehune are the legendary dwarf builders of Hawaiʻi, said to have raised temples (heiau), fishponds, roads, and canoes in a single night, working only in darkness and vanishing at dawn if unfinished. The 1820 census of Kauaʻi listed 65 of them. Scholars debate whether they remember earlier settlers (manahune, 'com

creatures.name: Menninkäinen
creatures.excerpt: Menninkäinen is a Finnish gnome-like forest spirit, small with large head and pointed features, wearing a pointed hat. Originally friendly spirits in isolated places (Ganander), later evolved into goblin-like creatures guarding treasures, enjoying riddles and dominance games (like leprechauns).

creatures.name: Merakyat
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a named spirit of Malaysian folklore; searches locate no being called 'Merakyat.' creatures.name: Merchildren
creatures.excerpt: In Danish folk belief, havbørn are the offspring of havmand and havfrue, dwelling in sea caves and kelp forests. They appear in ballads like "Agneta og Havmanden" where a human woman bears a merman's children, caught between sea and land. Unlike literary mermaids, these beings belong to oral tradition and are feared as

creatures.name: Merger
creatures.excerpt: Merger is the foundational epic hero of the Nanai people of the Amur River region, a powerful warrior-shaman in animal-decorated armor who can transform into tiger, bird, or fish. He combines martial prowess with shamanic magic, undertaking spirit journeys across multiple worlds to protect his people. His kind of hero

creatures.name: Merlin
creatures.excerpt: Merlin (Unknown). is a human. Merlin is the legendary wizard and advisor to King Arthur in British mythology. Possessing prophetic powers and magical abilities, he orchestrates Arthur's birth and guides the kingdom through its gol. Source: Historia Regum Britanniae (Geoffrey of Monmouth, 1136); Arthurian cycle

creatures.name: Mermaid
creatures.excerpt: Mermaid (Generic). is a mermaid. Aquatic beings with the upper body of a human and the tail of a fish, found in various global folklores. Source: Maritime folklore, global oral traditions

creatures.name: Mermaid Denmark
creatures.excerpt: Mermaid Denmark (Unknown). is a mermaid. The mermaid of Danish folklore is a sea creature with the upper body of a woman and the tail of a fish. The most famous Danish mermaid is the subject of Hans Christian Andersen's "The Little Mermaid" . Source: Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tales; Danish folklore

creatures.name: Mermaids of Black Rocks
creatures.excerpt: The Mermaids of Black Rocks are vengeful mermaids said to inhabit the volcanic Black Rocks on the northeastern coast of Saint Kitts. creatures.name: Merman Denmark
creatures.excerpt: Merman Denmark (Unknown). is a mermaid. The merman is a male sea spirit from Danish folklore who lures human women into his underwater realm through enchanted song.. Source: Danish folklore — Merman figure documented in Danish oral tradition.

creatures.name: Metsavana
creatures.excerpt: Metsavana (Estonia). is a deity. The 'Old Man of the Forest' in Estonian mythology, also called metsataat or metsaisa. Source: Estonian folklore; known as the Old Man of the Forest (Metsavana) in Estonian mythology.

creatures.name: Metsänhenki
creatures.excerpt: Metsänhenki (Finnish: 'forest spirit' or 'forest self') is not a distinct creature but the animistic concept of the forest's living essence in Finnish tradition. creatures.name: Midnight Robber (Trinidad Carnival Mas Character)

creatures.name: Migoi (Bhutanese Yeti)
creatures.excerpt: The Migoi (from Tibetan 'mi rgod' meaning 'wild man') is Bhutan's indigenous version of the Yeti, a magical wild creature inhabiting the high Himalayan pastures and deep forests. creatures.name: Mimi
creatures.excerpt: The Mimi (Mimih) are tall, extremely thin spirit beings of Arnhem Land and Kakadu who live in the rock crevices and escarpments and are so delicate that a strong wind can break them. creatures.name: Minotaur
creatures.excerpt: The Minotaur is a monster of Greek myth, a man with the head and body of a bull, born of Pasiphaë and the Cretan bull and known as Asterion. creatures.name: Miraculous Well of Sidi Bou Said
creatures.excerpt: The Miraculous Well of Sidi Bou Said is a legendary blessed water source in the famous blue-and-white Tunisian town of Sidi Bou Said, near Tunis. creatures.name: Mishipizheu
creatures.excerpt: Mishipeshu, the 'Great Lynx' of the Ojibwe and other Great Lakes Anishinaabe peoples, is the foremost underwater being: a horned, scaled panther with palmed paws and a copper tail dwelling in the depths of big lakes. creatures.name: Mitsina (Hermit)
creatures.excerpt: Mítsina is the Hermit of Zuni folklore, who dwelt all alone in the Canyon of the Pines southeast of Zuni. Because he was unwise and evil in his ways, the gods bade him live apart until, through much happening, he should become worthy to dwell among them; hunters passing by heard the sounds of his solitary gaming.

creatures.name: Mmoatia
creatures.excerpt: Mmoatia are small forest-dwelling spirits in Akan mythology, often described as dwarf-like beings with backwards-facing feet. creatures.name: Mngwa
creatures.excerpt: Mngwa (Swahili 'strange one'), also Nunda ('fierce animal'), is a Tanzanian cryptid: massive grey-fawn cat taller than a lion, leaving no tracks. creatures.name: Mnyazi
creatures.excerpt: Mnyazi refers to vampiric returning dead in Kenyan coastal (Swahili/Giriama) belief—jealous/greedy ancestors rising as red-eyed blood-drinkers to prey on kin. creatures.name: Mo'o
creatures.excerpt: Moʻo are powerful reptilian water deities of Hawaiian tradition who guard freshwater pools, streams, waterfalls, and ponds, and can appear as immense lizards, geckos, or beautiful women. creatures.name: Mocko Jumbie
creatures.excerpt: The Mocko Jumbie is a towering stilt-walking spirit dancer and a central figure in St. Kitts and Nevis Carnival and folklore traditions. creatures.name: Modimo
creatures.excerpt: Modimo is the supreme deity of the Sotho-Tswana people, the creator of all things, source of life, and controller of destiny. creatures.name: Mokele-Mbembe

creatures.name: Moko Jumbie
creatures.excerpt: The moko jumbie is a towering, stilt-walking ancestral spirit of the Caribbean, and Saint Vincent preserves the oldest written record of the tradition: William Young's 1791 account of 'Moco Jumbies' among the island's Black Caribs, who performed in costumes blending African motifs with women's petticoats and dresses.

creatures.name: Momoy
creatures.excerpt: Momoy are small, bearded duende-like guardians of water sources, rivers, forests, and agricultural lands in Venezuelan Andean folklore (Mérida, Táchira, Trujillo). creatures.name: Mon-Daw-Min

creatures.name: Mong

creatures.name: Moon God (Guarani)
creatures.excerpt: This entry conflates Kurupi with a moon deity. Kurupi is a Guaraní forest spirit, one of seven monstrous children of Tau and Kerana, known for his elongated prehensile phallus, backwards feet, and role as abductor/impregnator of women. He is a fertility figure and forest guardian, not a moon god.

creatures.name: Moon God (Guarani)
creatures.excerpt: The record conflates two distinct Guarani figures. creatures.name: Moon Maiden (Cherokee)

creatures.name: Moon Woman

creatures.name: Moose Guardian (Mapuche)

creatures.name: Moose Guardian of Apache
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a guardian of Apache folklore. No source records a moose guardian spirit among the Apache. Mapuche underground spirits are the Ngen-mapu (earth owners) and Anchimayen (little people), not moose guardians.

creatures.name: Moose Guardian of Muisca

creatures.name: Moose Nature-Spirit (Mixtec)

creatures.name: Moose Nature-Spirit of Cheyenne

creatures.name: Moose Nature-Spirit of Kwakiutl

creatures.name: Moose Nature-Spirit of Shoshone

creatures.name: Moose Spirit (Zapotec)

creatures.name: Moose Spirit of Aymara

creatures.name: Moose Spirit of Yoruba

creatures.name: Moose Trickster (Cree)

creatures.name: Moose Trickster (Cree)

creatures.name: Moose Trickster of Blackfoot
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a trickster of Blackfoot (Siksika) folklore. creatures.name: Moose Trickster of Kikuyu

creatures.name: Moose Trickster of Shona

creatures.name: Moose Trickster of Tlingit
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a trickster of Tlingit folklore. creatures.name: Moose Water-Spirit of Paiute

creatures.name: Mora
creatures.excerpt: Mora is a Serbian nocturnal spirit, often female, believed to press on the chest of sleeping people and cause nightmares and sleep paralysis. creatures.name: Morana
creatures.excerpt: Morana (Marzanna, Morena) is the Slavic goddess of winter, death, and the harvest's end, honored in spring rituals across Czech, Polish, and Slovak lands. creatures.name: Moskkjerringa

creatures.name: Moso

creatures.name: Mouse Spirit

creatures.name: Mousso Koroni

creatures.name: Moán
creatures.excerpt: Moán is a Colombian forest spirit of the Pacific/Chocó and Amazon regions who protects wildlife and punishes hunters who break taboos. creatures.name: Mujna

creatures.name: Muki
creatures.excerpt: Muki (Muqui) is an Andean mining goblin of Quechua/Aymara tradition in Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, and Colombia. Known regionally as chinchiliku, anchanchu, or jusshi.

creatures.name: Muladi

creatures.name: Mumbi

creatures.name: Mutiara (The Magic Rooster)

creatures.name: Myling

creatures.name: Mzé Moya

creatures.name: Mátsailéma (Evening Star, War God)
creatures.excerpt: Mátsailéma is the Zuni god of war and the Evening Star, the younger twin of Áhaiyúta; together the brothers are the Áhayuta, the Twin War Gods of Zuni tradition. creatures.name: Naato'si

creatures.name: Nacken

creatures.name: Nafanua

creatures.name: Naga
creatures.excerpt: Nagas are divine half-human, half-serpent beings in Hindu and Buddhist tradition, children of sage Kashyapa and Kadru. creatures.name: Naga (Burmese)

creatures.name: Nagual (Nahual)

creatures.name: Nahurac

creatures.name: Nai Tiki
