creatures.name: Ngalyod
creatures.excerpt: Ngalyod is the Rainbow Serpent creator being in the mythology of the Kunwinjku people of western Arnhem Land, Northern Territory. As a powerful ancestral being, Ngalyod created the landscape, waterholes, and living things during the Dreamtime. Unlike the purely serpentine Rainbow Serpent figures, Ngalyod is a composite

creatures.name: Ngirngemelas
creatures.excerpt: Ngirngemelas is the trickster spirit of Palauan mythology, a shapeshifting figure who uses camouflage and illusion to test and outwit humans. One Palauan account links him to Ngibtal, the boy turned giant clam whose tears made the tides. His mischievous, elusive nature reminds listeners of the unpredictability of the n

creatures.name: Ngua
creatures.excerpt: Vietnamese tradition mythologizes horses, but not as cosmic steeds pulling sun and moon: the iron horse of Thánh Gióng, the white horse as a sun symbol at Phù Đồng temple, and the White Horse God (Bạch Mã), said to guide Lý Thái Tổ to build Thăng Long citadel. The recorded horses 'whose hooves make thunder' are not ind

creatures.name: Ngueak (Lao Nāga Serpent)
creatures.excerpt: Ngueak is the Lao name for the nāga, the great serpent-deity of the Mekong and guardian spirit of the Lao people. Legend says the river's course was carved by the body of a Ngueak king. Village tales tell of nāga princes wedding mortal women, of protectors of boatmen and hoarders of river treasure; the Rocket Festival

creatures.name: Nguzunguzu
creatures.excerpt: Nguzunguzu is a carved canoe prow figurehead from the Western Solomon Islands that represents a powerful protective spirit. According to Roviana mythology, the figurehead is the transformed head of Tiola, a chief from Nduke (Kolombangara Island) who turned into a dog and whose carved image was placed at the front of wa

creatures.name: Nian
creatures.excerpt: Nian is the lion-like monster of Chinese folklore said to emerge each Lunar New Year's Eve to attack villages, its wide mouth and sharp teeth terrifying the countryside. Fearless of predators, it is driven away by the color red, firecrackers, and loud noises — the origin of red decorations and fireworks in Chinese New

creatures.name: Nica (or Nika)
creatures.excerpt: Nica (or Nika) is a Bulgarian water nymph, cognate with Russian rusalka and South Slavic samodiva/vila. Inhabits rivers and lakes as a beautiful young woman with long hair. Can be helpful to fishermen but dangerous if scorned, drowning swimmers. Part of the broader Slavic 'water maiden' complex. The name may derive fro

creatures.name: Nidaros-Munken
creatures.excerpt: Nidaros-Munken (the Monk of Nidaros) is a famous ghost that haunts Nidaros Cathedral in Trondheim. The specter is said to be a Catholic monk from the cathedral's pre-Reformation days who was killed during the Reformation turmoil of 1537. The ghost appears as a tall, hooded figure in a black or brown monk's habit, often

creatures.name: Nidelv-Nøkken
creatures.excerpt: Nidelv-Nøkken (the Nidelva Nixie) is a localized version of the nøkk (water spirit) that specifically inhabits the Nidelva river in Trondheim. The Nidelva flows through the heart of Trondheim, from Selbusjøen to the Trondheimsfjord, passing under several bridges and through the city center. According to Trondheim folkl

creatures.name: Nifoloa
creatures.excerpt: Nifoloa is a dreaded spirit deity of Samoan tradition, feared especially in the Falelima district of Savai'i, who is said to inflict fatal pricks on intruders and the unwary. The name is bound up with sharp, stinging harm, and the figure is counted among the malevolent forces of Samoan spirit belief. Villagers treat Ni

creatures.name: Night Marchers (Huakai po)
creatures.excerpt: The Night Marchers (huaka'i pō) are the ghostly processions of ancient Hawaiian warriors and chiefs who walk old trails and sacred sites, especially on moon phases tied to the gods Kū, Lono, Kāne, and Kanaloa. Marching with torches, drums, and conch blasts, they demand witnesses lie face down and avoid eye contact lest

creatures.name: Night Stalker (Cheyenne)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Cheyenne tradition; no recorded Cheyenne narrative describes a 'Night Stalker.' The closest attested beings of the night are the Nightspirits, 'Those Who Walk in Darkness,' of the Ho-Chunk, who spread darkness as they walk and grant war blessings to vision seekers. The entry appears to con

creatures.name: Nightingale Denmark
creatures.excerpt: Nightingale Denmark (Unknown). is a animal-spirit. This entry appears to reference the nightingale from Hans Christian Andersen's story "The Nightingale," which is set in China. The tale contrasts the beauty of nature with artificial imitation.. Source: Andersen's "The Nightingale" (1843)

creatures.name: Nihancan
creatures.excerpt: Nihancan (Nih'oo3oo) is the spider trickster figure of the Arapaho tribe. Like Iktomi of the Lakota and Wihio of the Cheyenne, Nihancan is both clever and foolish, wise and ridiculous. His stories range from benign mischief to more violent trickery—in one tale he tricks a bear family and kills the children, in another

creatures.name: Nikommo
creatures.excerpt: Nikommo belongs to the little people of Wampanoag tradition rather than to the giants. The attested Wampanoag giants are Maushop and his sons, whose struggles with the dangerous little people of the dawnland are told along the Massachusetts coast. Nikommo is better understood as one of those small, capricious forest be

creatures.name: Nile Water Spirits (Nilotic Folk Belief)
creatures.excerpt: Egyptian folk belief holds that spirits and jinn inhabit the Nile and its canals. The best-attested is El Naddaha ('the Caller'), a female, naiad-like spirit who appears near the river at night and calls men by name, hypnotizing and luring them to the water; the tradition was popular in 20th-century rural Egypt. Charms

creatures.name: Nimba
creatures.excerpt: Nimba (D'mba) is the Baga (Guinea) great mother headdress spirit, a monumental carved wooden bust worn in harvest dances. She embodies fertility, abundance, and the ideal woman — not a forest guardian. Appears as an elderly woman testing visitors' respect in some narratives. Documented in Baga art and ritual (Smithsoni

creatures.name: Nina
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Sudanese folklore by this name. Nina is described as a Nubian fertility spirit who appears as a beautiful woman or as water itself, protecting mothers and children and honoured in naming ceremonies. The closest documented beings are the Nubian water angels, malayket al-bahr, and the banat

creatures.name: Ninki Nanka
creatures.excerpt: Ninki Nanka is the Mandinka (Gambia/Senegal) dragon-like water spirit: a 30-foot reptilian creature with crocodile head, donkey/hippopotamus-giraffe body, mirror scales, and fatal Medusa-like stare. Inhabits swamps and caves; explains river disappearances. Carries a head gem of power. Documented in Mandinka oral tradit

creatures.name: Nis Puk
creatures.excerpt: Nis Puk (also called Puge) is a household spirit from Sønderjylland and the Danish-German border region, a variant of the Nisse but with distinct traits. Nis Puk is short and broad, wears red trousers and a red pointed cap, and lives in the barn or stable of a farm. His special talent is stealing grain and fodder from

creatures.name: Nisse
creatures.excerpt: Nisse (Swedish tomte, tomtenisse, tomtegubbe) is the Swedish household spirit: small, grey-clad, red-capped, dwelling under farmstead floorboards. Protects livestock, harvests, carpentry; expects Christmas porridge with butter. If neglected, turns vengeful: kills livestock, breaks tools, leaves farm. Shapeshifts (goat,

creatures.name: Nisse
creatures.excerpt: Nisse is the Danish household spirit (husnisse, god dreng, gårdbuk): small, bearded, grey-clad, red-capped, living in barns, lofts, stables. Begins in church but coaxed to farm. Protects animals and property; demands Christmas porridge — especially sweet buckwheat boghvedegrød with butter. Fastidious: missing butter ca

creatures.name: Nisse
creatures.excerpt: Nisse (Norwegian tufte, tuftekall, gardvord, fjøsnisse) is the Norwegian farm spirit: small, grey, red-capped, dwelling in barns and stables, especially in Østlandet and Trøndelag. Protects livestock; vengeful if Christmas porridge (rømmegrøt, later risengrynsgrøt) withheld. Shapeshifts. Distinct from Swedish tomte. Ch

creatures.name: Nisse
creatures.excerpt: Duplicate of nisse-denmark (slug #29). The Danish household spirit (nisse, husnisse, tomte): small, bearded, grey-clad, red-capped, dwelling in barns and lofts. Protects farm animals and property for Christmas porridge (especially buckwheat boghvedegrød with butter). Fastidious: missing butter triggers vengeful cow-kil

creatures.name: Nisse
creatures.excerpt: Nisse (Icelandic). is a wight. A small household spirit that protects the farm in exchange for porridge. Source: Scandinavian folklore; nisse/tomte are household spirits documented in Nordic folk belief collections.

creatures.name: Nisse
creatures.excerpt: The Nisse (Tomte, Tomtenisse, Tonttu) is a Nordic household spirit: small, human-like, gray-clad with a red pointed cap, dwelling in farmstead barns, stables, or under floorboards. Performs chores (threshing, animal care, carpentry) in exchange for a bowl of porridge (rømmegrøt or rice pudding) with butter on Christmas

creatures.name: Nix
creatures.excerpt: The Nix is a shape-shifting water spirit that inhabits the rivers and lakes of Switzerland. Similar to the Celtic kelpie, the Swiss Nix can assume multiple forms—most commonly a beautiful woman who lures men to watery deaths, but also a horse, fish, or even a log. According to Swiss folklore collected in central Switze

creatures.name: Nix
creatures.excerpt: Nix is a water-spirit from Switzerland mythology. Similar to the Celtic kelpie, the Swiss Nix can assume multiple forms—most commonly a beautiful woman who lures men to watery deaths, but also a horse, fish, or even a log. According to Swiss folklore collected in central Switzerland, the Nix has complete control over w

creatures.name: Nix
creatures.excerpt: Nix is a water-spirit from Germanic/Nordic mythology. Similar to the Celtic kelpie, the Swiss Nix can assume multiple forms—most commonly a beautiful woman who lures men to watery deaths, but also a horse, fish, or even a log. According to Swiss folklore collected in central Switzerland, the Nix has complete control ov

creatures.name: Nixe
creatures.excerpt: The Nixe is the female counterpart to the Nix, a freshwater mermaid of German rivers (Rhine, Danube). Beautiful woman with fish tail, wet hem distinguishes her. Her song lures men to drowning. Nibelungenlied mentions Rhine maidens guarding the Rhinegold. Wagner's Ring adapts them as Woglinde, Wellgunde, Flosshilde. She

creatures.name: Nişançı
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Turkish folklore under this name. Nisanci is described as a giant, fifteen to twenty feet tall with a long beard, who works at night shaping the hills and rock fields of Anatolia and hurls boulders at mockers. The tale echoes genuine Anatolian giant lore and the Ottoman court office of nis

creatures.name: Nk (or Nkanyin)
creatures.excerpt: Nkornkanyin (Nk or Nkanyin) is a Congolese forest guardian spirit (DRC). A tall humanoid with long hair, leaf clothing, and glowing eyes, it can appear as a gorilla or leopard. It enforces forest protocol, cursing overhunters and resource-wasters with disease. Healing and nature manipulation are its powers. It reinforc

creatures.name: Nk (or Nkanyin)
creatures.excerpt: Nkornkanyin (Nk or Nkanyin) is a Congolese forest guardian spirit (Republic of Congo). Identical to the DRC entry — a tall, leaf-clad humanoid with glowing eyes that shapeshifts into gorilla or leopard, curses taboo-breakers, and heals. It watches forest protocol and punishes overhunting. The duplicate slugs reflect th

creatures.name: Nkadi
creatures.excerpt: Nkadi (also known as Mbumba) is the great rainbow serpent of Kongo mythology, a primordial being dwelling at the boundary between the world of the living and the dead. In Kongo cosmology, Nkadi is a cosmic serpent encircling the universe, its body forming the rainbow bridging the waters above and below. Nkadi is associ

creatures.name: Nne Miri
creatures.excerpt: Nne Miri (literally "Mother of Waters") is the Igbo spirit of rivers, streams, and bodies of water. She is the patroness of fishermen and the guardian of marine life. Closely related to the pan-African Mami Wata figure, Nne Miri is a beautiful but dangerous water spirit who can grant wealth and fertility to those she f

creatures.name: Noaidegažži
creatures.excerpt: Noaidegažži (also saivogažži) are the helper spirits of the Sami noaidi (shaman), sent to perform tasks, gather information, and fight other noaidi's spirits. These spirits can take the form of birds (saivoloddi), fish (saivoguolli), or reindeer bulls (saivosarvvát — the strongest form). The noaidegažži assist with hea

creatures.name: Noion
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a figure of Tibetan folklore. No source documents a household spirit named 'Noion' tied to Manjushri, the bodhisattva of wisdom, who answers questions in dreams. The recorded traits resemble generic depictions of Manjushri, a well-attested figure, but the name and role appear in no Tibetan

creatures.name: Nokomis
creatures.excerpt: Nokomis is the wise grandmother of Nanabozho in Ojibwe and Anishinaabe mythology. She raised Nanabozho after his mother died during childbirth. Nokomis is a figure of great wisdom and spiritual knowledge, often providing guidance and counsel to Nanabozho during his adventures. She is associated with the earth, the moon

creatures.name: Nokomis
creatures.excerpt: Nokomis, 'my grandmother' in Anishinaabemowin, is the wise grandmother of Nanabush in Ojibwe tradition, the elder who raises the culture hero and counsels him through his adventures. Her name and role appear across the Anishinaabe nations of the Great Lakes, and she is a figure of kindness, humor, and steady guidance.

creatures.name: Nokomis
creatures.excerpt: Nokomis is the grandmother of Nanabush (Nanabozho) in Ojibwe tradition, her very name meaning 'my grandmother' in Anishinaabemowin. She raises the trickster culture hero after the death of his mother and guides him through his adventures. Cognate grandmother figures include Nukumi of the Mi'kmaq and Grandmother Woodchu

creatures.name: Nommo
creatures.excerpt: Nommo (Nummo) are Dogon primordial amphibious ancestral spirits, created by Amma as first living beings. Hermaphroditic, fish-tailed humanoids who descended from Sirius in an ark of fire and thunder, created water reservoirs, and sacrificed their bodies to populate the universe with Binu shrines. Masters of Water, Teac

creatures.name: Nonoma
creatures.excerpt: Nonoma is the Cheyenne spirit of thunder, a powerful being who controls storms and brings rain to the plains. When Nonoma flaps his wings, thunder rolls across the sky. He is both feared and respected—his storms can bring life-giving rain for crops and buffalo or destructive hail and lightning. The Cheyenne perform cer

creatures.name: Noqoilpi (Great Gambler)
creatures.excerpt: Noqoilpi is a powerful and malevolent figure in Navajo tradition who challenged all who came to him to gambling contests. He lived at the base of Ch'óol'į́'í (Great Spruce Mountain or El Capitan) and won the possessions, freedom, and even entire nations through his gambling prowess. He grew so powerful that the Holy Pe

creatures.name: Norns Iceland
creatures.excerpt: Norns Iceland (Unknown). is a spirit. The Norns are three female beings in Norse mythology who shape or decree the fate of gods and mortals. Their names are Urðr (past), Verðandi (present), and Skuld (future), and they dwell at the base o. Source: Poetic Edda; Prose Edda (Snorri Sturluson, 13th century)

creatures.name: Northern Lights
creatures.excerpt: The northern lights, called wâwâhtêwak, 'those that go in circles,' in Cree, are seen as spirits dancing across the winter sky. creatures.name: Nsenga
creatures.excerpt: Nsenga is a Congolese shapeshifter guardian taking forms of lion, leopard, python, or human with animal features — its eyes always remain wise and ancient. It protects sacred locations, tests human intentions, and can be helpful or dangerous depending on treatment. Representing ancestral spirits and nature guardians in

creatures.name: Ntikuma
creatures.excerpt: Ntikuma is the son of Anansi the spider in Akan folklore. Unlike his cunning father, Ntikuma often demonstrates wisdom that surpasses Anansi's schemes. In the famous story "Anansi and the Pot of Wisdom," when Anansi tried to hide all the world's wisdom in a pot at the top of a tree, it was young Ntikuma who pointed out

creatures.name: Ntsomi
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a West African creature. Ntsomi is Xhosa (South Africa) women's solo performance art combining storytelling, dance, and song with props — not a monster or forest spirit. Documented by Harold Scheub ('The Xhosa Ntsomi'). The record misattributes a South African performance tradition to West

creatures.name: Ntxwj Nyog (Spirit of Death and Sickness)
creatures.excerpt: Ntxwj Nyog (also Ndu Nyong or Ntxwj Nyug) is the primordial spirit of sickness, death, and evil in Hmong shamanic mythology. creatures.name: Nu-u
creatures.excerpt: The name nu-u has no independent attestation, but it corresponds most closely to the water babies of Great Basin tradition, known to the Southern Paiute as pit-u-u or paúngaa'a. These small, crying beings guard springs and lakes and aid shamans, but are dangerous to those who approach their waters. Their weeping is a w

creatures.name: Nuckelavee
creatures.excerpt: The Nuckelavee (also Nuckalavee, Knucker) is the most terrifying creature in Orkney folklore — a skinless horse-like centaur from the sea whose breath withers crops and spreads disease. creatures.name: Nugu
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in documented Solomon Islands folklore or academic sources. No dedicated source confirms a dwarf or forest people called Nugu who lead travelers astray or mine and craft in the forests. creatures.name: Nuku
creatures.excerpt: In Samoan spirit belief, Nuku is a ghost (aitu) said to return from death to unfinished business, appearing as a translucent or shadowy figure, sometimes in the form of familiar animals. Encounters bring misfortune, illness, or accidents, and the spirit may be appeased through proper rituals and offerings. Belief in ai

creatures.name: Num
creatures.excerpt: Num is the supreme sky god of the Nenets people of Siberia, the good creator of the earth and all living things and the high god of the Nenets pantheon. In Nenets dualistic cosmology he is one of two demiurges whose malevolent son Nga rules the dead below; in one myth a shaman went to Nga's realm, wed his daughter, and

creatures.name: Nunnehi
creatures.excerpt: The Nunnehi, meaning 'the travelers' or 'those who live anywhere,' are a race of immortal spirit people of the Cherokee, distinct from ghosts and from gods. They dwell in the mountains, forests, and stone houses of Cherokee country, are usually friendly, and sometimes showed themselves to warn of danger. During the Rem

creatures.name: Nurarihyon
creatures.excerpt: Nurarihyon, the 'Supreme Commander of the Yōkai,' is an elderly aristocratic yōkai of Japanese folklore with a gourd-shaped head and flowing robes. creatures.name: Nuribotoke
creatures.excerpt: Nuribotoke is a Japanese yōkai appearing as a living Buddhist monk statue with blackened teeth, a long lolling tongue, and an angry face. It manifests to those who misuse temples or neglect worship, cursing the disrespectful or teaching them to show proper reverence for sacred places. The figure embodies a warning agai

creatures.name: Nurikabe
creatures.excerpt: Nurikabe is the 'wall-spirit' of Japanese folklore, an invisible barrier that blocks travelers on roads and paths at night, sometimes showing an old man's face in the wall. It may be dispelled by knocking three times or reciting a charm, and is occasionally benevolent, shielding walkers from danger. The yōkai explains

creatures.name: Nut (Sky Goddess of Egypt)
creatures.excerpt: Nut is the Egyptian goddess of the sky and the heavens. She arches over the earth as the starry sky, her body covered with stars. Daughter of Shu (air) and Tefnut (moisture), sister and wife of Geb (earth). Each day she swallows the sun god Ra, who travels through her body at night and is reborn from her womb at dawn.

creatures.name: Nya-nya Bulembu
creatures.excerpt: Nya-nya Bulembu is a Swazi (Eswatini) monster haunting deep pools, described as a massive moss-green beast with fur like living seaweed. It preys on the careless, transforms victims into monsters, and punishes ritual violations. The name suggests a pool-dwelling entity in siSwati. Limited documentation outside local Sw

creatures.name: Nyabingi
creatures.excerpt: Nyabingi (Rwanda). is a deity. Unmarried woman made immortal by Imana after murder. Source: Rwandan folklore — Nyabingi spirit documented in Rwandan oral tradition.

creatures.name: Nyai Roro Kidul
creatures.excerpt: Nyai Roro Kidul is the goddess-queen of the Southern Ocean in Javanese and Sundanese belief, appearing as a beautiful woman in royal green robes with a spirit retinue. She rules the waters and is said to draw those who wear green into her undersea kingdom as soldiers. Revered across Java, she is the subject of widespre

creatures.name: Nyame
creatures.excerpt: Nyame (Onyame) is the supreme god of the Akan people (Ashanti, Fante, Akuapem) of Ghana. Also known as Nyankopon or Odomankoma, Nyame is the omniscient, omnipotent sky deity who created the universe and all living things. The name means "the one who knows and sees everything." Nyame is part of a trinity with Nyankopon

creatures.name: Nyamgondho (Lady of the Lake)
creatures.excerpt: Nyamgondho Wuod Ombare is a legendary lake spirit from Luo mythology who married a poor fisherman on Lake Victoria. The fisherman (whose real name was Julu son of Ombare) pulled a hideously ugly woman from his net. She promised to make him wealthy if he would take her as his wife and never reveal where she came from. T

creatures.name: Nyaminyami (Zambezi River God)
creatures.excerpt: Nyaminyami is the most famous river deity in Zambian mythology, the serpent-like god of the mighty Zambezi River. According to Tonga legend, Nyaminyami has the body of a snake and the head of a fish, symbolizing his dominion over both water and land. He is believed to control the flow of the Zambezi River and has the p

creatures.name: Nyang'idi (Lake Serpent)
creatures.excerpt: The Nyang'idi is a fearsome serpent monster in Luo mythology said to dwell in the depths of Lake Victoria, a bringer of disease and misfortune. According to tradition, the Nyang'idi was once a servant of Were (the supreme god) who was cast down into the waters as punishment for disobedience. The serpent grows to enormo

creatures.name: Nyenchen Thanglha
creatures.excerpt: Nyenchen Thanglha is the great mountain god of Tibet, lord of the Nyenchen Thanglha range and chief of the nyen spirits. creatures.name: Nyerum
creatures.excerpt: Nyerum are Bambara (Mali) water spirits inhabiting seasonal floodplains and ponds. They breathe water, immune to drought, and lure/drown intruders. Part of Bambara animistic tradition alongside Faro (river spirit) and pond genies. Documented in Bambara oral tradition and ethnographic surveys of Niger River communities.

creatures.name: Nyi Roro Kidul
creatures.excerpt: Nyi Roro Kidul is the legendary queen of the Southern Ocean of Javanese and Sundanese tradition: a beautiful, powerful spirit with long black hair, ruling the waves of the Indian Ocean south of Java. Tied to the fall of the Sunda Kingdom and later to Mataram, she appears in dreams and controls sea creatures, and is app

creatures.name: Nyikang
creatures.excerpt: Nyikang, son of Kang, is the semi-legendary founder and divine ancestor of the Shilluk people. Said to be born of a human father and a crocodile naiad, he crossed the White Nile into Shilluk country, established the kingship, and later vanished into the river. Shilluk kings are believed to inherit his spirit, tying eve

creatures.name: Nykur
creatures.excerpt: Nykur is the Icelandic water horse, a shape-shifting water spirit that lures people onto its back and drowns them. Unlike the Norwegian nøkk who uses music, the nykur appears as a beautiful dapple-grey horse with backward-facing hooves and fetlocks that trail water. It stands quietly by rivers, lakes, or the sea, invit

creatures.name: Nykur Iceland
creatures.excerpt: Nykur Iceland (Unknown). is a kelpie. Nykur is a water horse from Icelandic folklore who lures people onto its back then drowns them.. Source: Icelandic folklore — the Nykur water-horse/kelpie documented in Icelandic folklore.

creatures.name: Nykurin
creatures.excerpt: Nykurin is the Faroese nix, a dangerous freshwater shapeshifter. Appears as beautiful horse (nykur) on land; touching its tail sticks the victim as it drags them to watery death. Also appears as handsome youth luring women. Calling its true name 'nykur' breaks its power. Can become any quadruped except ram/lamb (cannot

creatures.name: Nyoaty
creatures.excerpt: Nyoaty (Tanzania). is a bird. Maasai eagle spirit that carries messages between humans and the divine. Source: Maasai folklore — Nyoaty eagle spirit documented in Tanzanian Maasai oral tradition.

creatures.name: Nyonyose Mask Spirit
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Mossi (Nyonyose) tradition. The figure appears to be a modern composite or fabrication rather than an authentic element of Mossi (Nyonyose) folklore.

creatures.name: Nyurgun Bootur
creatures.excerpt: Nyurgun Bootur, 'the Swift,' is the foremost hero of the Sakha (Yakut) epic cycle, the olonkho. A champion of the Middle World, he battles the hostile abaahy demons to defend his people and restore balance to the cosmos, aided by his swift steed and weapons forged by heavenly smiths. His songs were set down in written

creatures.name: Nzambi Mpungu
creatures.excerpt: Nzambi Mpungu (meaning 'Creator of All') is the supreme god of the Kongo people, the eternal Sky Father and creator of the universe. In Kongo cosmology, the world began as an empty void called mbungi (an empty circle of nothingness). Nzambi Mpungu, with his female counterpart Nzambici, created a spark of fire called ka

creatures.name: Nzazi
creatures.excerpt: Nzazi is the powerful spirit of thunder and lightning in Kongo mythology, a fearsome being who patrols the skies during storms hurling bolts of fire at those who break sacred laws. According to tradition, Nzazi was once a man who climbed too high in his ambitions and was transformed into a sky spirit. He patrols the he

creatures.name: Näcken
creatures.excerpt: Näcken (Strömkarlen, 'The Stream Man') is the Swedish male water spirit: slender, often naked/elegantly clad, green-haired (foliage), sitting on rocks playing violin, horn, flute in brooks and waterfalls. Music lures women and children to drown; most dangerous Midsummer, Christmas Eve, Thursdays.

creatures.name: Näkk
creatures.excerpt: Näkk (Estonia). is a water-spirit. Estonian variant of Nordic nixie, a shapeshifting water spirit with subtypes. Source: Estonian folklore; variant of the nixie (näkki) found in Estonian water-spirit lore.

creatures.name: Näkki
creatures.excerpt: Näkki is the Finnish malevolent water spirit, loaned from Swedish näck. Appears as beautiful woman combing golden hair on rocks, or as old green-skinned monster. creatures.name: Níðhöggr
creatures.excerpt: Níðhöggr ('Malice-Striker') is the monstrous dragon in Norse mythology gnawing Yggdrasil's roots in Niflheim. Wingless, serpentine, dark-scaled, red-eyed, powerful jaws. creatures.name: Nøkk
creatures.excerpt: Nøkk (also known as Nøkken, Näcken, Nykkjen) is a male freshwater spirit in Norwegian and Scandinavian folklore who dwells in dark lakes, rivers, and ponds. creatures.name: Nøstekatt
creatures.excerpt: The troll cat (Norwegian: trollkatt, also nøstekatt) is a witch's familiar in Scandinavian folklore, a supernatural cat sent by a witch to steal milk from neighbours' cows. creatures.name: Núi
creatures.excerpt: Núi is the Vietnamese word for mountain; the country's mountain-spirit tradition centers on documented figures like Sơn Tinh, the Mountain Lord, one of Vietnam's Four Immortals, who battled Thủy Tinh, the Water Lord, for Princess Mỵ Nương. creatures.name: Nûñnë'hï
creatures.excerpt: Nûñnë'hï is James Mooney's spelling of Nunnehi, the Cherokee word for a race of immortal spirit people, 'those who live anywhere,' who dwell in the mountains and forests of the old Cherokee country. creatures.name: Nāc
creatures.excerpt: Nāc is the Lao term for naga, the great river serpent of Lao Buddhist folklore: a huge, usually cobra-hooded serpent, sometimes multi-headed, scales shining, dwelling in the Mekong beneath water palaces. creatures.name: Nāga
creatures.excerpt: Nāga is the diacritically-marked Sanskrit form of naga (slug: naga), not a distinct entity. Identical to the naga entry: divine half-human, half-serpent beings, children of Kashyapa and Kadru, dwelling in Patala, guarding waters and treasures, rivals of Garuda.

creatures.name: Obambo
creatures.excerpt: Obambo (Obambou) is a supernatural being of the Baka and other Central African tribes. It possesses the sick, residing in their bowels until driven out by communal noise-making — singing, dancing, yelling, banging objects. The M'pongwe believed some are born with Obambo, causing innate insanity.

creatures.name: Obariyon

creatures.name: Obatala
creatures.excerpt: Obatala is the king of white cloth, the oldest of all orishas, and the sculptor of humanity. Sent by Olodumare to create the earth, Obatala descended from heaven on a golden chain carrying a snail shell of sand, a white hen, a black cat, and a palm nut. creatures.name: Obayifo
creatures.excerpt: Obayifo is an Ashanti (Akan, Ghana) vampire-witch who appears human by day but at night emits phosphorescent light from armpits and anus, flies as a ball of light, and sucks blood/vitality. creatures.name: Obrigwabibikwa
creatures.excerpt: Obrigwabibikwa is a mystical dwarf and shapeshifter from the mythology of the Mbuti Pygmy people of the Democratic Republic of Congo. creatures.name: Ocean Spider
creatures.excerpt: The Ocean-Spider is a monstrous water creature of Greenlandic Inuit tradition recorded by Hinrich Rink. creatures.name: Octopus Nuu Chah Nulth
creatures.excerpt: In Nuu-chah-nulth (Nootka) legend, the octopus appears in the tale 'Raven Annoys Octopus,' where Raven pesters the octopus people and learns a lesson in respect. An octopus woman with eight long braids digs on the shore with a stick, and the story teaches listeners about meddling and the boundaries of other beings.

creatures.name: Octopus Water-Spirit (Wolof)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a distinct named entity in Wolof tradition. Wolof water spirits (jinés/jinn) inhabit rivers and coasts but no specific 'octopus water-spirit' appears in ethnographic records (Diop, Faye). The octopus motif may reflect Atlantic marine influence but lacks attestation.

creatures.name: Octopus Water-Spirit (Wolof)
creatures.excerpt: The Octopus Water-Spirit is a Wolof (Senegalese) water spirit, not Cameroonian — the Wolof are a Senegalese ethnic group with some presence in Cameroon. creatures.name: Od Iedeh (Fire Spirit)
creatures.excerpt: Od Iedeh is the Evenki (Siberian Tungusic) fire spirit, mistress of the hearth. Appears as a face in the flames or an old woman made of fire, sometimes riding a fox. Must be respected with offerings; protects the household, aids cooking and warmth, but burns the dwelling if insulted. Communicates through crackling flam

creatures.name: Odin
creatures.excerpt: Odin (Odinn), the Allfather, is the highest god of Norse mythology — lord of wisdom, poetry, war, and the dead. He gave one eye to Mimir's well for wisdom and hanged nine nights on Yggdrasil to win the runes. He rides the eight-legged Sleipnir with his ravens Huginn and Muninn, and receives half the battle-slain into V

creatures.name: Odin
creatures.excerpt: Odin (Odinn) is the chief of the Norse Aesir — god of wisdom, poetry, war, and death. Icelandic sources, chiefly the Poetic and Prose Eddas, preserve the fullest accounts of his myths, including his sacrifice of an eye for wisdom and his winning of the runes. creatures.name: Oduduwa
creatures.excerpt: Oduduwa is the legendary progenitor of the Yoruba people, first Oba (king) of Ile-Ife, and an orisha of creation. creatures.name: Ogbanje
creatures.excerpt: Ogbanje (Ọgbanje) are Igbo 'spirit children' who cyclically die and are reborn into the same family, causing recurrent grief. creatures.name: Ogo (The Cosmic Fox)
creatures.excerpt: Ogo (Yurugu), the Pale Fox, is the Dogon trickster. Firstborn of Amma, he rebelled, stole a piece of the sun, and brought death, imperfection, and speech to humanity. creatures.name: Ogopogo
creatures.excerpt: Ogopogo is the lake monster of Okanagan Lake in British Columbia, rooted in Syilx (Okanagan) oral tradition, where the being is called n̓x̌aʔx̌ʔitkʷ, the sacred water creature said to demand safe passage of travellers. creatures.name: Ogou (Lwa of War and Iron)
creatures.excerpt: Ogou is the fierce lwa of war, iron, fire, politics, and justice in Haitian Vodou. He is second only to Papa Legba in importance and is the patron of soldiers, blacksmiths, mechanics, drivers, and all who work with metal. creatures.name: Ogress Iceland

creatures.name: Ogun

creatures.name: Ojalehto (Stream Leaf)
creatures.excerpt: Ojalehto ('Stream Leaf') is a small Finnish water spirit of brooks and streams, childlike, greenish-brown with fish scales or gills. creatures.name: Okwa Naholo

creatures.name: Ol' Hige (Jamaican Vampire Hag)
creatures.excerpt: The ol' hige is the Jamaican vampire-hag: an elderly woman bound by a diabolical pact who, by night, sheds her skin, hides it in a mortar or under a tree, and flies as a ball of fire to suck the blood of sleeping victims, often infants.

creatures.name: Olapa (Rainbow Serpent)
creatures.excerpt: Olapa is the moon goddess of Maasai cosmology, regarded as the wife of Enkai, the sky god and creator. creatures.excerpt: Old Man Coyote (Isáahkawuattee, Akbaatatdia) is the central creator and trickster figure of Crow mythology. creatures.name: Old Master
creatures.excerpt: Old Master is a recurring character in African American folklore, particularly in the 'trickster slave' narrative cycle. creatures.name: Old Woman's Water
creatures.excerpt: Old Woman's Water is a powerful water spirit in Cheyenne mythology, associated with a sacred healing spring. creatures.name: Ole Higue
creatures.excerpt: Ole Higue (Ol' Higue) is a Guyanese/Caribbean vampire-witch from West African soucouyant traditions. creatures.name: Ole Lukøje (Sandman)
creatures.excerpt: Ole Lukøje ('Ole Close-Eye') is the Danish Sandman, a small elderly man in long coat with magic sand bag. creatures.name: Olifat
creatures.excerpt: Olifat is a trickster god in Micronesian mythology, particularly among the islands of Chuuk. creatures.name: Olobit
creatures.excerpt: The olobit, also called the 'sharp-breasted snake,' is a monstrous serpent of the Natchez, a people of the lower Mississippi. Described in John R. Swanton's field research, it is a supernatural reptile closely related to the Uktena of the Cherokee and other great serpents of the Southeast.

creatures.name: Olodumare
creatures.excerpt: Olodumare is the Supreme Being and ultimate creator in Yoruba religion. creatures.name: Olokun
creatures.excerpt: Olokun is the Yoruba orisha of the deep ocean, owner of the sea, parent of Ajé (wealth). Androgynous: male in coastal areas, female inland. creatures.name: Olorun
creatures.excerpt: Olorun (Unknown). is a deity. Olórun is the supreme god in the Yoruba pantheon, the owner of the sky and the source of all life force (àṣẹ). He is considered the creator of the universe and delegates authority to the Orishas.. Source: Yoruba cosmology; Ifá tradition

creatures.name: Onatah
creatures.excerpt: Onatah is the corn spirit of the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois), one of the Three Sisters who sustain the people with the bean and squash spirits. creatures.name: Ondù
creatures.excerpt: Ondù is the Alpine water-spirit of Lombardy and Trentino, cousin of the Germanic Nixe and Nordic Nøkken: a pale youth in wet clothing, often playing a violin, sometimes a horse with a drenched mane. creatures.name: Ongon Spirit

creatures.name: Oniare

creatures.name: Orang Bunian

creatures.name: Orang Bunian

creatures.name: Orang Minyak (Oily Man)

creatures.name: Oriole Spirit
creatures.excerpt: The oriole (vàng anh) is a spirit figure of Vietnamese folk narrative, most famously in the tale of Tấm and Cám, where the wronged heroine is transformed into an oriole that sings beside the royal palace and later into other natural forms. creatures.name: Oro
creatures.excerpt: The supreme god of war and peace in Tahitian mythology, son of Ta'aroa (the creator god). creatures.name: Orochi
creatures.excerpt: Orochi (Unknown). is a serpent. Yamata no Orochi is an eight-headed, eight-tailed serpent from Japanese mythology. The storm god Susanoo slays the creature after discovering it has been devouring the daughters of an earthly couple.. Source: Kojiki (712 CE); Nihon Shoki (720 CE)

creatures.name: Orunmila
creatures.excerpt: Orunmila is the Yoruba orisha of wisdom, divination, knowledge, and prophecy. He is the custodian of the Ifá divination system, which contains 256 sacred verses (Odu) that encode the entire knowledge of the universe. Present at creation, Orunmila witnessed everything that would happen and recorded it in the Ifá corpus.

creatures.name: Osiris
creatures.excerpt: Osiris is the ancient Egyptian god of the afterlife, death, and resurrection. creatures.name: Ossobó
creatures.excerpt: Ossobó is a mystical rain-bird in Forro (São Toméan) folklore. Inhabiting cloud forests and mountain peaks, it manipulates weather and heals through sonic powers — its melodic calls bring nurturing energy. A symbol of hope, renewal, and connection to ancestral spirits. The tale 'Gertrude's Bird' features it.

creatures.name: Otso
creatures.excerpt: Otso ('The Bear', 'Honey-Paw') is the sacred bear spirit, king of the Finnish forest. Divine embodiment of bear, walking upright as man in powerful form. creatures.name: Owl Animal-Spirit of Haida

creatures.name: Owl Deity (Guarani)

creatures.name: Owl Deity (Guarani)
creatures.excerpt: No owl deity exists in Guarani religion, and the Guarani are a South American people of Paraguay, Brazil, and Argentina, not of the United States. Guarani and Paraguayan folklore instead cast the great horned owl (ñacurutú) as an evil bird of ill omen and the urutau as a spirit bird; no owl is worshipped or made a god.

creatures.name: Owl Deity of Blackfoot
creatures.excerpt: No owl deity is attested in Blackfoot religion. The Blackfoot (Siksika, Kainai, Piikani) instead held that owls could be inhabited by the spirits of medicine men, and owl feathers marked warriors and leaders, as in the black-dog society leader's owl-feather bonnet. The owl is a medicine bird, never a god.

creatures.name: Owl Deity of Blackfoot
creatures.excerpt: No owl deity is attested among the Blackfoot of Canada (Siksika, Kainai, Piikani of the Blackfoot Confederacy). Their genuine owl traditions are the Owl Dance, a social and courtship dance, and the belief that owls may carry the spirits of medicine men. The owl is honored in song and story but is not a deity.

creatures.name: Owl Deity of Mi'kmaq
creatures.excerpt: No owl deity is recorded in Mi'kmaq tradition. The Mi'kmaq know the owl as kokokwes, a name drawn from the barred owl's calling, and in the celestial story of the stars the Owl is one of the hunters who pursues the Great Bear across the night sky. But the owl is never a god.

creatures.name: Owl Giant of Yurok

It appears as a horse, goat, or human with animal features, leading travelers on wild rides but doing no lasting harm. Controlled by sharp spurs (cold iron). creatures.name: Pygmalion
creatures.excerpt: Pygmalion (Unknown). is a human. Pygmalion is a figure from Greek mythology, a sculptor from Cyprus who fell in love with his own ivory statue of a woman. creatures.name: Pyinsarupa
creatures.excerpt: The pyinsarupa is the Burmese chimeric guardian, from Pali pañcarūpa, 'five forms': a composite of the elephant, bullock, horse, white carp, and the tonaya (a horned leo-dragon); some renderings use lion, elephant, water buffalo, white carp, and hamsa. creatures.name: Páutiwa (Chief of Kóthluwalawan)
creatures.excerpt: Páutiwa is the winter-solstice kachina and the most venerable chief of the Zuni spirit pantheon. He rules Kothluwalawa, the spirit village beneath Kothluwalawa Lake, receives the spirits of the dead, and controls the ceremonial calendar, sending the kachinam to dance at Zuni when the world's rituals require them.

creatures.name: Póngo (Circle) Kachina
creatures.excerpt: Póngo, the Circle Kachina, is a figure of Hopi tradition. creatures.name: Põrgupõrgu (Hell)
creatures.excerpt: Põrgupõrgu (Hell) (Estonia). is a demon. Põrgupõrgu (Hell) is a demon from the folklore and mythology of Estonia.. Source: Estonian folklore; Põrgupõrgu refers to hell-demons in Estonian mythology.

creatures.name: Púca
creatures.excerpt: The Púca is an Irish shapeshifting spirit (púca, plural púcaí) of Celtic, English, and Channel Islands folklore. It appears as a sleek black horse with golden eyes, or as goat, cat, rabbit, raven, fox, wolf, goblin, or dog—always dark-furred. creatures.name: Púca (or Pook-al)
creatures.excerpt: The Púca (or Pook-al) is a regional Irish name for the púca, emphasizing its horse form: a shiny black steed that lures riders, or a goat with long horns, or a dark-haired slightly deformed human. creatures.name: Pārī
creatures.excerpt: The pari, or peri, is a Persian winged spirit of radiant beauty, born of fire yet gentle and luminous. creatures.name: Płanetnik
creatures.excerpt: Płanetnik (also chmurnik, obłocznik) is a Polish demonic cloud spirit — the soul of a suicide or sudden-death victim who controls storms and hail. creatures.name: Pūķis
creatures.excerpt: Pūķis (Latvia). is a household-spirit. Pūķis is a household spirit from the folklore and mythology of Latvia.. Source: Latvian folklore; Pūķis is a household spirit often appearing as a dragon.

creatures.name: Qals Mink Coast Salish
creatures.excerpt: Mink is the trickster of the Coast Salish, told of among the Saanich, Comox, and Lummi. Compared with Raven he is a negative hero, greedy, reckless, and vain, and his adventures — being swallowed by a whale, running across the sky as the Sun's son, tussling with Devilfish — are cautionary tales of how not to behave.

creatures.name: Qalupalik
creatures.excerpt: Qalupalik (Qallupilluit) is a humanoid sea creature of Inuit tradition that dwells beneath Arctic shorelines and ice floes, waiting to snatch children who wander too close to the water. creatures.name: Qalupalik
creatures.excerpt: The Qalupalik (Qallupilluit) is an Inuit sea creature of Greenland and Arctic Canada that kidnaps children wandering too close to ice floes. creatures.name: Qalupalik
creatures.excerpt: Qalupalik is the child-stealing ocean spirit told of across the Inuit world, including Greenland. creatures.name: Qamata
creatures.excerpt: Qamata (also known as uThixo) is the supreme creator god of the Xhosa people who existed before all things. creatures.name: Qarakorshaq
creatures.excerpt: Qarakorshaq is a monster of Turkic folklore said to lurk in dark hollows, abandoned houses and hidden pits, seizing and devouring anyone who draws near at night. creatures.name: Qat
creatures.excerpt: Qat is the creator deity and culture hero of the Banks Islands, Vanuatu. He is credited with fashioning the first humans from wood, bringing light by distributing darkness, and establishing many customs. creatures.name: Qilin
creatures.excerpt: Qilin (麒麟) is the benevolent composite beast of Chinese tradition, with a dragon's head, deer's body, ox's tail, and fish-scale skin, sometimes bearing a single horn. creatures.name: Qori-Ismaris

creatures.excerpt: Qori-Ismaris (literally 'the stick-rubber') is a legendary figure from Somali mythology known as the Hyena-Man, the Somali equivalent of the Western werewolf. creatures.name: Queen Arawelo
creatures.excerpt: Queen Arawelo (Carraweelo) was a legendary proto-Somali queen who established a matriarchal society in the Sanaag region around the 1st century CE. creatures.name: Quetzalcoatl
creatures.excerpt: The Feathered Serpent, key Mexican-American deity. Aztec god of wind (Ehecatl) and the morning star (Venus), he made humanity in Mictlan from his blood and ancestral bones. creatures.name: Qutb Shah
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Pakistani folklore as a ghost entity. 'Qutb Shah' primarily refers to the Qutb Shahi dynasty rulers of Golconda (1518–1687) or the mythological ancestor of the Punjabi Awan tribe.

creatures.name: Qutrub
creatures.excerpt: The Qutrub (also spelled Qutrub) is a type of werehyena from Arabian folklore, a shape-shifting creature that combines human and hyena traits. creatures.name: Quỷ
creatures.excerpt: Quỷ is the Vietnamese term for ghost and demon, from the Chinese character 鬼, the soul of the dead. In folk belief quỷ are souls unable to reincarnate, wandering the world; in Buddhist cosmology the term includes malevolent beings (Ác quỷ, Ngạ quỷ, yaksha, la sát), and Cao Đài holds vengeful souls transform into them.

creatures.name: Qwaxw (Raven)
creatures.excerpt: Qwaxw, the Raven of the Nuxalk people of Bella Coola, British Columbia, is the great transformer who freed the light: in the Nuxalk creation account of the four carpenters, Qwaxw released Nusximta, a crystal ball of sunlight held in a container, to light the world. creatures.name: Qwaxw Raven Nuxalk
creatures.excerpt: Qwaxw is the Raven of Nuxalk (Bella Coola) tradition, made from charcoal by the youngest of the Four Carpenters, who cried 'qwaxw, qwaxw, qwaxw' when he came to life. creatures.name: Ra (Sun God of Egypt)
creatures.excerpt: Ra (or Re) is the supreme sun god of ancient Egyptian religion, the creator of all life and the ruler of the cosmos. creatures.name: Radien-attje
creatures.excerpt: Radien-attje (also Raedie or Veralden Olmai, meaning 'World Man') is the supreme high god in Sami mythology, the ruler of the cosmos and the celestial father. creatures.name: Raedieahkka

creatures.name: Ragana
creatures.excerpt: Ragana (Lithuania). is a goddess. Ragana is a goddess from the folklore and mythology of Lithuania.. Source: Lithuanian mythology; a goddess or witch figure associated with magic and fate.

creatures.name: Rahko
creatures.excerpt: Rahko is a Finnish lunar spirit who paints the moon's phases with tar, documented by Ganander in Mythologia Fennica (1789) as a being who covers the moon during eclipses. creatures.name: Rainbow Serpent

creatures.name: Rakke
creatures.excerpt: Rakke is the supernatural dog of the Stallo giant in Sami folklore. If Stallo is slain, Rakke can lick his wounds and restore him to life, so a hero who defeats the giant must also kill the dog or the victory is undone. Rakke appears in the Stallo tales recorded by Qvigstad, including 'How the Stalos Were Tricked.'

creatures.name: Rakshasa

creatures.name: Rana Niejta
creatures.excerpt: Rana Niejta is the Sami spring and vegetation goddess, the daughter of the high god Radien-attje and his wife Raedieahkka. Her name means 'the green' or 'the fertile fields.' creatures.name: Rangda (Demon Queen)
creatures.excerpt: Rangda is the terrifying demon queen of the Leyaks in Balinese mythology, the eternal antagonist of Barong. creatures.name: Rannamaari

creatures.name: Ranta

creatures.name: Raróg

creatures.name: Ratcatcher of Hamelin
creatures.excerpt: The Pied Piper of Hamelin (Rattenfänger von Hameln) is a German legend from 1284. A multicoloured ('pied') piper lured rats into the Weser River with his magic pipe; when the town refused payment, he returned on Saints John and Paul's day and led 130 children into a mountain cave (Koppenberg/Calvary), never to return.

creatures.name: Ratovantany
creatures.excerpt: Ratovantany is the earth creator god in Malagasy mythology who shaped the physical bodies of all living beings from clay. creatures.name: Ravana
creatures.excerpt: Ravana is the ten-headed demon king of Lanka in the Indian epic Ramayana. creatures.name: Raven

creatures.name: Raven (Nang Kilslas)

creatures.name: Raven Coast Salish

His stories are told from the Squamish to the Halkomelem and Nooksack, where he shares the stage with other animal transformers in the tales of the myth age.

creatures.name: Raven Deity of Ashanti

creatures.excerpt: Nang Kílslaas, 'The One Whose Voice is Obeyed,' is the Haida name for Raven, the creator-transformer who shaped Haida Gwaii and stole the sun, moon, stars, and fresh water to bring them to the world. creatures.name: Raven Nature-Spirit (San)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in San (Khoisan) tradition of Botswana. While San folklore includes avian spirits (e.g., ostrich, vulture in /Xam narratives documented by Bleek & snip Lloyd), a specific "Raven Nature-Spirit of the valley" lacks verification. Ravens are rare in the Kalahari; snip the entry appears templated.

creatures.name: Raven Nature-Spirit (San)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested. The San are the indigenous peoples of southern Africa, not of the United States, and no San tradition records a raven nature-spirit; the record's 'USA mythology' framing is a double misattribution. Ravens appear as trickster-creators only in far northern traditions, so this entry appears to

creatures.name: Raven Nature-Spirit of Ashanti
creatures.excerpt: The Raven Nature-Spirit of Ashanti protects swamp domains with stone manipulation and animal friendship, teaching ecological respect through guidance.

creatures.name: Raven Nature-Spirit of Blackfoot
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Blackfoot folklore. Ravens and crows play no significant role in Blackfoot tradition, whose transformer and trickster is Napi (Old Man), helped by his wife Old Lady; the Blackfoot Sky World holds the Sun Naato'si, the Moon Ko'komiki'somm, and the star heroes. A raven nature-spirit of the B

creatures.name: Raven Nature-Spirit of Blackfoot
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Blackfoot folklore. Ravens and crows play no significant role in Blackfoot tradition, whose transformer and trickster is Napi (Old Man), helped by his wife Old Lady; the Blackfoot Sky World holds the Sun Naato'si, the Moon Ko'komiki'somm, and the star heroes. A raven nature-spirit of the B

creatures.name: Raven Nature-Spirit of Ute
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Ute folklore. No Ute valley-spirit is a raven; Ute mythology centers on Sinawav, the Coyote creator who let the peoples escape from his bag of sticks, and on the Coyote cycle of trickster tales. A raven nature-spirit of the Ute appears to be a modern fabrication, not a genuine Ute being.

creatures.name: Raven Qwaxw Nuxalk
creatures.excerpt: Raven, called Qwaxw in Nuxalk, is the culture hero of Bella Coola mythology, a revered transformer who shaped the world for the people. Benevolent in his great acts, he is also a trickster, and many Nuxalk stories tell of his frivolous, ill-considered behavior landing him in trouble.

creatures.name: Raven Spirit (Laotian)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a named figure of Lao folklore; searches locate no 'Raven Spirit.' A crow appears in the Lao legend of the crow and the peacock, in which the two birds painted each other's plumage, and the raven's scavenging ties it to death in village belief, but no documented entity named 'Raven Spirit'

creatures.name: Raven Spirit of Hopi
creatures.excerpt: Crows and ravens are genuinely important in Hopi tradition: the Crow Mother kachina (Angwusnasomtaka, also Angwushahai-i) is a chief kachina who supervises the Powamu initiation whipping and is called the mother of all the kachinas, and the crow acts as a Hopi messenger between the living and the dead. Its black plumag

creatures.name: Raven Trickster (Cree)
creatures.excerpt: Raven is a central trickster and culture hero of Northwest Coast peoples such as the Tlingit, Haida, and Nuxalk, credited with bringing light and daylight to the world. Among the Cree, however, the primary trickster is Wisakedjak (Whiskeyjack); the raven appears mainly in minor or incidental roles. The attribution of a

creatures.name: Raven Trickster of Cheyenne
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Cheyenne folklore. The Cheyenne trickster is Veeho (Wihio), the spider, who appears as a man and whose foolish, self-serving adventures teach lessons; ravens are not tricksters in Cheyenne tales. This entry is a misattribution, almost certainly transplanting the Raven trickster of the Paci

creatures.name: Raven Trickster of Miwok
creatures.excerpt: The Raven is a genuine figure of Miwok mythology, a great hunter and one of the first animal people. In Southern Sierra Miwok tales, Raven (Kah'-kool) painted himself black with charcoal so the deer could not see him and became the successful hunter whose black plumage he still wears; in creation accounts, Raven (Kok'-

creatures.name: Raven Trickster of Yurok
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Yurok folklore. The Yurok trickster is Coyote, as among the neighboring Karuk and Hupa of northwestern California; no Yurok tale makes Raven a river-guardian or trickster. The entry appears to be a misattribution of the Pacific Northwest Raven cycle to a people whose trickster traditions c

creatures.name: Raven Trickster of Zulu
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Zulu tradition. No ethnographic source documents a raven trickster guarding springs. Zulu avian spirits include the lightning bird (impundulu) and vultures as ancestral messengers. The "raven trickster" template duplicates other regional entries with swapped animals.

creatures.name: Raven Water-Spirit of Blackfoot
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Blackfoot folklore. No water-spirit raven exists in Blackfoot tradition, where the waters are instead the home of the Horned Snake (Omahksoyisksiksina), a fearsome man-eating lake monster, and the tribe's trickster is Napi. A 'Raven Water-Spirit of Blackfoot' is a modern invention or misat

creatures.name: Raven Water-Spirit of Blackfoot
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Blackfoot folklore. No water-spirit raven exists in Blackfoot tradition, where the waters are instead the home of the Horned Snake (Omahksoyisksiksina), a fearsome man-eating lake monster, and the tribe's trickster is Napi. A 'Raven Water-Spirit of Blackfoot' is a modern invention or misat

creatures.name: Raven Water-Spirit of Inuit
creatures.excerpt: Raven (tulugaq) is a bringer of light and a creator in Inuit tradition, most fully developed among western Arctic and Alaskan Inuit. In the origin of light, the raven-billed child Tulugaak cried until its grandfather's bladder, which held the light, broke open and light filled the world; raven is credited with creating

creatures.name: Raven Water-Spirit of Kazakh
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a distinct water-spirit of Kazakh folklore. No source confirms a raven water-spirit guarding mountains or causing drownings; attested Kazakh water lore centers on the lake-serpent Aidakhar and the wind-camel Jhelmaia, with no such raven figure in ethnographic records. The traits recorded a

creatures.name: Raven Water-Spirit of Tlingit
creatures.excerpt: Raven (Yéil) is the foremost transformer and trickster of the Tlingit, the shaper of the present world. In the eternal stories (tlaagú), he placed the sun, moon and stars in the sky, stole the box of light from its keeper to end the darkness, and gave form to the rivers and landscape. Sometimes helpful, often mischievo

creatures.name: Raven Water-Spirit of Tlingit
creatures.excerpt: Raven (Yéil) is the foremost transformer and trickster of the Tlingit, the shaper of the present world. In the eternal stories (tlaagú), he placed the sun, moon and stars in the sky, stole the box of light from its keeper to end the darkness, and gave form to the rivers and landscape. Sometimes helpful, often mischievo

creatures.name: Ray Water-Spirit (Botswana)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Botswana tradition. No ethnographic source documents a "Ray Water-Spirit" protecting fields. The Herero have Zumwani (water woman), Tswana have water spirits (modimo wa metsi), but a ray-specific spirit is unverified. Appears to be a fabricated templated entry.

creatures.name: Ray Water-Spirit (Botswana)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in documented Tswana or Tongan folklore or academic sources. No source links a ray fish to a water-spirit in Botswana or Tongan tradition. The record conflates a Tongan attribution with Malagasy-flavored descriptions of a field- and valley-protecting spirit and appears to be a speculative con

creatures.name: Red Boy
creatures.excerpt: In the Jicarilla Apache creation narrative, Holy Boy (the record's 'Red Boy') is the younger companion of Killer-of-Enemies. At the dawn of the world he traveled to obtain the sun from White Hactcin and the moon from Black Hactcin, bringing light into the darkened world. His deeds are central to the Jicarilla origin cy

creatures.name: Red Headband
creatures.excerpt: Red Headband is a Comorian nature spirit haunting Mount Karthala's active crater on Grande Comore. Appears as a giant human wearing a red headband, stalking and killing intruders, naturalising unexplained volcanic deaths. Documented in Comorian oral tradition as deterrent against venturing into the dangerous summit zon

creatures.name: Red-headed Duck
creatures.excerpt: Red-headed Duck is a transformed aspect of the Flat Pipe Creator in Arapaho creation mythology. When all other animals had failed to bring up mud from the primordial waters, the Creator transformed his Flat Pipe into a Red-headed Duck and dove into the waters himself alongside Turtle. Together they succeeded in bringin

creatures.name: Redcap
creatures.excerpt: The Redcap (powrie) is a malevolent goblin of Anglo-Scottish Border folklore. He haunts ruined castles, wears iron boots and a red cap dyed in victims' blood, carries a pikestaff, and throws stones at travelers. Driven off by Scripture or a crucifix, vanishing in flames and leaving a large tooth. The most famous is Rob

creatures.name: Redcap
creatures.excerpt: The Redcap (Robin Redcap) is a murderous goblin of English Border folklore (Northumbria), haunting ruined castles—especially those of tyrannical lords. Wears a red cap soaked in victims' blood, iron boots, carries an iron pikestaff, throws huge stones. Repelled by religious symbols. Famous as familiar of Lord Soulis of

creatures.name: Restless Spirit (Blackfoot)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Blackfoot folklore. No source records a restless water-spirit in Blackfoot tradition; the Blackfoot believe the souls of the dead journey to the Sand Hills, the shadow-land of the afterlife, and their water beings are the Horned Snakes. 'Restless Spirit (Blackfoot)' appears to be an AI-gen

creatures.name: Revenant Iceland
creatures.excerpt: Revenant Iceland (Unknown). is a undead. A revenant from Icelandic saga tradition is a reanimated corpse with supernatural strength.. Source: Icelandic folklore — revenants documented in Icelandic sagas and folk tradition.

creatures.name: Rice Spirit
creatures.excerpt: The rice spirit of Lao and Thai tradition, closely tied to Mae Phosop (Mother Rice), holds the life force believed to inhabit the rice crop. Farmers propitiate her with rituals and offerings at planting and harvest, and the loss of her presence is thought to drain fields of vitality. The figure links agricultural pract

creatures.name: Riri Yaksha (Blood Demon of Sri Lanka)
creatures.excerpt: Riri Yaksha (Blood Demon) is one of the most feared demonic figures in Sinhalese folklore, central to the Bali and Tovil exorcism traditions of Sri Lanka. According to legend, Riri Yaksha was born from the blood of a slain demon — when a powerful demon was killed, his spilled blood gave rise to this new, even more male

creatures.name: Risin
creatures.excerpt: Risin (The Giant) is a colossal petrified giant who, along with his wife Kellingin, was sent from Iceland to steal the Faroe Islands. Risin waded into the sea while Kellingin climbed Mount Eiðiskollur with a heavy rope to tie the islands together so she could push them onto his back. They struggled through the night bu

creatures.name: River Mother (Cherokee)
creatures.excerpt: The Cherokee 'River Mother' matches the Siren of the French Broad River, a water spirit of Cherokee Tennessee tradition first published by William Gilmore Simms in 1845 as 'The Syren of Tselica'. She lures travelers to a mountain stream and drags them underwater. Her story warns of seductive deception rather than the p

creatures.name: River Mumma
creatures.excerpt: River Mumma (River Maiden) is a Jamaican water spirit appearing as a beautiful woman with long black hair, comb and mirror, dwelling at river sources. Derived from West African Mami Wata traditions via the Twi Nsuo Ba (river child/virgin). She lures men, grants riches to the favored, and punishes disrespect.

creatures.name: River Woman (Zapotec)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a drowning or luring 'river woman' spirit in Zapotec folklore. The closest genuine Zapotec water-woman is Lucía Zenteno, 'The Woman Who Outshone the Sun,' a beautiful Zapotec woman of magic who was exiled by her jealous village and took the river's water away with her in punishment. Her st

creatures.name: River Woman (Zapotec)
creatures.excerpt: The record's 'River Woman (Zapotec)' is Lucía Zenteno, the radiant Zapotec woman of Oaxacan tradition so beautiful that the sun itself fell in love with her and carried her away. Her husband pursued her into the sky, but a jealous moon spirit parted them forever. The story, retold by Alejandro Cruz Martínez in 'The Wom

creatures.name: Robin Chinook
creatures.excerpt: Robin is the long-suffering elder brother of Blue Jay in Chinook myth as recorded by Franz Boas. Patient and obedient, Robin endures Blue Jay's tantrums, sings at his shamanic cures, and helps gather the payments of roots, meat, and grease that the brothers bring home after healing the duck and the wolf girl.

creatures.name: Roc
creatures.excerpt: The Roc (rukh) is the giant bird of Arabian legend, large enough to carry an elephant in its talons. In the Sinbad voyages of the Thousand and One Nights, sailors mistake its egg for a dome and are lifted aloft when they cling to its leg. The roc also served medieval audiences as an explanation for giant fossil bones,

creatures.name: Roc
creatures.excerpt: The Roc (rukh) is a colossal mythical bird of Arabian Peninsula legend, said to be so huge it can carry elephants and darken the sky with its wings. A motif of the Thousand and One Nights and of Arab geographers' accounts (al-Qazwini, Ibn Battuta), it dwells on remote mountains and islands; its supposed bones explained

creatures.name: Roc
creatures.excerpt: Roc (Arabic/Persian). is a bird. An enormous bird of prey, so large it is capable of carrying away elephants. Source: Arabic and Persian folklore, The Thousand and One Nights

creatures.name: Roc (Rukh)
creatures.excerpt: The Rukh (roc) is the gigantic bird of prey of Arabic and Persian legend, an eagle-like creature with talons strong enough to lift an elephant and carry it to its mountain nest. Solitary and ancient, it is the apex predator of the remote seas; its role in Sinbad's voyages and the accounts of medieval geographers made i

creatures.name: Roc (Rukh)
creatures.excerpt: The roc, called rukh in Persian, is a colossal bird of prey from the tales of One Thousand and One Nights. With wings that blot out the sun and talons large enough to lift an elephant, it carries its prey to mountain-top nests. In the voyages of Sinbad the Sailor, sailors mistake its egg for a dome, and the furious bir

creatures.name: Rock Crystal Boy
creatures.excerpt: Rock Crystal Boy is a resident deity in Navajo tradition, appointed by First Man and First Woman to dwell at the sacred mountain Sisnaajiní (Blanca Peak) in the East. Along with Rock Crystal Girl, he was created when the sacred mountains were re-established in the Fourth World. Sisnaajiní was decorated with white shell

creatures.name: Rock Crystal Girl
creatures.excerpt: Tséghádiʼnídíinii atʼééd, Rock Crystal Girl, is a Navajo holy being who dwells with her brother Rock Crystal Boy at Sisnaajiní (Blanca Peak), the sacred mountain of the East. She was created by the Holy People when the six sacred mountains were re-established after the emergence into the Fourth World, embodying the whi

creatures.name: Rokurokubi
creatures.excerpt: Rokurokubi (轆轤首) is a Japanese yōkai that looks like an ordinary person, usually a woman, by day but whose neck stretches to surprising length at night, letting her head roam, spy, and lick lamp oil. Folklore warns that a person whose neck aches at night may be a rokurokubi; the head can be kept from rejoining the body

creatures.name: Rolling Calf
creatures.excerpt: The Rolling Calf is a feared Barbadian and Jamaican duppy (malevolent spirit) taking the form of a headless bull or goat with blazing red eyes, trailing chains, and foul stench. It roams villages at night, chasing and terrifying travelers. A classic duppy variant documented in Caribbean folklore collections.

creatures.name: Rongo
creatures.excerpt: The god of agriculture and cultivated food in Cook Islands mythology. Rongo was one of the twin sons of Avatea (the first man) and Papa (the earth goddess), born alongside his twin Tangaroa. The twins divided dominion over all things between them. Rongo is also the grandfather of Rangi, the first king of Mangaia who pu

creatures.name: Rongo (Rongomatane)
creatures.excerpt: God of agriculture, cultivated food, peace, and the kumara (sweet potato). Rongo is one of the great children of Ranginui and Papatuanuku. After the separation of the parents, Rongo and his brother Haumia were relentlessly pursued by Tawhirimatea's storms. Their mother Papatuanuku hid them in her body, and they became

creatures.name: Roro Jonggrang (Slender Maiden)
creatures.excerpt: Roro Jonggrang is the tragic princess at the heart of the Javanese legend explaining the origin of Prambanan Temple. When the powerful prince Bandung Bondowoso fell in love with her and she rejected him, he attacked and conquered her father's kingdom. Forced to consider marriage, Roro Jonggrang set an impossible condit

creatures.name: Rounce
creatures.excerpt: The Rounce is a malevolent spirit in the folklore of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, said to grunt like a pig and carry people away if they are out at night. Tradition holds that someone seized by a Rounce must be beaten with a stick, counting the blows, since passing the set count summons a rival Rounce. It is class

creatures.name: Rounces
creatures.excerpt: Rounces are Vincentian spirit-animals causing night terrors by riding sleepers, producing paralysis and oppression. Documented in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines folklore as nocturnal entities that sing and induce sleep paralysis, related to the wider Caribbean duppy/jumbie complex.

creatures.name: Rumpelstiltskin
creatures.excerpt: Rumpelstiltskin (Rumpelstilzchen) is a German fairy-tale imp collected by the Brothers Grimm (1812, KHM 55). A miller's daughter, locked to spin straw into gold, is aided by a little man who demands her necklace, ring, and finally her firstborn.

creatures.name: Rusalka
creatures.excerpt: Rusalka is the female water spirit of Slavic origin who occupies a central place in Ukrainian folklore distinct from the forest-dwelling Mavka. creatures.name: Rusalka
creatures.excerpt: Rusalka is a water-spirit from Czech Republic mythology. She is the soul of a young woman who drowned, either by suicide after a broken heart or by accident, or of an unbaptized child. Rusalki appear as beautiful pale maidens with long, loose green or brown hair, disproportionately long arms, and translucent skin. They

creatures.excerpt: Rusalka is a water-spirit from Ukraine mythology. She is the soul of a young woman who drowned, either by suicide after a broken heart or by accident, or of an unbaptized child. creatures.name: Rusalka (Water Spirit)
creatures.excerpt: Rusalka are the female water spirits of Slavic folklore, often the souls of drowned maidens who sing and lure travelers to the water. creatures.name: Ruwa
aliases: the Supreme God of the Chaga
creatures.excerpt: Ruwa is the supreme god of the Chaga people of Tanzania, a solar deity dwelling on the snow-capped peak of Kilimanjaro. Ruwa resides in the sky alongside his consort the moon on Kibo peak. The mountain is the physical manifestation of Ruwa's presence -- its glaciers his crown, its forests his garments, its rivers his b

creatures.name: Ryangombe
creatures.excerpt: Ryangombe is the Rwandan culture hero—great warrior and healer—who became leader of the Imandwa (spirits mediating between Imana the supreme deity and humans). The Kubandwa cult centres on spirit possession ceremonies invoking Ryangombe for healing, fertility, and justice. He exemplifies post-mortem apotheosis: a human

creatures.name: Rávga
creatures.excerpt: Rávga (from Norse 'draug') is an undead sea creature in Sami folklore — the soul of a drowned person whose body was never found and properly buried. Unlike the Čáhcerávga (water wraith) which was known to be fictional, the Rávga was believed to be real and dangerous. It appears as a long-haired, large-mouthed creature

creatures.name: Rørosgubben
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Norwegian folklore. No scholarly or primary source documents a ghost-miner legend of Røros; the name appears as a Røros polska folk tune in music collections rather than as a supernatural figure.

creatures.name: Rùa
creatures.excerpt: Rùa, the turtle of Vietnamese legend, is best known as Thần Kim Quy, the Golden Turtle God who lent An Dương Vương the magic claw that built his citadel and later reclaimed Lê Lợi's sword in Hoàn Kiếm Lake. As a cosmic turtle it also bears the world, an image of the enduring Vietnamese earth.

creatures.name: Rübezahl
creatures.excerpt: Rübezahl, mountain giant of the Giant Mountains (Riesengebirge/Krkonoše), rules weather, mines, and beasts. First recorded by Praetorius (1662), popularised by Musäus (1783). He appears as monk, giant, or gnome, rewarding the virtuous and punishing mockery. Name from Rübe (turnip) and zählen (count)—a princess tasked h

creatures.name: Rākshasa
creatures.excerpt: Rākshasa (with diacritics) is the Sanskrit term for Rakshasa — the same entity as 'rakshasa' entry. Not a distinct being. creatures.name: Rồng (Vietnamese Dragon)
creatures.excerpt: Rồng, the Vietnamese dragon, is a serpentine water dragon with flowing whiskers and a flaming pearl, bringer of rain and symbol of imperial power. creatures.name: Rồng Biển
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a named spirit of Vietnamese folklore; no source documents a sea dragon called 'Rồng Biển.' Vietnam's attested water beings are the dragon-like thuồng luồng (a riverine crocodile-serpent), maritime deities such as Hải Long Vương, and the whale-spirit veneration of fishing villages, but no

creatures.name: Rồng Hồ
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a named spirit of Vietnamese folklore; no source documents a golden lake dragon called 'Rồng Hồ.' The Hoàn Kiếm legend that anchors the entry centers on the Golden Turtle, Thần Kim Quy, not a dragon: the turtle received Lê Lợi's sword and returned it to the deep, giving the lake its name.

creatures.name: Saci Pererê
creatures.excerpt: Saci Pererê is Brazil's most iconic trickster: a one-legged black youth wearing a red magical cap, smoking a pipe, traveling in dust devils (wind swirls). He plays pranks, hides objects, braids horse manes, and can be captured by throwing a sieve into his whirlwind and stealing his cap. Originates from Tupi-Guarani 'Ma

creatures.name: Sacred Birds of Summerland
creatures.excerpt: The Sacred Birds of Summerland are the origin of the small birds in Zuni tradition. A Zuni man found a magical bundle of feathers left by the spirits, and when he walked into a field of flowers the bundle burst open, releasing small wings that became jaybirds, sparrows, finches and all the bright little birds that hera

creatures.name: Sacred Drum Spirit
creatures.excerpt: The Luba ngoma is a sacred royal drum of the Luba people of the Democratic Republic of Congo: a single-headed goblet drum carved from wood with a reptile-skin head. Played at the Luba court for the investiture or funeral of a ruler or dignitary, royal drums (milumbu) were central to the sacred kingship of the mulopwe.

creatures.name: Saharan Desert Jinn (Jenun)
creatures.excerpt: In Mauritania, belief in desert jinn (jenun) is deeply embedded in culture, shaped by the vast Sahara. Made of smokeless fire, they inhabit deserts, ruins, oases and remote passes; sandstorms, mirages and the howling of winds are read as their work. Some jinn are Muslim and harmless, others malevolent; travellers fear

creatures.name: Saharan Ghoul (Al-Ghul)
creatures.excerpt: Al-Ghul, the desert ghoul, is a shapeshifting, corpse-eating spirit of Saharan and Mauritanian tradition. It haunts graves, ruins and remote wastes, luring travelers to their death by appearing as a familiar face or a beautiful woman; the female ghula may even marry a man before revealing her nature. Belief in it disco

creatures.name: Saint Yared
creatures.excerpt: Saint Yared is the legendary 6th-century Ethiopian saint who founded the liturgical music tradition of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. Born in Axum, Yared was a slow learner as a child who often ran away from his studies. One day, inspired by watching a caterpillar persistently climb a stalk after repeated fall

creatures.name: Saint-Chart (or Saint Chartres)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in documented French folklore or academic sources: no legend records a dragon named Saint-Chart or a dragon-saint victory at Chartres. The record appears to conflate the Saint George pattern with Chartres, whose documented legends concern the martyrs' well and the Virgin's veil; its south por

creatures.name: Saka
creatures.excerpt: Saka is a guardian familiar of Malay folklore: a spirit inherited within a family or acquired through a pact, bound to protect its keeper in exchange for offerings. creatures.name: Sakpata
creatures.excerpt: Sakpata is the Fon vodun of the earth, smallpox, disease, healing, and agriculture. As one of the children of Mawu and Lisa, Sakpata was born as part of a pair of twins and given dominion over the earth pantheon. Sakpata is a dual-natured deity — he rules the fertility of the land and provides for humanity but also pun

creatures.name: Salmon Ancestor-Spirit of Cheyenne
creatures.excerpt: Not attested in Cheyenne folklore. The Cheyenne are a Plains buffalo-hunting people with no salmon in their territory or recorded stories; their trickster is Veeho, a spider who appears as a man. Salmon traditions belong to Northwest Coast peoples such as the Haida, Tlingit, and Chinook. This entry transplants coastal

creatures.name: Salmon Ancestor-Spirit of Dogon
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested: salmon are not native to the Niger bend region of Mali, and no salmon ancestor-spirit appears in Dogon cosmology. The closest real Dogon analogue is the Nommo, amphibious ancestral beings tied to water and creation.

creatures.name: Salmon Ancestor-Spirit of Inuit
creatures.excerpt: Not attested as an Inuit ancestor-spirit. Inuit mythology centers on sea-mammal spirits such as Nuliajuk (Sedna) and the moon god; salmon and char are food fish but do not appear as ancestral spirits in the recorded corpus. 'Salmon Ancestor-Spirit' does not occur in Inuit tradition and is a modern coinage.

creatures.name: Salmon Boy Nuxalk
creatures.excerpt: Salmon Boy is a guardian-spirit tale told by the Nuxalk and many Northwest Coast peoples. creatures.name: Salmon Chief Tsimshian
creatures.excerpt: The Salmon Chief is the ruler of the salmon people, who in Northwest Coast belief don salmon coats each season. In the story recorded by Boas, a fisherman releases a talking salmon chief and is repaid with fortune; when he fails to keep the salmon bones, the chief's daughter tells him the bones are babies. The tale und

creatures.name: Salmon Deity of Ashanti
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested: salmon do not occur in Ghanaian waters, and no salmon deity appears in Ashanti sources. Likely a conflation with West African riverine spirits such as those honored at the Antoa shrine or the crocodile guardian of Ashanti royal tradition.

creatures.name: Salmon Deity of Guarani
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested. Salmon (Salmo salar, Oncorhynchus) are native to the northern hemisphere and absent from Paraguay's subtropical/tropical rivers. creatures.excerpt: Serpan is a Seychellois serpent spirit from Creole oral tradition, capable of shapeshifting into pearl necklaces or children. Associated with forest magic and the supernatural world. Limited English documentation; primarily in Seychellois Creole folklore collections. May relate to Indian Ocean 'Naga' serpent traditions

creatures.name: Set (God of Chaos and Storms)
creatures.excerpt: Set is the Egyptian god of chaos, storms, violence, and the desert. He murdered his brother Osiris out of jealousy and fought his nephew Horus for the throne of Egypt for 80 years. Depicted as a mysterious animal with a curved snout (the Set animal), he was associated with the barren desert, foreign lands, and upheaval

creatures.name: Seven Bison
creatures.excerpt: Seven Bison are sacred spirit animals in Crow mythology who fought against the monster Bones Together. After breaking their legs against Bones Together's impenetrable bone armor, they were healed through the first Sweat Lodge ceremony performed by their human companion. After this victory and healing, the Creator raise

creatures.name: Seven Rams
creatures.excerpt: Seven Rams are magnificent spirit animals in Crow mythology. A Crow man of immense ability and power once encountered them in the mountains. Confident in his own strength, he thought he could overpower them. But the Seven Rams taught him humility—despite his great power, the man learned he must respect the Sweat Lodge

creatures.name: Seven Sisters
creatures.excerpt: The Seven Sisters is a widespread Aboriginal Australian Dreaming story found across many language groups. The story tells of seven sisters who fled across the land and into the sky to escape a persistent pursuer, often a man named Wurrurrumbi or a hunter who wanted to take one of the sisters as his wife.
