creatures.name: SGaana (Supernatural Killer Whale)
creatures.excerpt: SGaana are the powerful supernatural killer whales of Haida mythology, considered the most powerful of the undersea beings. They can transform into human form and own houses, territories, and crests just like human chiefs. The SGaana live in magnificent underwater villages with houses made of copper and abalone shell.

creatures.name: Sgaana Supernatural Killer Whale Haida
creatures.excerpt: Sgaana, in Haida belief, are the supernatural beings of the sea, and the killer whale is their visible form in this world. creatures.name: Shade (Olmec)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a 'shade' or vengeful ghost of Olmec folklore. The Olmec left no textual record of a haunting water-spirit, and scholars identify only a small pantheon of Olmec supernaturals, including the Maize God and a rain/were-jaguar figure. The burial-site and ruin-haunting traits resemble generic g

creatures.name: Shade (Olmec)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Colombia. The Olmecs were a Mesoamerican civilization (Veracruz/Tabasco, Mexico, 1400-400 BCE), not Colombian. Colombia's pre-Hispanic cultures include Muisca, Quimbaya, Tairona, San Agustín. 'Shade' as a ghost type is European; no Olmec ghost tradition exists in Colombia.

creatures.name: Shade (Olmec)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a USA or North American being. The Olmec were an ancient Mesoamerican civilization of the Gulf Coast of Mexico, and no specific 'Shade' spirit is documented among them; the record's burial-site and battlefield habitat tags are template filler.

creatures.name: Shadhavar
creatures.excerpt: The Shadhavar is a legendary antelope-like creature from medieval Muslim bestiaries, thought to have originated in what is now Iraq. creatures.name: Shahmaran
creatures.excerpt: Shahmaran (from Persian Shah-i-Maran, 'King of Snakes') is a mythical half-woman, half-snake creature revered in Azerbaijani, Turkish, and Kurdish folklore. She is the immortal queen of all serpents, possessing profound wisdom and magical healing powers. According to widespread legend, Shahmaran dwells in an undergroun

creatures.name: Shahmaran
creatures.excerpt: Shahmaran ('King of Snakes') is a mythical half-woman, half-snake being revered in Azerbaijani, Turkish and Kurdish folklore: the immortal queen of serpents, keeper of profound wisdom and healing power. In Azerbaijani variants the legend is known in Nakhchivan, Lankaran and the Araz River basin. The tale of Cəmşab reco

creatures.name: Shahmaran (Kurdish Serpent Queen of Wisdom)
creatures.excerpt: Shahmaran is a legendary half-woman, half-serpent figure in Kurdish, Turkish, Persian, and Mesopotamian folklore. The name means 'King of the Serpents' in Persian. According to legend, a young man named Camsab accidentally discovered the underground realm of the serpents, where Shahmaran (the beautiful serpent queen) r

creatures.name: Shaitan (Iblis, the Devil in Islam)
creatures.excerpt: Shaitan (Ash-Shaytan), also known as Iblis, is the leader of the devils (shayatin) in Islamic theology. Originally a devout jinn created from smokeless fire, Iblis was elevated to a high station among the angels due to his piety. When God commanded all beings to bow to Adam, Iblis refused out of pride, arguing that he

creatures.name: Shakuru
creatures.excerpt: Shakuru is the Sun god in Pawnee mythology, one of the last of all gods placed in the heavens by Tirawa. Along with Pah (the Moon), Shakuru is of relatively minor standing in Skidi Pawnee spirituality compared to the more prominent star gods. The Sun and Moon produced a son, a boy who was placed on Earth to be the ance

creatures.name: Shalako
creatures.excerpt: The Shalako are tall, ten-foot kachina messengers of the Zuni, beings of great spiritual power who appear each winter. During the Shalako ceremony, six Shalako—each the horned, feathered impersonation of a rain-bringing spirit—visit the newly built ceremonial houses, blessing the homes and the people.

creatures.name: Shaman
creatures.excerpt: Shamans are ritual practitioners, not spirits: among the Tlingit the shaman (íx̲t) gained power from spirit helpers to heal, find lost souls and combat witchcraft; among the Inuit the angakkuq serves the community and speaks with the sea mother Sedna. The record uses 'Shaman' as a generic spirit entry; the genuine figu

creatures.name: Shaman

The record uses 'Shaman' as a generic spirit entry; the genuine figu

creatures.name: Shango
creatures.excerpt: Shango is the Yoruba orisha of thunder, lightning, fire, virility, dance, and justice. Originally the third Alaafin (king) of Oyo, Shango was deified after death and ascended to heaven. He is the patron of twins (Ibeji) and the owner of the double-headed battle axe (oshe), which represents swift divine justice. Shango

creatures.name: Shape-shifting Demon
creatures.excerpt: The Shape-shifting Demon is a malevolent entity in Comanche creation mythology. It formed in the shadows, envious of the powerful Comanche people created by the Great Spirit. It tormented the Comanche by taking many forms. The Great Spirit cast the demon into a bottomless pit, but before falling, the demon shattered in

creatures.name: Sheikh of the Nile (Nile River Spirit)
creatures.excerpt: The Sheikh of the Nile is a protective river spirit in Egyptian folk belief, a powerful guardian who inhabits the Nile River. He is a wali (saint) who oversees the river's bounty and dangers, controlling the annual flood, protecting fishermen and sailors, and punishing those who pollute or disrespect the Nile. The figu

creatures.name: Shenlha Okar
creatures.excerpt: Shenlha Ökar ('Wisdom gshen of white light,' also Shiwa Ökar) is the foremost deity of the Yungdrung Bon tradition of Tibet, counted among the Four Transcendent Lords. Creator of the world with the nine cosmic gods and sambhogakaya emanation of the founder Tonpa Shenrab Miwoche, he embodies supreme compassion, omniscie

creatures.name: Shetani
creatures.excerpt: Shetani (Swahili, from Arabic shaytan) are malevolent spirits of East African popular belief (Tanzania, Kenya, Mozambique), especially among the Makonde. creatures.name: Shetani (Spirit Carvings)
creatures.excerpt: Shetani (singular and plural in English, mashetani in Swahili) are spirits of East African mythology prevalent in Mozambique, particularly among the Makonde people of the northern Cabo Delgado province. These are mostly malevolent entities that manifest in a bewildering variety of forms with different powers and attrib

creatures.name: Shichhid
creatures.excerpt: Shichhid (or Chichid) is a Himalayan nature spirit in Uttarakhand/Arunachal folklore — smaller, benign Yeti variant inhabiting rhododendron forests. Local names vary by tribe (Monpa, Sherdukpen, Bhotiya). Described as hairy, forest-dwelling, protective of flora/fauna. Not a major deity but a local forest spirit. Docume

creatures.name: Shidaidaka
creatures.excerpt: Shidaidaka (次第高) is a yōkai reported in Shimane Prefecture and the Chūgoku region of Japan that grows taller and taller the longer a person looks up at it, looming ever higher over the viewer. creatures.name: Shiktur (Erlik)

No source confirms a deceiver called 'Shiktur' associated with Erlik; Buryat tradition knows Erlik (Erlen) as the underworld judge, but no 'Shiktur' appears in published mythology. creatures.name: Shir (or Sheed)
creatures.excerpt: Shir (or Sheed) is the Armenian mythical lion — a giant golden or dusty-brown lion with glowing eyes, often depicted with a solar motif or crown. creatures.name: Shiva
creatures.excerpt: Shiva (Mahadeva) is a supreme Hindu deity (Trimurti) — god of destruction, transformation, meditation, asceticism. Not a folkloric creature but a major god. creatures.name: Shteli Kherkher
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a distinct nature-spirit of Afghan or Pashtun folklore. creatures.name: Shtojzovalle
creatures.excerpt: Shtojzovalle, the 'moonlight dancers' of Albanian folklore, are beautiful spirit women who dance in moonlit meadows and mountain clearings, enchanting mortals with hypnotic grace. creatures.name: Shwe Temperature

creatures.name: Si'lah

creatures.name: Si'lat

creatures.name: Si'lat
creatures.excerpt: The si'lat is a shape-shifting female jinn of Palestinian and wider Arab folklore, kin to the ghoul but wickeder and unable to change her limbs. creatures.name: Si'luwa
creatures.excerpt: The Si'luwa is a female water demon from Iraqi folklore that haunts rivers, streams, and caves near running water. creatures.name: Sieidi Spirit
creatures.excerpt: Sieidi (also seita) spirits are the spiritual forces dwelling in unusual rock formations, stones, or landscape features considered sacred in Sami religion. creatures.name: Sielulintu
creatures.excerpt: The Sielulintu is not a bird of flesh and bone, but a luminous projection of the human psyche. creatures.name: Sigbin
creatures.excerpt: The sigbin is a creature of Visayan folklore, a hornless, dog-like beast with oversized hind legs and enormous flapping ears that walks backwards with its head between its legs. creatures.name: Siguanaba
creatures.excerpt: La Siguanaba is one of the most famous figures in Salvadoran folklore — a shapeshifting spirit that appears as a beautiful long-haired woman from behind but reveals the face of a horse or skull when she turns around. creatures.name: Sihuanaba

creatures.name: Silver Fox

creatures.name: Simbi Spirits

creatures.name: Sina
creatures.excerpt: Sina is one of the most important female figures in Samoan mythology, best known from 'Sina and the Eel,' the story that explains the origin of the coconut. creatures.name: Singbonga (Supreme God of the Munda)
creatures.excerpt: Singbonga is the supreme creator god of the Munda; his name means 'Sun God.' In the creation myth he set a cosmic egg afloat on a primordial sea, from which hatched Horo the tortoise and Karakom the crab. creatures.name: Singh Dhan
creatures.excerpt: Singh Dhan (Golden Lion/Deer) appears in Rajasthani folk tales as a divine golden deer granting wishes. creatures.name: Singing Well Spirit

No source confirms a singing well-spirit prophesying fate in Khiva or Khorezm; the attested Kheyvak well legend involves the boy Shem, not a prophetic singing spirit. creatures.excerpt: Sint-Holo is the horned serpent of Chickasaw and Choctaw tradition, a great water serpent who dwells in rivers, lakes and springs. creatures.name: Sinti
creatures.excerpt: Sinti is the Great Serpent of Choctaw tradition, a water monster with a panther's head and horns that dwells in rivers, lakes and whirlpools. creatures.name: Sinti Lapitta
creatures.excerpt: Sinti Lapitta is the great horned serpent of Choctaw tradition, a giant water snake with two horns on its head, in some accounts a panther head, that lives in the deep waters. It possesses great power and wisdom and was said to visit unusually wise young men, granting them knowledge and strength.

creatures.name: Sirdalsjøormen

creatures.name: Siring
creatures.excerpt: Siring are dwarfs of Philippine lower mythology, tiny green-skinned beings with pointed ears who dwell in nunuk (banyan) trees and forest mounds. creatures.name: Sisimito
creatures.excerpt: The Sisimito is a bipedal gorilla-like cryptid from Belizean and Honduran folklore, often called the Mexican Bigfoot. It is described as large, covered in black or dark brown fur, with four fingers on each hand and no thumbs, ape-like facial features, and backward-facing feet with no knees. creatures.name: Sisimito
creatures.excerpt: The Sisimito is a cryptid from Panamanian and Central American folklore, described as a bipedal gorilla-like humanoid with long unkempt fur and a human-like head. creatures.name: Sisiutl
creatures.excerpt: The Sisiutl is the double-headed sea serpent of the Kwakwaka'wakw and neighboring Northwest Coast peoples, with a serpent head at each end of its body and a human-like face at the centre, all three horned. Seeing it means death to the unprepared, but a warrior who faces it may gain superhuman strength and armor from it

creatures.name: Sisiutl (Double-Headed Sea Serpent)
creatures.excerpt: Sisiutl is a supernatural sea serpent of the Kwakwaka'wakw, usually shown as a double-headed snake with two horned serpent heads flanking a central human face, its body marked with crescents. Its glance can turn a person to stone, yet it also grants protective power, and can transform into an invincible war canoe or a

creatures.name: Sisiutl Kwakwaka Wakw
creatures.excerpt: Sisiutl is the double-headed sea serpent of the Kwakwaka'wakw, a fearsome supernatural creature whose glance can kill or turn an adversary to stone. creatures.name: Siv Yis (Shee Yee — First Hmong Shaman)
creatures.excerpt: Siv Yis (also spelled Shee Yee or Siv Yig) is the legendary first shaman in Hmong mythology who received shamanic power from the spirit world and taught it to humanity. creatures.name: Själens port

creatures.name: Sjöjungfru
creatures.excerpt: Sjöjungfru (Lake Maid) is a Swedish freshwater spirit, a beautiful woman with long wet hair who dwells in deep lakes. creatures.name: Sjöorm

creatures.name: Sjörået

creatures.name: Sjødraug

creatures.name: Skadegamutc

creatures.name: Skan
creatures.excerpt: Skan (Taku Skanskan) is the sky spirit and supreme judge in Lakota cosmology as recorded by James R. Walker. creatures.name: Skarsfjellgubben

creatures.name: Skeleton Spirit

creatures.name: Skimina (Granddaughter of Alhkw'ntam)

creatures.name: Skogsfru

The name means 'forest-wife' (skog = forest, fru = wife/lady).

creatures.name: Skookum

In Chinook folklore the wild man of the woods, called Boqs, Siatco, Sasquatch or Skookum, is a large, hairy forest being, usually a dangerous man-eater though sometimes benign.

creatures.name: Skrzak
creatures.excerpt: Skrzak (or skrzat) is a household spirit of Polish and West Slavic folklore, a small goblin-like being who lives in the home or its garden, brings luck and prosperity while the household is virtuous, and hides or turns spiteful when mistreated. creatures.name: Sky Father (Cheyenne)

creatures.name: Slattenpatte

creatures.name: Snåsavettern

creatures.name: Stikini
creatures.excerpt: The Stikini are dreaded owl-witches of Seminole folklore. By day they look like ordinary people, but at night they vomit up their souls and internal organs and become undead owl-monsters with bloodshot eyes that feed on human hearts. In some communities, saying the name aloud is itself thought to risk transformation.

creatures.name: Stiklestadsgjenferden
creatures.excerpt: Stiklestadsgjenferden (the Stiklestad Ghosts) are the spectral apparitions said to haunt the Stiklestad battlefield in Verdal, Trøndelag. creatures.name: Stone Coat
creatures.excerpt: The Stone Coats, or stone giants, are terrible giants of Iroquois tradition, taller than any man and covered in a skin of rock-hard scales (native names include Genonsgwa). They wander the winter lands of the Adirondacks and Alleghenies, and heroes defeat them by striking their one soft spot.

creatures.name: Stone Giant
creatures.excerpt: The Stone Giants (Otneyarhed or Stone Coats) are a race of cannibalistic giants from Iroquois mythology whose skin is as hard as stone, making them nearly invulnerable to weapons. creatures.name: Storjunkare
creatures.excerpt: Storjunkare are sacred stone beings in Sami religion — unusually shaped stones or rock formations resembling humans or animals that were set up on mountaintops, in caves, or near rivers and lakes as objects of worship. The term comes from Scandinavian Sami tradition and describes large, sacred stones that were treated

creatures.name: Stormkäringen
creatures.excerpt: Stormkäringen (the storm hag) is a malevolent old woman figure in Swedish coastal folklore who raises storms to destroy ships and drown fishermen. creatures.name: Storsjöodjuret
creatures.excerpt: Storsjöodjuret is Sweden's most famous lake cryptid, reported in Lake Storsjön (Jämtland) since the 17th century. Described as serpentine, 10-14 meters, with humps, smooth skin, sometimes a long neck. Briefly granted protected species status (1986-2005). A modern cryptid phenomenon with deep roots in local oral traditi

creatures.name: Strandvaskare
creatures.excerpt: Strandvaskaren (shore wanderer) is the ghost of a drowned person whose body was never given proper Christian burial. Unlike a regular ghost, the Strandvaskare is bound to the shoreline where the body washed up, wandering the beach at dusk searching for rest. It leaves wet footprints on dry sand that lead nowhere — no b

creatures.name: Stria
creatures.excerpt: Stria (striga) is a vampire spirit of Bulgarian and Balkan folklore, sometimes a witch who leaves her body at night to harm the living, sucking blood and bringing illness. creatures.name: Strig (or Štrig)
creatures.excerpt: Strig (strigoi) is a vampire or evil spirit of Croatian and broader Balkan folklore, the restless dead who return to drink blood and trouble their families. The term derives from the Latin striga, and folk belief prescribed protections at burial, including poppies, thorns, and the burning of suspected undead.

creatures.name: Striga
creatures.excerpt: A semi-demonic being with supernatural powers used to harm her community. creatures.name: Strigoi

creatures.name: Strzyga
creatures.excerpt: Strzyga is a vampire of Polish folklore, depicted with two hearts, two souls, and sometimes a bird of prey birthmark, who rises at night to drink blood. creatures.name: Stállo
creatures.excerpt: Stállo is the most iconic antagonist in Sami folklore — a large, human-like cannibal giant who eats people, especially children. creatures.name: Stökkull

creatures.name: Su Anasi
creatures.excerpt: Su Anasy (the Water Mother) is the water spirit of Tatar and wider Turkic folklore: a beautiful woman who dwells in rivers and lakes, combing her long hair on the bank. creatures.name: Suliskongen
creatures.excerpt: Suliskongen (the King of Sulitjelma) is the troll king of the Sulitjelma mountains in Nordland, and the father of the legendary Seven Sisters — Botnkrona, Grytfoten, Skjeringen, Tvillingene (the Twins), Kvasstinden, and Breitinden. creatures.name: Sumanguru Kante
creatures.excerpt: Sumanguru Kanté is the villainous sorcerer-king of the Sosso people in the Epic of Sundiata. He was a powerful king who seized the remnants of the Ghana Empire and conquered nine neighboring kingdoms, including the Mandinka lands. Sumanguru was a master blacksmith and powerful sorcerer, invulnerable to all weapons exce

creatures.name: Sumbo
creatures.excerpt: Sumbo refers to the ritual masks of the Bwaba (Bobo) people of Burkina Faso, which are believed to embody powerful spirits that connect the human world with the invisible realm of ancestors and bush spirits. creatures.name: Sumpurnis
creatures.excerpt: Sumpurnis (Latvia). is a shapeshifter. Permanent predator wrapped in dense, shaggy fur - bear-like humanoid with man's torso and dog's head. Source: Baltic folklore; a shaggy humanoid predator from regional myths.

creatures.name: Sun
creatures.excerpt: In Chiricahua and Mescalero Apache tradition, the Sun is the great creator deity who brought light and order to the world. Their creation story begins with a great flood that destroyed a malevolent world, and the creator, closely linked to the Sun, shaped the world, the gods, and all living things through his power.

creatures.name: Sun (Jóhonaaʼéí)
creatures.excerpt: Jóhonaaʼéí, the Sun, is a central deity of the Navajo (Diné). A being in human form, he carries the Sun across the sky each day and hangs it on a peg in his home at night. creatures.name: Sun Goat
creatures.excerpt: Among the Garap people of Chad, a myth explains the taboo on eating he-goat: a man found daylight personified as a he-goat in the forest but ate it instead of delivering it to the priest. creatures.name: Sun Goddess (Muisca)
creatures.excerpt: Partially attested but gender is incorrect. The Muisca sun deity is Sué (Xué, Zuhé), a male god, not a goddess. creatures.name: Sun Goddess (Muisca)
creatures.excerpt: Muisca tradition pairs the Moon goddess Chía with Sué (also Sua), the masculine Sun god, both born from the creator Chiminigagua. creatures.name: Sun Nuxalk
creatures.excerpt: The Sun is a powerful sky deity of the Nuxalk (Bella Coola), who dwells in a celestial house and carries the torches that light the day. He tests his sons-in-law with impossible tasks, and in the origin tale his mortal wife bears a son who takes the sun's course, burns the earth, and is cast down to become the mink.

creatures.name: Sun Spirit (Olmec)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a named sun spirit of Olmec folklore. creatures.name: Sun Tsimshian
creatures.excerpt: In Tsimshian myth the Sun is a celestial chief whose son, Walks-All-Over-The-Sky, carries a burning cedar-bark mask across the heavens each day; sparks from his mouth become the stars and his charcoal-faced brother becomes the moon. creatures.name: Sun Wukong
creatures.excerpt: Sun Wukong (孫悟空), the Monkey King, is the trickster hero of the Ming-dynasty novel Journey to the West: a stone-born monkey with a magic staff that can grow to any size, somersault clouds, transformations, and hairs that create copies of himself. After rebelling against heaven, he guards the pilgrim Xuanzang westward,

creatures.name: Sundiata Keita
creatures.excerpt: Sundiata Keita was the legendary founder of the Mali Empire, the greatest empire in West African history. Born crippled and unable to walk, Sundiata was the son of King Maghan Kon Fatta and the ugly, hunchbacked woman Sogolon. A prophecy foretold his greatness. creatures.name: Sungrasspan
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a named entity in Brazilian Cerrado folklore. The name 'Sungrasspan' appears to be an English portmanteau ('sun grass span'). Brazilian savanna spirits include Caipora, Curupira, and local 'encantados,' but no specific 'Sungrasspan' is documented.

creatures.name: Suniyam Demon (Sinhalese Sorcery Spirit)
creatures.excerpt: Suniyam is the chief demon of sorcery and black magic in Sinhalese folklore, believed to be one of the most powerful and dangerous of the Yaksha spirits. creatures.name: Supay
creatures.excerpt: Supay is the Inca/Quechua/Aymara lord of Uku Pacha (the underworld), an ambivalent deity of death, shadows, and mineral wealth. creatures.name: Supernatural Seal Iceland
creatures.excerpt: Supernatural Seal Iceland (Unknown). is a animal-spirit. A supernatural seal from Icelandic folklore is a shapeshifting selkie that sheds its skin to become human.. Source: Icelandic folklore — selkie/seal spirits documented in Icelandic maritime tradition.

creatures.name: Suuke (cave-dwelling monsters)
creatures.excerpt: The Suuke are cave-dwelling monsters of Zuni tradition, lesser demonic beings who live in the cliffs and caves around Zuni lands. They carry off children in their baskets, and are counted among the dangerous supernatural creatures associated with Atahsaia, the terrible man-eating ogre of Zuni legend.

creatures.name: Suv Peri (Water Fairy)
creatures.excerpt: Suv Peri (Water Fairies) are mythical water spirits from Turkmen folklore inhabiting the Caspian Sea coast and rivers such as the Amu Darya. creatures.name: Svartalv (Swedish)

creatures.name: Swaichen

creatures.name: Swan Maiden

creatures.name: Sweat House

creatures.name: Sweet Medicine
creatures.excerpt: Sweet Medicine (Motsé'eóeve) is the greatest prophet and law-giver of the Cheyenne people. creatures.name: Sylph
creatures.excerpt: The sylph is the air elemental of Western esotericism, coined by Paracelsus in the 16th century as the airy counterpart of the salamander, undine and gnome. creatures.name: Syöjätär
creatures.excerpt: Syöjätär is a Finnish ogress from runic songs and Ganander's Mythologia Fennica (1789). creatures.name: Sáráhkká

creatures.name: Takhar

creatures.name: Talking Fox
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a named entity in Nordic folklore. creatures.name: Taniwha

creatures.name: Taotaomo'na
creatures.excerpt: Taotaomo'na, the 'people of before,' are the ancestral spirits of the ancient Chamorro, told across Guam and the Northern Marianas. Said to be the ghosts of early inhabitants, they inhabit banyan trees, deep jungle, and caves, and can be hostile to those who trespass or disturb ancient sites and bones. Their displeasur

creatures.name: Tar-Baby
creatures.excerpt: The Tar-Baby is a doll made of tar and turpentine created by Br'er Fox to trap Br'er Rabbit in the most famous African American folktale. Br'er Fox fashions the doll and sets it in the road. When Br'er Rabbit greets the silent figure and receives no reply, he grows angry and strikes it, becoming stuck. Each successive

creatures.name: Tata Duende
creatures.excerpt: Tata Duende is one of Belize's most famous mythical creatures — a powerful forest spirit that protects animals and the jungle. Described as a small, bearded man about three feet tall who wears a wide-brimmed red hat, animal skins for clothing, and has his feet pointing backwards. He notably lacks thumbs. Parents warn c

Described as a small, bearded man about three feet tall who wears a wide-brimmed red hat, animal skins for clothing, and has his feet pointing backwards. He notably lacks thumbs. Parents warn c

creatures.name: Tatzelwurm
creatures.excerpt: A legendary dragon-like lizard creature from Alpine folklore, also called Stollenwurm, Bergstutz, or Stutzn depending on the region. The Tatzelwurm is described as having the face of a cat with a long serpentine body, four short legs (or sometimes only two forelegs), ranging from one to seven feet in length. Local name

creatures.name: Tatzelwurm
creatures.excerpt: Tatzelwurm is a dragon from Germany mythology. The Tatzelwurm is described as having the face of a cat with a long serpentine body, four short legs (or sometimes only two forelegs), ranging from one to seven feet in length. Local names in Styria and Tyrol include Bergstutz ('mountain stump'), reflecting its stubby appe

creatures.name: Tatzelwurm
creatures.excerpt: Tatzelwurm is a dragon from Austria mythology. The Tatzelwurm is described as having the face of a cat with a long serpentine body, four short legs (or sometimes only two forelegs), ranging from one to seven feet in length. Local names in Styria and Tyrol include Bergstutz ('mountain stump'), reflecting its stubby appe

creatures.name: Tautramunken
creatures.excerpt: Tautramunken (the Monk of Tautra) is a ghostly figure that haunts the ruins of Tautra Cistercian monastery on the island of Tautra in the Trondheimsfjord, near Frosta. The monastery was founded in 1207 and was one of the most important Cistercian houses in Norway until it was dissolved during the Reformation in 1532. T

creatures.name: Tawa (Sun Spirit)
creatures.excerpt: Tawa is the primary creator deity in Hopi tradition, the Sun Spirit who existed alone in endless space (Tokpella) before creation. He formed the First World and created Sotuknang, his nephew, who in turn created Spider Woman as a messenger. Tawa divided himself creating Muiyinwuh, God of All Life Germs. He destroyed th

creatures.name: Tawescaron
creatures.excerpt: Tawescaron is the malevolent twin brother of Huron mythology, the younger twin and eternal antagonist of Ioskeha. He created monsters, darkness, winter, and all that is harmful in the world. He constantly tried to undo his brother's good works. Tawescaron represented darkness, destruction, and death. In the great race

creatures.name: Tawhirimatea
creatures.excerpt: God of winds, storms, clouds, and weather. Tawhirimatea, son of Ranginui and Papatuanuku, was the only one of the children who opposed the separation of their parents. Enraged at the forced separation, he joined his father in the sky and became the god of wind and storms. He unleashed devastating tempests against his b

creatures.name: Tay
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Sudanese folklore under this name. Tay is described as a serpent-like water spirit of the Nile who blesses fishermen with good catches or drags the disrespectful beneath the water. The figure fits the documented river-spirit world of northern Sudan and Nubia, including the banat el Hur and

creatures.name: Taytoru
creatures.excerpt: Taytoru is the magical steed of Semetey in the Kyrgyz Epic of Manas, a sleek, fiery-eyed horse of supernatural speed and endurance. She carried Semetey from Bukhara across the mountains to the Talas valley so he could avenge his father Manas's death. Loyal and shrewd, she is the archetype of the epic hero's faithful mo

creatures.name: Te Ngaru
creatures.excerpt: Te Ngaru ('The Wave') is a culture hero of Mangaia in the Cook Islands, whose exploits explain the ocean's power. Grandson of Moko the Great Lizard, he matched himself against the great ocean swell Tikokura and the man-eating shark Tumutearetoka, riding the crests of the sea in a struggle recorded by the missionary Wil

creatures.name: Te Pusi mo te Ali
creatures.excerpt: Te Pusi mo te Ali ('The Eel and the Flounder') is a Tuvaluan creation tale of the lagoon: an eel and a flatfish are bound in a conflict or agreement that shapes the lagoon's life, and eels are regarded as sacred and tapu in Tuvaluan tradition. The story carries the lagoon-based world-view of the atolls.

creatures.name: Te Wheke-a-Muturangi
creatures.excerpt: The giant octopus that was pursued across the Pacific by the Polynesian navigator Kupe. Te Wheke-a-Muturangi belonged to Muturangi, a chief from Hawaiki. The octopus harassed Kupe's fishing lines and stole his bait repeatedly. Kupe vowed to destroy it and chased it across the Pacific Ocean in his canoe Matahourua. The

creatures.name: Tefolaha
creatures.excerpt: Tefolaha is the founding ancestor of Nanumea atoll in Tuvalu, a partly divine hero said to have come from Tonga and to have established the island's chiefly lines. His spear Kaumaile is a treasured heirloom of the island, and descent from him is claimed by Nanumea's principal families, making him a central figure of Tu

creatures.name: Tek-ko-kui
creatures.excerpt: Tek-ko-kui, the 'bamboo pole ghost' of Taiwanese folklore, is said to haunt bamboo groves at dusk, bending a bamboo culm under tension and letting it snap to strike and kill those who pass. Stories place it near the former Kawabata Bridge in Taipei as well as in Yonghe and Chiayi. The legend is used to explain the dang

creatures.name: Teke
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Kyrgyz folklore by this name. Teke, the Turkic word for the ibex, is here described as a guardian spirit of mountain passes and high peaks who protects or misleads according to respect shown. The documented protector of wild game in Kyrgyz and Turkic hunting tradition is Kayberen, guardian

creatures.name: Teke Teke
creatures.excerpt: Teke Teke (Unknown). is a ghost. Teke Teke is a modern Japanese urban legend about the ghost of a woman who was cut in half by a train. She drags herself on her elbows through the streets, making a "teke teke" sound, and will cut her. Source: Japanese urban legend; contemporary folklore

creatures.name: Telematua
creatures.excerpt: Telematua is a legendary giant-ancestor of Tuvaluan tradition, a being of colossal size said to have shaped the islands and their channels; his passage or labour is recalled as the origin of the passages (ava) between islets. Sluggish and indifferent to humans in most accounts, he is nonetheless a figure of the islands

creatures.name: Temple Guardian (Mixtec)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a named 'temple guardian' figure of Mixtec folklore. No Mixtec source records a stone or jade sentinel guarding temple entrances. The closest real analogue is the deity presiding over the Mixtec Temple of Death at Ñuu Ndeya (Chalcatongo): the skeletal goddess Lady 9 Grass (a Cihuacoatl-lik

creatures.name: Temple Guardian (Mixtec)
creatures.excerpt: In Mixtec (Ñuu Dzaui) belief the ñuhu are sacred beings who guard places: ancient stones, caves and springs are their homes, and hunters, farmers and builders must ask their leave. Temple entrances were watched by carved guardians and by ancestral spirits with clawed hands who seize the disrespectful, as with Lady 9 Gr

creatures.name: Tenga
creatures.excerpt: Tenga is the earth goddess of the Mossi (Moose) people of Burkina Faso, wife of Wende, the supreme sky god. She is the guardian of the land, its fields, and its fertility, and authority over the earth belongs to her; humans direct their prayers through Tenga to reach Wende. She is central to Mossi ideas of land, farmin

creatures.name: Tengbiswem Earth Spirit
creatures.excerpt: The Earth Spirit is the invisible guardian of the land, believed by the Mossi to be the true owner of the soil. This spirit governs the fertility of the crops and the overall health of the community. To avoid angering the spirit—which could result in drought, famine, or illness—the community relies on the Tengbiswem (E

creatures.name: Tengri
creatures.excerpt: Tengri is the supreme sky god of the Turkic peoples, the eternal blue sky whose worship long preceded Islam in Central Asia. Creator and sustainer above all spirits, he was honoured by shamans and steppe nomads with open-air rites on high ground. Kazakh reverence for Tengri still echoes in proverbs and in prayerful rai

creatures.name: Tengri Khormusta
creatures.excerpt: Khormusta, king of the western heavens, is the supreme sky deity of Buryat Tengriism and father of the hero Abai Geser. A radiant warrior-king amid celestial hosts, he wages eternal war against the eastern gods of darkness. His scattering of the slain Atai Ulan's body, meant to prevent resurrection, instead seeded the

creatures.name: Tengu
creatures.excerpt: Tengu are supernatural mountain spirits of Japanese folklore, commonly shown with long noses and magical powers, believed to be reincarnations of the proud. The daitengu are elder masters with red noses and feather fans, and karasu-tengu are crow-like; the daitengu Sōjōbō is said to have taught young Minamoto no Yoshit

creatures.name: Tepuhi
creatures.excerpt: Tepuhi is the founding ancestor of Nanumaga atoll in Tuvalu, a spirit who is said to have come from Fiji in the form of a sea serpent and to have established the island's people. Unlike Nanumea's ancestor Tefolaha, who came from Tonga as a half-human hero, Tepuhi's serpent form ties Nanumaga's origin to the ocean and t

creatures.name: Termite Animal-Spirit (Komi)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested: termites do not occur in the boreal forests of the Komi Republic, and no termite ancestor-spirit appears in documented Komi tradition. The entry likely conflates Komi nature guardians with an unrelated insect totem; no real analogue is recorded.

creatures.name: Terton (Treasure Revealer)
creatures.excerpt: Tertöns are treasure revealers of Tibetan Buddhism: visionary lamas and yogins who discover hidden terma, teachings concealed by Padmasambhava and Yeshe Tsogyal in caves, lakes, rocks, and monasteries. Entering meditative states, they often break convention to retrieve the hidden dharma. The terma system let Buddhist t

creatures.name: Teryel
creatures.excerpt: Teryel is the most famous ogress in Kabyle (Algerian Amazigh) mythology — a terrifying female monster with an anthropophagic (man-eating) appetite. According to a foundational Kabyle myth, when humanity was created as fifty men and fifty women, 98 chose to settle and build houses, but one man and one woman chose to liv

creatures.name: Thagyamin (King of the Nats)
creatures.excerpt: Thagyamin is the Burmese name for Sakka (Indra), king of the Tāvatiṃsa heaven and head of the 37 nats. King Anawrahta of Pagan placed him atop the nat pantheon in the 11th century to harmonize animism with Buddhism; unlike nats who died violent deaths, he earned his throne by merit. During Thingyan he descends invisibl

creatures.name: Thaman Kyah
creatures.excerpt: Thaman Kyah is the weretiger of Burmese folklore, a human who takes tiger form, gaining the beast's strength and stealth in jungles and remote villages. Predatory and secretive, it hunts by night and can only be unmasked by exposure of its true identity, after which its power fails. The figure reflects fear of hidden p

creatures.name: Thanh Gióng
creatures.excerpt: Thanh Gióng (Unknown). is a hero. Thánh Gióng is a legendary hero from Vietnamese mythology who grew from a three-year-old boy into a giant warrior overnight to defend the country from foreign invaders. After victory, he flew into the. Source: Vietnamese mythology; The Tale of Saint Giong

creatures.name: Thanh Minh
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a folkloric creature. In Vietnamese culture 'Thanh Minh' (Qingming) is the grave-sweeping festival of early April, a solar term for honoring the dead, not a wandering ghost of cold months. No source documents such a spirit tempting the living into the cold; the record conflates the festiva

creatures.name: The Chureca
creatures.excerpt: The Chureca is a Virgin Islands death-omen spirit appearing as an owl-like creature. Its cry or appearance near a home predicts imminent death in the household. A localized variant of the widespread Caribbean 'owl as death messenger' belief (cf. Jamaican rolling calf, Haitian loogaroo owl form). Not to be confused with

creatures.name: The Coastal Leviathan
creatures.excerpt: The Coastal Leviathan (Somali Maritime). is a beast. A giant sea monster that haunts the Indian Ocean coasts of Somalia. Source: Somali Coastal Oral History

creatures.name: The Dandan (World Fish)
creatures.excerpt: The Dandan, also known as Bahamut, is a colossal cosmic fish from Arabian and Islamic mythology that supports the structure of the world. According to medieval Islamic cosmography attributed to al-Qazwini and others, the Dandan lies deep beneath the earth, carrying on its back a massive bull named Kuyutha or Kiyuban, u

creatures.name: The Fish-Wife of Lake Toba
creatures.excerpt: The Fish-Wife of Lake Toba is the tragic spirit-woman at the center of North Sumatra's most famous origin myth. A poor fisherman named Toba caught a magical golden fish that transformed into a beautiful woman. She agreed to marry him on one condition: he must never reveal her fish origins. They had a son named Samosir,

creatures.name: The Forest Phantom
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a named entity in Ugandan folklore. 'Forest Phantom' / 'Green Shadow' / 'Way-Wanderer' appears to be a generic compilation of widespread Ugandan forest trickster motifs (hare/rabbit, leopard, mimicry spirits in Bwindi).

creatures.name: The Goli Spirit
creatures.excerpt: The Goli is a spiritual force manifested through an elaborate series of masks and dances among the Baoulé people. Rather than a single creature, it is a composite ancestral entity summoned from the forest to intervene in human affairs. The Goli appears during times of crisis, such as droughts or epidemics, or to celebr

creatures.name: The Great Nile Serpent
creatures.excerpt: The Great Nile Serpent is a colossal, iridescent-scaled serpent spirit guarding the Victoria Nile's deep trenches in Ugandan Nilotic/Bantu oral tradition. It emerges during lunar eclipses or ecological crisis, controlling currents and demanding tribute. Associated with Ruhanga (creator) and the underworld ruler.

creatures.name: The Great Peacemaker
creatures.excerpt: The Great Peacemaker, known as Deganawida, is the legendary founder of the Iroquois Confederacy (Haudenosaunee), the oldest living democracy in North America. Born among the Huron, he crossed Lake Ontario in a stone canoe to bring peace to the warring Iroquois nations. With the orator Hiawatha and the Seneca chief Jigo

creatures.name: The Great Whale of Creation
creatures.excerpt: In Kemak creation mythology from the Atsabe region of East Timor, a colossal cosmic whale caused a devastating flood that reshaped the world. creatures.name: The Helpful Fish
creatures.excerpt: The helpful fish of Qatari coastal lore is a benevolent water spirit that guards tide pools and the shallow Gulf waters, guiding honest fishermen to good catches. Often identified with the two-banded porgy known locally as al-fisaikra, it embodies foresight and clear speech, rewarding respect and punishing greed. Tales

creatures.name: The Kanaga Spirits
creatures.excerpt: The kanaga is the great wooden mask of the Dogon of Mali, danced during the dama, the funeral rite that escorts the soul of the deceased from the village of the living to the ancestral realm. creatures.name: The Lion of Njie
creatures.excerpt: In Serer tradition of Senegal, the lion is a totemic guardian associated with the Njie (Njai) clan and lineage. Clans hold specific animals as sacred ancestors and protectors, and the lion's strength and dignity mirror the clan's claims to authority. The figure connects the living community with the ancestors and the n

creatures.name: The Mantis
creatures.excerpt: The Mantis (Unknown). is a animal-spirit. The Mantis (also known as Kaggen or Cagn) is a central trickster-creator figure in San (Bushman) mythology of the Kalahari. He is a praying mantis who possesses great cunning and creative power.. Source: San (Bushman) mythology; Bleek and Lloyd collection

creatures.name: The Milkman of Pieter Both
creatures.excerpt: According to a popular local legend, the distinctive rock formation at the peak of Pieter Both Mountain is actually a milkman who was turned to stone. creatures.name: The Mountain Giant
creatures.excerpt: The Mountain Giant (Burundian). is a giant. A colossal stone-skinned giant inhabiting the mountains of Burundi. Source: Highland Oral History Found in L' la highest summits of the Burundi highlands and the Congo-Nile Divide.. Documented in ethnographic records.

creatures.name: The Mythical Korp
creatures.excerpt: The Korp (Raven) in Swedish folklore is far more than a bird; it is a conduit for prophecy and a witness to the fates of men. creatures.name: The Night-Walker
creatures.excerpt: The Night-Walker (Burundian). is a spirit. A spectral night-spirit that feeds on fear and dreams in Burundi. Source: Rural Burundian Folklore Found in Open valleys and the outskirts of rural Burundian villages during the night.. Documented in ethnographic records.

creatures.name: The Pale Fox
creatures.excerpt: The Pale Fox (Ogo, Yurugu) is a central figure in the creation mythology of the Dogon of Mali, the trickster twin who rebelled against the creator god Amma, bringing disorder, language, and divination to the world. creatures.name: The Rolling Cauldron
creatures.excerpt: The Rolling Cauldron is a Jamaican magical object — a cauldron that rolls along roads and crossroads at night. It contains either treasure or a curse depending on whether one touches it. A road-spirit motif warning against greed and nocturnal travel. Part of Jamaican 'duppy' (ghost) folklore complex.

creatures.name: The Saltigue
creatures.excerpt: Saltigue (saltigi) are the hereditary priests and priestesses of the Serer people of Senegal, guardians of the traditional religion and its pangool — the ancestral spirits and sacred forces believed to dwell in nature. creatures.name: The Tanganyika Serpent
creatures.excerpt: The Tanganyika Serpent (Burundian). is a beast. A silver serpent guarding the depths of Lake Tanganyika in Burundi. Source: Lakeside Oral Traditions Found in The deepest benthic zones of Lake Tanganyika.. Documented in ethnographic records.

creatures.name: The Trung Sisters (Hai Bà Trưng)
creatures.excerpt: The Trung Sisters — Trưng Trắc and Trưng Nhị — are Vietnam's most celebrated legendary heroines who led a rebellion against Chinese Han occupation in 40-43 CE. creatures.name: The Tuku'uru
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a siren or sea spirit of Solomon Islands folklore. The entry appears to be a gen

creatures.name: The Vao
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a ghost of Cook Islands folklore. In Cook Islands Māori, vao means 'bush' or 'wilderness' and does not name a spirit; documented spirits of the dead are tūpāpaku and the tīni, recorded by ethnographers such as Christian Clerk. 'Vao' is also the name of an island off Malekula, Vanuatu. The

creatures.name: Thoth
creatures.excerpt: Thoth, the ibis-headed god of the moon, is the Egyptian lord of wisdom, writing, magic, and judgement. Scribe of the gods and arbitrator of their disputes, he stands beside Ra's solar barque and records the verdicts of the dead. creatures.name: Three Sisters
creatures.excerpt: The Three Sisters are the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) story of corn, beans and squash as three sisters who refuse to be parted. creatures.name: Three-Fingered Jack (Jamaican Outlaw Hero)
creatures.excerpt: Three-Fingered Jack (Jack Mansong or Jack Mantong) was a legendary Jamaican outlaw and folk hero who terrorized the island in the late 18th century (c. creatures.name: Thunder Beings
creatures.excerpt: The Cherokee Thunder Beings (Aniyvdaqualosgi) are sky warriors who command thunder, lightning and life-giving rain and protect people from evil spirits. creatures.name: Thunder Spirit
creatures.excerpt: The Thunder Spirit is a powerful sky spirit in Blackfoot mythology, associated with storms, thunder, and lightning. According to legend, the Thunder spirit gave the Blackfoot the sacred pipe, where lightning had struck a tree and left a beautifully carved pipe. The Thunder spirit instructed the finder to form a society

creatures.name: Thunderbird
creatures.excerpt: The Thunderbird is a powerful sky spirit of Wabanaki (Mi'kmaq, Passamaquoddy, and other Wabanaki tribes) mythology. creatures.name: Thunderbird (Chinook)

creatures.name: Thunderbird (Wakinyan/Animikii/Hohoq)
creatures.excerpt: Legendary giant bird in Native American mythology—one of the most widespread and spiritually significant creatures. Creates thunder with wing-flaps and lightning from its flashing eyes or beak. Found in dozens of tribes from Pacific Northwest (Haida, Tlingit, Kwakwaka'wakw) to Great Plains (Lakota, Blackfoot) to Great

creatures.name: Thunderbird (Wakinyan/Animikii/Hohoq)
creatures.excerpt: Legendary giant bird in Native American mythology—one of the most widespread and spiritually significant creatures. Creates thunder with wing-flaps and lightning from its flashing eyes or beak. Found in dozens of tribes from Pacific Northwest (Haida, Tlingit, Kwakwaka'wakw) to Great Plains (Lakota, Blackfoot) to Great

creatures.name: Thunderer
creatures.excerpt: The Thunderers (Hadiwennoda:dye's), led by Hino (Hi-nun), are the storm spirits of Iroquois (Haudenosaunee) mythology: mighty bird-men who bring thunder and rain, battle the horned serpent (Oniare) and protect humanity and the crops. creatures.name: Thunders
creatures.excerpt: The Cree Thunderers are great thunderbirds (Piyesiw): immense eagles whose wing-beats roll as thunder, whose flashing eyes strike lightning, and who fight the underwater serpents. creatures.name: Thuy Tinh
creatures.excerpt: Thuy Tinh (Unknown). is a deity. Thủy Tinh (the Water God) is a deity from Vietnamese mythology who brings annual floods in his eternal rivalry with Sơn Tinh (the Mountain God) for the love of Princess Mỵ Nương.. Source: Vietnamese mythology

creatures.name: Thạch Tinh
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a distinct Vietnamese nature spirit. No source describes a 'Thạch Tinh,' a being living in rocks and boulders that is helpful or dangerous; searches surfaced the Sơn Tinh–Thủy Tinh legend of the Mountain God versus the Sea God and unrelated game lore, but no stone-spirit entity. The figure

creatures.name: Thủy Tinh (Water Spirit)
creatures.excerpt: Thủy Tinh (literally 'Water Spirit' or 'Water God') is the powerful deity of waters, seas, and floods in Vietnamese mythology. In the famous legend from the Hùng King period, Thủy Tinh sought to marry the beautiful princess Mỵ Nương but lost to his rival Sơn Tinh (Mountain Spirit), who arrived first with wedding gifts.

creatures.name: Ti Malice
creatures.excerpt: Ti Malice (Little Malice) is the Haitian trickster, a clever hare who repeatedly outwits his greedy, slow-witted uncle Bouki (hyena). creatures.name: Tibetan Snow Leopard Spirit
creatures.excerpt: In Tibetan tradition the snow leopard is a sacred guardian of the high Himalayas, linked to the mountain and wilderness deities of Tibetan Buddhism as a spiritual protector of the highlands. Its solitary, elusive nature lends an aura of purity and spiritual insight, and deities are said to ride it or take its form. The

creatures.name: Tiddalik the Frog
creatures.excerpt: Tiddalik is a giant frog of Gunaikurnai (south-eastern Australian) Dreaming tradition who drank all the water of the world, leaving the land dry and thirsty. creatures.name: Tide Woman Tlingit
creatures.excerpt: Tlingit storytellers recount how Raven made the tides, teaching the ocean to rise and fall. In the tale of how the tides began, the tide-water is kept by an old woman, in some versions Raven's grandmother, and Raven tricks her into releasing the water so the beaches can be walked and the sea fished.

creatures.name: Tidzi
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Senegalese folklore. No published source records a Senegalese bush spirit named Tidzi; searches return only Tidzi, a rural commune in Essaouira Province, Morocco, and related place names. The claim that a 'Senegalese bush spirit tests travelers' resembles the Rab spirits of Wolof and Lebou

creatures.name: Tie Snake
creatures.excerpt: The Tie-Snake, also called Water Serpent or Underwater Serpent, is a water spirit of the Muscogee (Creek) and other Southeastern peoples: though the size and shape of an ordinary snake, it possesses immense strength and deadly poison, seizing humans and dragging them under to drown. creatures.name: Tie-Snake
creatures.excerpt: The Tie-Snake (u'lax daxgi'ilu in Natchez) is a water spirit common to Southeastern Native American folklore, documented among the Natchez and neighboring peoples. creatures.name: Tifon
creatures.excerpt: No clear attestation of a demon named Tifon in Russian folk tradition; the figure appears to be a borrowing of the Greek Typhon, the storm giant, into Slavic demonology. Without primary documentation the entry cannot be verified, and no distinct Russian folk analogue is recorded.

creatures.name: Tigilau
creatures.excerpt: A powerful Samoan chief and warrior from ancient legend, Tigilau is remembered for his strength, leadership, and exploits. creatures.name: Turtle Giant of Dogon

creatures.name: Turtle Guardian of Haida

creatures.name: Utburd
creatures.excerpt: Utburd (also called utbør, utburðr) is the haunting spirit of an abandoned or murdered infant in Norwegian folklore. In pre-Christian and early Christian Norway, unwanted children - especially those born out of wedlock - were sometimes abandoned in the wilderness to die of exposure, a practice called utburd. The spirit

creatures.name: Uthixo
creatures.excerpt: Uthixo (Unknown). is a deity. uThixo is the supreme being in Xhosa cosmology, the creator of the universe and humanity. The name has been adopted for the Christian God in Xhosa-language Bibles.. Source: Xhosa oral tradition

creatures.name: Utlat (Carthaginian Netherworld Spirits)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in Carthaginian folklore or religion. No Punic or Carthaginian source records spirits called 'Utlat'; the name is not a Carthaginian term, and the entry wraps real tophet facts around an invented spirit class.

creatures.name: Utrøst-folket
creatures.excerpt: Utrøst-folket (the people of Utrøst) are a hidden folk who live on the legendary sunken island of Utrøst off the coast of Vestlandet. Utrøst is a fairy island that appears only to the pious or those with second sight — a paradise with golden barley fields, green pastures, and goats with golden horns. The inhabitants ar

creatures.name: Valraven
creatures.excerpt: Valraven (Unknown). is a undead. The Valraven is a mythical raven creature from Nordic folklore, an omen bird associated with the dead and supernatural forces in legend.. Source: Danish folklore — undead figure documented in Danish oral tradition.

creatures.name: Valravn
creatures.excerpt: Valravnen (the Raven of the Slain) is a supernatural raven in Danish medieval ballads and folklore. According to legend, a knight who died unshriven or a person who committed terrible acts could be transformed into a Valravn. The Valravn possesses human intelligence, speaks in human tongues, and has supernatural powers

creatures.name: Vampir
creatures.excerpt: Vampir is the Serbian vampire — the etymological root of the English word 'vampire'. An animated corpse rising from the grave at night to drink blood of the living. Created by suicide, excommunication, caul birth, or animal jumping over corpse. The 18th-century cases of Petar Blagojevich and Arnold Paole sparked the Eu

creatures.name: Vampire
creatures.excerpt: Vampire (Generic). is a vampire. Undead beings that subsist by feeding on the life essence of the living, often characterized by immortality and charm. Source: Global folklore, Balkan traditions

creatures.name: Varulv
creatures.excerpt: Den svenska varulven (the Swedish werewolf) differs from continental European werewolf legends in several ways. Swedish varulvar were often not voluntary shapeshifters but people born under a curse — those born with a 'vargbälte' (wolf belt, a caul) were doomed to become werewolves. Alternately, a person could become a

creatures.name: Varulv
creatures.excerpt: Den danske varulv (the Danish werewolf) has a unique origin not found in other countries: if a pregnant woman crawls through a horse's afterbirth to ease her labor pains, a son will become a werewolf and a daughter will become a mare (nightmare spirit). The Danish varulv is always male and transforms at sunset, his hum

creatures.name: Vasuki (King of Serpents)
creatures.excerpt: Vasuki is the king of the nagas (serpent beings) in Hindu mythology and one of the most important serpent deities. He is best known for his role in the Samudra Manthana (the churning of the Ocean of Milk), where he served as the churning rope wrapped around Mount Mandara. The devas (gods) held Vasuki's tail while the a

creatures.name: Verdalsdraugen
creatures.excerpt: Verdalsdraugen (the Verdal Draug) is a sea draug specific to the Verdal area at the northern end of the Trondheimsfjord. The draug is a malevolent undead being from Norwegian folklore, and the Verdalsdraugen is a localized version haunting the Verdal coast and the lower reaches of the Verdalselva river. According to lo

creatures.name: Veshtitza
creatures.excerpt: Veshtitza is a Montenegrin witch-vampire whose soul leaves her body at night in the form of a black hen or moth to scout homes with children. She returns to drain blood and consume hearts. By day she appears as an ordinary woman. A South Slavic variant of the striga/shtriga, blending witch and vampire traits. Feared as

creatures.name: Vetal
creatures.excerpt: Vetal is the Sri Lankan form of the vetala, a corpse-inhabiting spirit from Indian tradition that spread with Buddhism. It dwells in cremation grounds and ancient trees (tamarind, baobab), animating corpses to move. Known for posing riddles and knowing past, present, and future. Can be helpful or dangerous. The Vetala

creatures.name: Vetala
creatures.excerpt: Vetala (Sanskrit: वेताल) are corpse-inhabiting spirits in Hindu mythology who animate dead bodies (often feet-forward) and dwell in cremation grounds and tamarind/baobab trees. They possess uncanny knowledge of past, present, and future, and delight in riddles. The Vetala Panchavimshati features King Vikramaditya captu

creatures.name: Vette
creatures.excerpt: Vette (feminine: vetta, plural: vetter, from Old Norse vættr meaning wight/spirit) is a general term in Norwegian folklore for nature spirits and supernatural beings. The vetter are guardian spirits of specific natural places - forests, lakes, rivers, mountains, rocks, and farm buildings. The concept is related to the

creatures.name: Vetāla
creatures.excerpt: Vetāla is the diacritically-marked Sanskrit form of vetala (slug: vetala), not a distinct entity. This record duplicates vetala with near-identical data. In Sanskrit texts, vetāla inhabits corpses and trees (baobab/tamarind), knows past/present/future, and features in the Vetala Panchavimshati. The record's 'benevolent

creatures.name: Veyis Baba
creatures.excerpt: Veyis Baba is the protective spirit (iye) of camels in Turkmen mythology and folklore. Originally based on the historical figure Veysel Karani, a Yemeni Muslim camel herder known for his love of the Prophet Muhammad, Veyis Baba became the mythological guardian of camels among Turkmen and other Turkic peoples. In Turkme

creatures.name: Viejito del Monte
creatures.excerpt: El Viejo del Monte, the 'Old Man of the Forest' (Kiwíkgolo in Miskito), is the ghost of a tireless hunter punished by becoming a shaggy giant with a single eye who now defends the animals of the Nicaraguan bush. He rules over deer and game, thunder and rain, and can ride as a monstrous horseman; hunters must ask his le

creatures.name: Vila
creatures.excerpt: The Vila (plural Vile) are beautiful female nature spirits of South Slavic mythology, deeply embedded in Montenegrin folklore. They are described as eternally young maidens with pale cheeks, long flowing hair, dressed in white, with invisible wings enabling them to fly through the air. There are three kinds: land and f

creatures.name: Vila
creatures.excerpt: Vila is a spirit from South Slavic / Illyrian-influenced Mythology mythology. They are described as eternally young maidens with pale cheeks, long flowing hair, dressed in white, with invisible wings enabling them to fly through the air. There are three kinds: land and forest Vile (zagorkinje/pozemne vile), water nymph

creatures.name: Vila
creatures.excerpt: Vila is a spirit from Slavic mythology. They are described as eternally young maidens with pale cheeks, long flowing hair, dressed in white, with invisible wings enabling them to fly through the air. There are three kinds: land and forest Vile (zagorkinje/pozemne vile), water nymphs (brodarice/povodne vile), and cloud

creatures.excerpt: Vila is a spirit from Slavic mythology. They are described as eternally young maidens with pale cheeks, long flowing hair, dressed in white, with invisible wings enabling them to fly through the air. There are three kinds: land and forest Vile (zagorkinje/pozemne vile), water nymphs (brodarice/povodne vile), and cloud

creatures.name: Vindrå
creatures.excerpt: The Vindrå is the ethereal spirit of the wind, a volatile and invisible entity that governs the currents of the air. Unlike the grounded rån, the Vindrå is an entity of pure movement and change. In Swedish lore, the Vindrå is responsible for the sudden gusts that blow out candles or the gentle breezes that carry scents

creatures.name: Vinmara
creatures.excerpt: Vinmara (also called Ro-Lei) is a sky maiden from Vanuatu mythology, particularly in the Banks Islands. According to legend, Qat discovered a group of sky maidens who had removed their wings to bathe. He buried one pair of wings, forcing Vinmara to remain behind on earth. She became Qat's wife and was called Ro-Lei. Th

creatures.name: Vishap
creatures.excerpt: Vishap is the Armenian dragon — a winged serpentine creature closely associated with water (lakes, rivers, mountain springs). Dwelling on Mount Ararat, it causes thunderstorms, whirlwinds, and eclipses by ascending/descending. It steals children, replacing them with evil spirits. Vishap fought Vahagn the Dragon Slayer;

creatures.name: Vishnu
creatures.excerpt: Vishnu is a major Hindu deity (not a folklore creature), one of the Trimurti as Preserver. He reclines on the cosmic serpent Shesha in the Ocean of Milk and takes avatars (Rama, Krishna, Narasimha) to restore dharma. Classifying him as a 'water spirit' and 'mythical creature' is a category error — he is a supreme deity

creatures.name: Vitorm
creatures.excerpt: Vitormen (the white snake) is a magical serpent in Swedish folklore that guards hidden treasures beneath ancient rune stones, burial mounds, and Viking-age monuments. The Vitorm is distinguished by its pure white or pale golden color and is far larger than ordinary snakes. According to tradition, whoever manages to kil

creatures.name: Vittra
creatures.excerpt: Vittra are invisible underground wights of northern Sweden (Norrland), living in parallel cities with livestock. Resemble humans but unseen unless they choose. Peaceful if paths/dwellings undisturbed; cause accidents, illness, livestock loss if buildings block roads. 'Vittra-way' and 'Vitterställe' denote relocated pla

creatures.name: Vittra
creatures.excerpt: Vittra (Icelandic). is a wight. Invisible underground beings who live in parallel cities and protect their territory. Source: Icelandic and Scandinavian folklore

creatures.name: Vještica
creatures.excerpt: Vještica is the Croatian/Serbian word for 'witch' (from 'vješti' — to know), not a distinct creature. The record appears to conflate the general term with a specific ogre. Actual Croatian witch beliefs involve night flight on wooden beams, causing storms, illness, and infertility.

creatures.name: Vodnik
creatures.excerpt: Vodnik (Unknown). is a water-spirit. The Vodnik is a water spirit from Slavic folklore, particularly known in Slovenian tradition. It is said to dwell in rivers, lakes, and streams, and can appear as a humanoid with green hair and webbed. Source: Slavic Folklore: A Handbook (Kononenko, 2007)

creatures.name: Vodník
creatures.excerpt: Vodník is the Czech male water spirit, ruler of rivers and ponds. He appears as a green-clad man with a dripping coat, or as a frog. Uses colored ribbons to lure victims into water, storing their souls in porcelain pots in his underwater palace. Can be benevolent (helping fishermen) or malevolent (drowning bathers). Hi

creatures.name: Vodník
creatures.excerpt: Vodník is the Slovak water spirit, nearly identical to the Czech Vodník. Inhabits Orava region lakes and rivers. Uses ribbons to lure humans, stores drowned souls in pots. His wife appears as a frog; a widespread tale has a woman serve as godmother to the vodník's frog-wife and free captive souls. Can be helpful to fis

creatures.name: Vodun Spirits
creatures.excerpt: Vodun is the Fon/Ewe/Aja religion of Benin/Togo/Ghana venerating hundreds of spirits (vodún) under Nana Buluku and Mawu-Lisa. Key spirits: Legba (crossroads), Sakpata (earth/smallpox), Xêbioso (thunder), Gû (iron/war), Dàn (serpent wealth), Mami Wata (water wealth). Living priesthood tradition; Benin's national religio

creatures.name: Vodyanoy
creatures.excerpt: Vodyanoy (dedushka vodyanoy) is the East Slavic male water spirit, ruler of rivers, lakes, and millponds. Appears as a naked, green-haired old man with a pot belly, covered in slime and weeds, or as a giant catfish/frog. Demands blood sacrifices (livestock, historically human) when mills are built. Helps fishermen who

creatures.name: Vonde-Åsmund
creatures.excerpt: Vonde-Åsmund (Evil Åsmund) is the restless ghost of Åsmund Rygnestad (ca. 1540-1596), a historical outlaw from Rygnestad in the Setesdal valley. Åsmund was a violent, law-defying man who fought as a mercenary in the Dutch war for independence and later built the famous Rygnestadloftet as his fortified storehouse — now

creatures.name: Vukodlak
creatures.excerpt: Vukodlak (volkolak, vovkulaka) is the Slavic werewolf — a human shapeshifter who temporarily becomes a wolf. Most detailed beliefs among Belarusians, Poles, and Ukrainians; South Slavs conflate it with vampires. Transformation via sorcery (rolling over knives, crawling through horse collar), curse, or birth predisposit

creatures.name: Vungu
creatures.excerpt: Vungu (Kenya). is a spirit. Vungu is a spirit from the folklore and mythology of Kenya.. Source: Kenyan folklore — Vungu spirit documented in Kenyan oral tradition.

creatures.name: Väinämöinen
creatures.excerpt: Väinämöinen is the eternal sage and culture hero of Finnish mythology, central figure of Kalevala. Born ancient after Ilmatar's 700-year gestation, shapes world through magical song. Invented kantele from pike's jaw; forged sky's dome in some runic songs. Battles Joukahainen in song, wins, sings him into mire. Quests f

creatures.name: Väki
creatures.excerpt: Väki is not a discrete spirit but the core Finnish concept of supernatural power residing in natural sites, objects, animals — comparable to mana or orenda. Impersonal force, not universal deity.

creatures.name: Vätt
creatures.excerpt: Vätt (Swedish, also vätt, vette, vätte) is a household/land spirit synonymous with tomte/nisse, dwelling under houses, barns, rocks, forests. Small, grey-clad, red-capped. Helpful if respected and fed (Christmas porridge with butter); vengeful if neglected. Shapeshifts (goat, horse, goose). Name from ON vættr ('wight')

creatures.name: Vättar
creatures.excerpt: Vättar (Unknown). is a nature-spirit. Vättar (singular: vätte) are nature spirits in Swedish folklore that live in rocks, caves, and hills. They are similar to the Icelandic Huldufólk and can be either helpful or malicious depending on ho. Source: Swedish folklore tradition

creatures.name: Vågakallen
creatures.excerpt: Vågakallen (the Old Man of Vågan) is the troll king of Lofoten, said to sit on his throne 1,000 meters above sea level in the Lofoten mountains. He was the ruler of the Lofoten trolls and the father of Hestmannen (the Horseman). Vågakallen sat on his mountain throne watching over his kingdom — the Lofoten archipelago,

creatures.name: Vård
creatures.excerpt: Vård (Swedish 'warden') is a nature guardian spirit of a specific place — sacred tree (vårdträd), rock, spring, forest, field. Personifies land's genius loci. Manifests as white deer, snake, bird, light, or elderly humanoid; often felt as invisible presence. Protects those who respect land and leave offerings; punishes

creatures.name: Völva Iceland
creatures.excerpt: Völva Iceland (Unknown). is a witch. A Völva was a female seer and shaman in Norse and Germanic tradition who practiced seiðr magic and prophesied the future. The most famous völva recounts the creation and end of the world in the Völusp. Source: Poetic Edda; Norse sagas; archaeological evidence

creatures.name: Waaq
creatures.excerpt: Waaq (Somali). is a deity. Waaq is the pre-Islamic supreme sky god of the Cushitic peoples of Somalia and the Horn of Africa, associated with rain, fertility, and the natural forces of the sky.. Source: Somali oral tradition, pre-Islamic Somali mythology, Wikipedia - Somali mythology

creatures.name: Wadlim
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a Guatemalan water spirit. No source records a jungle river guardian named 'Wadlim' who keeps the fish and drowns offenders; searches surface only Maine surnames and place names. The nearest attested Maya and Central American water beings that punish disrespect for rivers include the Sigua

creatures.name: Wagyl
creatures.excerpt: Wagyl (also spelled Waugal or Wogal) is the Rainbow Serpent creator being in the mythology of the Noongar people of southwestern Australia. According to Dreamtime stories, Wagyl emerged from the ground and traveled across the land, creating the Swan River, the Avon River, and many other waterways of the southwest. As W

creatures.name: Wairangi
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in documented Māori folklore or academic sources. No dedicated source confirms a trickster figure named Wairangi associated with forests and villages. Māori trickster roles are dominated by Māui, and the recorded traits appear to be a generic trickster composite rather than a named figure fro

creatures.name: Wakan Tanka
creatures.excerpt: Wakan Tanka (Great Mystery or Great Spirit) is the supreme sacred power in Lakota religion, the unified totality of all that is mysterious, powerful, and sacred. Unlike a personified deity in Western traditions, Wakan Tanka is better understood as the sum of all wakan (sacred) forces that permeate the universe. The ter

creatures.name: Wakinyan
creatures.excerpt: Wakinyan is the great Thunderbird of Lakota mythology, a powerful sky spirit associated with thunder, lightning, and storms. His flapping wings create thunderclaps and his eyes flash lightning. When Unhcegila emerged from primordial waters to flood the land, Wakinyan flapped his wings to create a great storm to dry the

creatures.name: Wakinyan Lakota
creatures.excerpt: Wakinyan is the Thunderer of the Lakota, a powerful sky spirit that dwells in the west and appears as a giant bird whose wingbeats roll thunder and whose eye blinks lightning. Wakinyan brings the life-giving rains and, as the enemy of the evil water monsters, keeps the world in balance.

creatures.name: Walumbe
keywords: walumbe, uganda, death personified, baganda mythology, warumbe, kintu and nambi
creatures.excerpt: Walumbe is the personification of death in Baganda mythology, the brother of Nambi and son of the sky god Ggulu. In the creation myth, Walumbe is forbidden by his father from knowing about Kintu—the first man—and his sister Nambi's marriage. When Kintu and Nambi prepared to descend to Earth, Ggulu warned them to leave

creatures.name: Wamala
aliases: the Brother of Mukasa and Kibuka
creatures.excerpt: Wamala is the god of the underworld in Ganda mythology, the third of three powerful divine brothers alongside Mukasa (lake god) and Kibuka (war god). Wamala rules the realm of the dead, a watery underworld beneath Lake Victoria. While Mukasa governs surface waters and life-giving bounty, Wamala rules the dark depths an

creatures.name: Wandjina
creatures.excerpt: The Wandjina are powerful cloud and rain spirits in the beliefs of the Wanjina Wunggurr cultural bloc of northwestern Australia, including the Worrorra, Wunambal, and Ngarinyin peoples of the Kimberley region. According to Dreamtime legends, the Wandjina created the landscape and its inhabitants and continue to influen

creatures.name: Waniwani
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in documented Māori folklore or academic sources. No source confirms a giant monitor lizard or reptile named Waniwani. Māori tradition does record the taniwha, powerful supernatural beings often pictured as giant lizards or lake monsters, and fossil finds of giant moa-eating eagles may have s

creatures.name: Warimu (Kilimanjaro Spirits)
creatures.excerpt: The Warimu (singular: Mrimu) are the mountain spirits of Kilimanjaro in Chaga mythology, ancient guardians inhabiting sacred groves (mshitu) on the mountain's slopes. According to tradition, the Warimu were the original inhabitants of Kilimanjaro before the Chaga arrived. They dwell in patches of virgin forest never cu

creatures.name: Warlock (Loup-Garou)
creatures.excerpt: The loup-garou is the werewolf of French and French-Canadian tradition: a person cursed — often for missing Easter communion seven years running — to become a wolf by night. creatures.name: Warlock (Loup-Garou)
creatures.excerpt: The loup-garou of Acadian and French Canadian tradition is a werewolf, usually imagined as a shaggy dog or bear-like creature rather than a wolf. According to the Canadian Encyclopedia, it was understood as a curse, often the price of failing to perform Easter confession for years, and breakable by drawing its blood. I

creatures.name: Wasgo (Sea Wolf)
creatures.excerpt: Wasgo, the Sea Wolf, is a Haida supernatural being combining wolf and killer-whale features — wolf head and body with the fins and tail of a whale. A crest figure for Haida clans, he crosses between ocean and forest worlds, and his stories teach the fluid boundaries between animal beings in the Haida worldview.

creatures.name: Wasgo Sea Wolf Haida
creatures.excerpt: Wasgo, the sea wolf, is a powerful being of Haida tradition that moves between ocean and land, part wolf and part killer whale. Capable of seizing a whale and of storming the shore, it appears in crest carvings and pole legends as a creature of great supernatural strength linking the sea and the forest.

creatures.name: Watchman (Tupi)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested as a named 'Watchman' in Tupi tradition. Tupi/Guaraní guardianship figures include Jurupari (men's secret cult deity), Tupã (thunder/creator manifestation), and forest owners, but no specific 'Watchman (Tupi)' entity. The generic 'shadowy humanoid at forest edge' description appears fabricate

creatures.name: Watchman (Tupi)
creatures.excerpt: The Tupi-Guarani forest watchman is Curupira, guardian of the hunt: a red-haired, boy-like being with backward feet and a piercing whistle who defends trees and animals. He misleads hunters who take more than they need, making them lose their way in the deep woods, and punishes those who wound or fell without respect.

creatures.name: Water Babies
creatures.excerpt: Water babies are small, crying beings of Great Basin and Plateau tradition, known among the Southern Paiute as pit-u-u and to other nations by related names. creatures.name: Water Dragon (Olmec)
creatures.excerpt: The Olmec Dragon, reconstructed by archaeologist Karl Taube, is a composite water-and-earth deity blending caiman, eagle, jaguar, serpent and human features, with flame-like eyebrows and distinctive L-shaped or trough eyes. Carved at La Venta and San Lorenzo, it is among Mesoamerica's oldest dragon-like beings and fore

creatures.name: Water Horse Iceland
creatures.excerpt: Water Horse Iceland (Unknown). is a animal. The water horse from Icelandic folklore is a deadly Nykur that appears as a tame horse near water.. Source: Icelandic folklore — the water horse/kelpie of Icelandic oral tradition.

creatures.name: Water Spider
creatures.excerpt: In the Cherokee story of how fire came to the people, Water Spider (Dilsdohdi, Kanane'ski Amai'yehi) volunteered when raven, hawk, and the other animals failed. creatures.name: Water Spirits
creatures.excerpt: Water spirits form one of the oldest and widest classes of Native American belief in the United States, though no single being bears the plain name 'water spirit.' Each nation has its own: the horned Underwater Panther of the Great Lakes and East, the water babies of the Great Basin, and the Okwa Naholo of the Choctaw.

creatures.name: Water Spirits
creatures.excerpt: Water spirits are a broad, attested class across Canada's First Nations, though each people knows them by its own names. Among them are the horned great lynx of the Anishinaabe, the water babies of the north, and the Naitaka of Okanagan Lake. They rule the rivers, lakes, and ocean, and ceremonies are offered to them fo

creatures.name: Water Sprinkler (Tó Neinilí)
creatures.excerpt: Water Sprinkler (Tó Neinilí) is a Navajo Holy Person closely associated with water, rain, and all forms of moisture. He works alongside Talking God and other Diyin Dine'é in the creation narratives, helping to shape the sacred mountains and assisting in the emergence from the Third World during the great flood. He crea

creatures.name: Wats'usi (Twin War God)
creatures.excerpt: Wats'usi (Twin War God) is the younger of the sacred twin deities in Zuni mythology, the swift and cunning brother of Ko'wituma. While his elder brother leads the charge against monsters and evil spirits, Wats'usi uses strategy, speed, and clever deception to outmaneuver threats to the Zuni people. He is associated wit

creatures.name: Wee-kin
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested in any recorded Canadian First Nations tradition. No tribal account or published source describes a spirit named Wee-kin, and the name appears to be invented or garbled. creatures.name: Wee-Tent (or Wee-Tin)
creatures.excerpt: Not independently attested under the name Wee-Tent. The Ojibwe and other Anishinaabe peoples do tell of little people, known as Bagwajiwininiwag, 'the wilderness little Anishinaabe,' along with the water-dwelling memengwesi and the mischievous bajiine, but no source names one of them Wee-Tent. The entry appears to be a

creatures.name: Wee-Willie-Winkle
creatures.excerpt: Wee Willie Winkie is a Scottish nursery rhyme character created by poet William Miller in 1841 ('Whistle-Binkie: Stories for the Fireside'), not a folkloric fairy. creatures.name: Weeget Raven Tsimshian
creatures.excerpt: Weeget is the Raven of the Coast Tsimshian, the trickster and creator whose clever thefts gave the people light, fresh water, and salmon. He shapeshifts freely and meddles in the affairs of gods and men, and Tsimshian tellers recount both his world-making deeds and the greed that drives his schemes.

creatures.name: Weeget Txamsem Giant Raven Tsimshian
creatures.excerpt: Txamsem, also called Weeget, is the great raven of the Coast Tsimshian, the creator and trickster who stole the sun and stars to light the world and brought fresh water and the salmon. A being of immense appetite and endless ingenuity, he both made the world and causes its troubles, and his deeds are told in Tsimshian

creatures.name: Weeget Txamsem Raven Tsimshian
creatures.excerpt: Weeget Txamsem is the raven trickster-creator of the Tsimshian, a shapeshifter whose voracious appetite drives his adventures. He steals the sun to light the world, releases the first salmon, and orders the tides and seasons, while his greed and mischief teach the lessons of the adaawx.

creatures.name: Weerwolf
creatures.excerpt: Weerwolf is the Dutch werewolf, documented in 16th–17th century witchcraft trials in the Netherlands. De Blécourt and Meder recorded cases of transformation via devil's salve or wolf-skin belt. Dutch cases clustered 1590s–1620s. Word derives from Middle Dutch weerwolf (man-wolf), cognate with Old English werwulf and Ge

creatures.name: Weiße Frauen
creatures.excerpt: Weiße Frauen are elf-like spirits in German folklore, derived from Norse Ljósálfar (light elves) per Jacob Grimm. Appear at noon bathing in brooks or combing hair, guarding treasure or haunting castles. Their enchantment symbolises Christianity's ban on older divinities (Holda, Perchta, Ostara). Dutch Witte Wieven (wis

creatures.name: Wekufe
creatures.excerpt: Wekufe (Mapuche: 'outside being') are malevolent spirits, a category of soulless entities from Minchenmapu (western evil realm). creatures.name: Well Spirit
creatures.excerpt: Well Spirit (Unknown). is a spirit. A well spirit is a guardian entity from European folklore who dwells in springs and wells, protecting the water source.. Source: Polish folklore; well spirit traditions documented in Slavic folk belief collections.

creatures.name: Wendigo
creatures.excerpt: The wendigo, also spelled windigo, is the cannibal spirit of the Algonquian-speaking peoples, from the Cree and Ojibwe of Canada to the Wampanoag and Pequot of New England. A human possessed by greed and hunger is said to become a gaunt, ice-hearted monster that devours human flesh and never fills its stomach. Scholars

creatures.name: Wenebojo

creatures.name: Were (Nyasaye)
creatures.excerpt: Were (also known as Nyasaye) is the supreme creator god of the Luo people. According to Luo cosmology, Were created the world from primordial waters, fashioning the sky, earth, sun, moon, and stars. creatures.name: Werehyena
creatures.excerpt: The werehyena is a human-hyena shapeshifter of West, East, and Central African folklore. creatures.name: Werewolf
creatures.excerpt: Greek tradition offers the oldest named werewolf: the Arcadian king Lycaon, who tested Zeus by serving human flesh and was transformed into a wolf (Ovid, Metamorphoses).
