stories.title: The Maasai and the Great Lion Hunt

stories.name: The Maasai Origin of Fire
stories.excerpt: Long ago, the Maasai lived without fire, eating their food raw and shivering through cold nights. stories.title: The Maasai Origin of Fire

stories.name: The Maboyo of the Layou
stories.excerpt: A colossal serpent spirit guards the deepest pools of the Layou River, and those who offend the waters risk being dragged beneath the surface forever.
stories.title: The Maboyo of the Layou

stories.name: The Magic Book

stories.excerpt: A poor musician discovers a magical guitar that brings uncontrollable joy and dance to all who hear it.

stories.title: The Magic Scythe

stories.excerpt: An evil magician lives in a mountain palace filled with frightened young girls he has stolen from their families. stories.title: The Magician's Cape

stories.excerpt: A poor boy named Olle (or Theo in some versions) is always wishing for things he cannot afford — a knife, a sled, a horse and carriage. stories.title: The Magpie with Salt on Her Tail

stories.name: The Maiden in the Castle of Rosy Clouds
stories.excerpt: A poor, hardworking young man (named Cedric in some versions) collapses from exhaustion and dreams of a beautiful fairy maiden who walks out of rosy clouds and invites him to find her. stories.title: The Maiden in the Castle of Rosy Clouds

stories.excerpt: A Zuni story about the beautiful daughter of the high priest of the Village of the Yellow Rocks. Despite her beauty, her pride and coldness drove away suitors. stories.title: The Maiden of the Yellow Rocks

stories.title: The Maiden the Sun Made Love To

stories.excerpt: A Navajo story about a young woman who transformed into a bear after being mistreated by her family or community. stories.title: The Maiden Who Became a Bear

stories.name: The Making of the Mojo Bag
stories.excerpt: Mojo bags—small red flannel pouches filled with roots, herbs, coins, and personal objects—are central to Hoodoo practice, and their creation is surrounded by elaborate lore. stories.title: The Making of the Mojo Bag

stories.excerpt: A lonely hunter meets and marries a beautiful woman, only to discover that she is actually a fox in human form. stories.title: The Man and the Fox Wife

stories.name: The Man and the Girl at the Underground Mansion

stories.excerpt: A surreal narrative describing a journey to a hidden subterranean world, exploring themes of the subconscious and the mysteries of the underground.
stories.title: The Man and the Girl at the Underground Mansion

stories.name: The Man and the Seven Rams
stories.excerpt: A Crow man of immense ability and power once encountered the Seven Rams, magnificent creatures of the mountains. The man, confident in his strength, thought he could overpower them. stories.title: The Man and the Seven Rams

stories.name: The Man Who Carried Sickness Out of the Village

stories.title: The Man Who Carried Sickness Out of the Village

stories.excerpt: A wicked man named Kalle Kula dies on Holy Innocents' Day and finds himself caught between Heaven and Hell, bargaining for his soul with a blend of humor and desperation. stories.title: The Man Who Died on Holy Innocents' Day

stories.name: The Mapinguari of the Xingu
stories.excerpt: A giant, foul-smelling beast with backward feet guards the deepest parts of the Amazon, and the hunter who pursues it finds the jungle turned against him.

stories.name: The Marquesan Hero Nukuhiva

stories.title: The Marquesan Hero Nukuhiva

stories.excerpt: A Cree hunter marries a woman who is secretly a marten spirit, and when she returns to the forest, he must choose between his world and hers.
stories.title: The Marten's Wife

stories.name: The Master and His Apprentice

stories.excerpt: A young man becomes a 'Master Thief' through his extraordinary cunning. He outwits a farmer, a priest, and a squire, eventually winning the hand of the squire's daughter by proving his skills.

stories.title: The Mbari Houses of Ala (Igbo)

stories.title: The Menehune: Hawaii's Hidden Builders

stories.title: The Mi'kmaq Creation Story (Seven Levels of Creation)

stories.title: The Migoi: Bhutan's Yeti Legends

stories.title: The Moose and the Sun

stories.title: The Mossy Rock (Blackfoot)

stories.title: The Myth of the Djinn of the Hoggar Mountains

stories.title: The Nahurac: Spirit Animal Lodges

stories.title: The Natchez Great Sun and Tattooed Serpent (Natchez)

stories.excerpt: A determined young violinist makes a dark bargain with Näcken, the water spirit, trading his most beloved animals for the ability to play music that can move the world.
stories.title: The Neck's Violin

stories.name: The Necken's Enchanted Violin
stories.excerpt: Deep in the forests of Sweden, where the pine trees grow so thick that sunlight filters through the needles like light through stained glass, there runs a river called the Silverån.
stories.title: The Necken's Enchanted Violin

stories.name: The Ngoma Drums of the Swahili Coast
stories.excerpt: The ngoma drum is sacred along the entire Swahili coast, serving as both musical instrument and spiritual vessel. According to legend, the first ngoma was given to the people by sea spirits (pepo) who rose from the Indian Ocean during a storm. The drum's voice could summon rain, heal the sick, and communicate with ance
stories.title: The Ngoma Drums of the Swahili Coast

stories.name: The Night Marchers
stories.excerpt: In Hawaii, when the sun dips below the Pacific and the shadows of the volcanic peaks stretch across the land like dark fingers, the wise ones stay indoors.
stories.title: The Night Marchers

stories.name: The Night Marchers of Hawaii
stories.excerpt: The Huaka'i Po (Night Marchers) are ghostly processions of ancient Hawaiian warrior spirits who march along traditional pathways on moonlit nights. Led by fire-wielding priests and accompanied by the sound of conch shells and war chants, they travel to sacred sites and battlefields. They can appear as torches floating
stories.title: The Night Marchers of Hawaii

stories.name: the Night-Walker, Shadow of the Savanna
stories.excerpt: A shadow that walks the savanna at night, taking the shape of anyone who has ever died — and if you see it, it will take your shape next, so that someone, someday, will see you walking where you have never been.
stories.title: the Night-Walker, Shadow of the Savanna

stories.name: The Nightingale
stories.excerpt: An emperor prefers a mechanical, jeweled bird over a real nightingale, only to realize the true, irreplaceable value of natural beauty and song.
stories.title: The Nightingale

stories.name: The Nisse and the Christmas Porridge
stories.excerpt: A house spirit (Nisse) demands his Christmas porridge with a pat of butter on top. When a farmer skimps on the butter, the Nisse plays terrible tricks until properly fed.
stories.title: The Nisse and the Christmas Porridge

stories.name: The Nisse's Barn Revenge
stories.excerpt: Every traditional farm is said to have a Nisse, a small wight who protects the animals and the property. If the farmer treats the Nisse with respect and provides a bowl of porridge with butter on Christmas Eve, the farm prospers. However, if insulted, the Nisse will sabotage the barn and terrorize the livestock.
stories.title: The Nisse's Barn Revenge

stories.name: The Nix of the Millpond
stories.excerpt: A miller's daughter must outsmart a malevolent water spirit to save her brother from a desperate bargain made by her father.
stories.title: The Nix of the Millpond

stories.name: The Nixie's Song
stories.excerpt: By the old millpond on the edge of the Black Forest, where the water lay still and dark under the shadow of the willows, there lived a nixie.
stories.title: The Nixie's Song

stories.name: The Nommo Descend in the Ark of Sirius
stories.excerpt: After the Pale Fox disrupted creation, Amma sent the Nommo, twin amphibious beings half-human and half-fish, to restore order. They descended from the star Sirius (Sigi Tolo) in a spinning copper ark that traced a spiral path to Earth. The ark landed at the Bandiagara Escarpment in Mali, where the Nommo stepped out car
stories.title: The Nommo Descend in the Ark of Sirius

stories.name: The Nun's Priest Tale
stories.excerpt: In the bustling streets of 14th-century Florence, where merchants hawked their wares and the scent of fresh bread mingled with the aroma of roasting meat, there lived a priest whose appetite for earthly pleasures far exceeded his devotion to spiritual matters.
stories.title: The Nun's Priest Tale

stories.name: The Nunnehi: Cherokee Spirit People (Cherokee)
stories.excerpt: The Nunnehi, meaning 'The Travelers' or 'Those Who Live Anywhere,' are a race of invisible spirit people who dwell in the mountains and forests of Cherokee country. They are friendly toward humans and often appear as regal Cherokee warriors. The Nunnehi are said to be great dancers and musicians; travelers sometimes he
stories.title: The Nunnehi: Cherokee Spirit People (Cherokee)

stories.name: The Nutcracker and the Mouse King
stories.excerpt: The Monkey King, Sun Wukong, is the greatest trickster in all of Chinese mythology.
stories.title: The Nutcracker and the Mouse King

stories.name: The Nuxalk Origin of the Sun (Nuxalk)
stories.excerpt: The Nuxalk people tell that before the sun existed, there was only the dim light of copper-colored darkness. The people prayed constantly to Alhkw'ntam, the Creator, for light. In Nusmata, the house of the gods in the upper world, the Creator's granddaughter Skimina lived. The Four Carpenters created Raven (Qwaxw) from
stories.title: The Nuxalk Origin of the Sun (Nuxalk)

stories.name: the Nyonyose, Spirit Behind the Mask
stories.excerpt: When the mask dancer puts on the Nyonyose mask, the human disappears and the ancestor speaks — because in Burkina Faso, the dead do not leave, they wait behind the mask.
stories.title: the Nyonyose, Spirit Behind the Mask

stories.name: The Näcken – Water Fiddler of Åland's Lakes and Streams
stories.excerpt: The Näcken (Näkk in Finnish Swedish) is a male water spirit who sits naked among the reeds or under waterfalls, playing hauntingly beautiful violin music. His playing is irresistibly seductive, luring listeners — especially children and young women — toward the water, where they drown. However, the Näcken can be outwit
stories.title: The Näcken – Water Fiddler of Åland's Lakes and Streams

stories.name: The Näckens Violin
stories.excerpt: By the dark lake in Hälsingland, where the water is black even in daylight, there lived a fiddler named Anders who could play as no other in the village.
stories.title: The Näckens Violin

stories.name: The Nāga Fireballs of the Mekong
stories.excerpt: An enduring Thai legend surrounding the mysterious Nāga fireballs (Bang Fai Phaya Nak) that rise from the Mekong River each year during the full moon of the 11th lunar month (October). According to tradition, the serpent king Phaya Nāga who dwells beneath the Mekong releases these glowing red orbs — ranging from tiny s
stories.title: The Nāga Fireballs of the Mekong

stories.name: The Nāga of the Mekong: Guardian Serpent of Laos
stories.excerpt: In Lao mythology, the Nāga (Ngueak in Lao) is the most powerful and revered supernatural being — a great serpent deity that dwells in the Mekong River and serves as the guardian spirit of the Lao people. According to legend, the Mekong River was created by the Nāga king as he slithered across the land, carving the rive
stories.title: The Nāga of the Mekong: Guardian Serpent of Laos

stories.name: The Obambo That Would Not Cross
stories.excerpt: When a man dies before completing his life's work, his Obambo ghost lingers at the river crossing between the world of the living and the dead, unable to move on until his unfinished task is completed.
stories.title: The Obambo That Would Not Cross

stories.name: The Ocean Spider's Gaze
stories.excerpt: A skilled kayaker paddling near Godthaab notices the sea floor is unexpectedly shallow. He recalls warnings about the Ocean Spider, a massive creature that lurks beneath the waves. Just as he realizes the danger, he sees a giant eye staring back at him from the depths. Thanks to his agility and quick reactions, he mana
stories.title: The Ocean Spider's Gaze

stories.name: The Octopus Spirit of the Coastal Waters
stories.excerpt: The Octopus Water-Spirit of the Cameroonian coast taught the Douala people the art of diving and gathering shellfish, but demanded they never harvest from the coral beds where her children slept.
stories.title: The Octopus Spirit of the Coastal Waters

stories.name: The Ogbanje Spirit (Igbo)
stories.excerpt: The Ogbanje is a malevolent reincarnating spirit in Igbo cosmology that deliberately plagues a family by being born, dying young, and then being reborn to the same mother repeatedly. These spirits cause endless grief to families, with children dying before puberty in each cycle. The Igbo believe that each Ogbanje burie
stories.title: The Ogbanje Spirit (Igbo)

stories.name: The Old Dame and her Hen
stories.excerpt: An old woman's hen is stolen by a Man of the Hill. Her three daughters search for it; the first two are killed, but the youngest outwits the ogre and rescues her sisters.
stories.title: The Old Dame and her Hen

stories.name: The Old Troll of Big Mountain
stories.excerpt: A poor cottager and his wife own little more than a small cottage, two goats, and their five-year-old son Olle. While they work as day laborers, they lock Olle in the cottage with bread and milk, letting the goats graze in an enclosure. One evening, they return to find both goats gone — the evil old troll of Big Mounta
stories.title: The Old Troll of Big Mountain

stories.name: The Old Woman and the Fish
stories.excerpt: An old woman catches a talking pike that grants three wishes: that her pails fetch water by themselves, that whatever she strikes breaks right off, and that whatever she pulls becomes long. Each wish backfires—she slaps her knees in delight and breaks her legs off, then blows her nose and it grows terribly long.
stories.title: The Old Woman and the Fish

stories.name: The Old Woman and the Origin of the Sea
stories.excerpt: Among the Baining people of New Britain, Papua New Guinea, a myth explains how the sea was created. In the beginning, the sea was only a tiny waterhole from which an old woman extracted saltwater to flavor her food, keeping it hidden under a cover of tapa cloth. One day, her sons became curious and tore open the cover.
stories.title: The Old Woman and the Origin of the Sea

stories.name: The Old Woman and the Tramp
stories.excerpt: A clever tramp talks a stingy old woman into giving him shelter, then tricks her into contributing ingredients one by one to make 'nail broth'—starting with a nail and adding oatmeal, beef, potatoes, barley, milk, and brandy until they feast together.
stories.title: The Old Woman and the Tramp

stories.name: the Orang Bunian, the Hidden People
stories.excerpt: A race of invisible beings who live alongside humans in the same forests and villages, visible only to those with the gift, because in Singapore the world is wider than you can see.
stories.title: the Orang Bunian, the Hidden People

stories.name: The Origin of Breadfruit
stories.excerpt: During a terrible famine in Tahiti, the people prayed to the gods for deliverance. The god Rongo, moved by their suffering, transformed himself into a great breadfruit tree. The tree bore fruit that tasted like fresh bread when roasted, saving the people from starvation. Each part of the tree proved useful—the fruit as
stories.title: The Origin of Breadfruit

stories.name: The Origin of Corn
stories.excerpt: The gods create humans from corn after failing with mud and wood, establishing maize as the sacred foundation of Maya civilization.
stories.title: The Origin of Corn

stories.name: The Origin of Corn (Pueblo)
stories.excerpt: In Pueblo mythology, corn was a gift from the Holy People. The origin story varies between communities but commonly involves a culture hero or deity who obtained corn from the underworld or from supernatural beings. In one version, the Corn Maidens (Blue Corn Maiden, Yellow Corn Maiden, etc.) brought corn to the people
stories.title: The Origin of Corn (Pueblo)

stories.name: The Origin of Corn: First Mother's Sacrifice
stories.excerpt: In the time of the first people, the Abenaki were hungry. Gluskabe's grandmother Nokomes taught the people to survive on wild plants, but food was scarce. First Mother, the first woman created by Gichi Niwaskw and Gluskabe, saw her children starving. She told her husband to kill her and drag her body across a clearing.
stories.title: The Origin of Corn: First Mother's Sacrifice

stories.name: The Origin of Death in Ambrym
stories.excerpt: On the island of Ambrym in Vanuatu, a myth explains how death came into the world. After the creation of humanity, the good deities proposed that humans should shed their skin like snakes, preserving their youthful appearance forever and living eternally. However, the evil deities disagreed, arguing that when humans gr
stories.title: The Origin of Death in Ambrym

stories.name: The Origin of Disease and Medicine (Cherokee)
stories.excerpt: Long ago, all plants, animals, and humans lived together in harmony, and animals were larger and stronger. As the human population grew, they began killing animals without respect. The animals held councils to decide how to protect themselves. The Deer council decreed that any hunter who killed a deer without asking fo
stories.title: The Origin of Disease and Medicine (Cherokee)

stories.name: The Origin of Fire
stories.excerpt: How fire first came to the world, stolen from the gods for the benefit of humanity.
stories.title: The Origin of Fire

stories.name: The Origin of Fire (Motu People)
stories.excerpt: Among the Motu people of southern Papua New Guinea, a myth tells that the ancestors originally ate all food raw because they had no fire. One day, smoke was seen rising far out at sea. A dog volunteered to investigate the source, swimming across the water. The dog reached an island where women were cooking with fire. S
stories.title: The Origin of Fire (Motu People)

stories.name: The Origin of Ganesha's Elephant Head
stories.excerpt: Goddess Parvati, longing for a son, created a boy from sandalwood paste and turmeric from her own body, breathed life into him, and appointed him as her guardian while she bathed. When Lord Shiva returned and tried to enter, the boy — who had never met his father — stopped him, obeying his mother's command. Enraged by
stories.title: The Origin of Ganesha's Elephant Head

stories.name: The Origin of Hmong New Year (Noj Peb Caug)
stories.excerpt: The Hmong New Year legend explains the origins of the most important celebration in Hmong culture — Noj Peb Caug (Eat Thirty), marking the end of the agricultural cycle. According to Hmong oral tradition, in ancient times the spirit of the New Year (Xyoo Tshiab) was a powerful deity who traveled through the villages br
stories.title: The Origin of Hmong New Year (Noj Peb Caug)

stories.name: The Origin of Kava
stories.excerpt: A Tongan chief and his wife prayed to the gods for a child. Their prayers were answered with a son, but he was born with leprosy. The grief-stricken parents buried the child, and from his grave grew two plants—a tall, branching plant (the kava) and a shorter broad-leafed plant (the sugarcane). A wandering spirit discov
stories.title: The Origin of Kava

stories.name: The Origin of Kava in Fiji
stories.excerpt: In Fijian oral tradition, the origin of kava (yaqona) is tied to a sacred ritual. According to legend, a chief and his followers were instructed by the gods to perform a ceremonial planting. From a specific plant, the roots were discovered to produce a potent drink that connected the drinker to the spirit world. The pr
stories.title: The Origin of Kava in Fiji

stories.name: The Origin of Lake Victoria
stories.excerpt: Long ago, the land where Lake Victoria now sits was a lush valley filled with prosperous villages. But the people grew greedy and forgot to honor Were with sacrifices. Were sent a great flood as punishment, but one old woman named Nyanjala was warned by a spirit. She gathered her family and a few animals and climbed to
stories.title: The Origin of Lake Victoria

stories.name: The Origin of Maple Sugar (Wenebojo and the Maple Trees)
stories.excerpt: Long ago, when Wenebojo was wandering the earth, he discovered that the maple trees produced thick, sweet syrup that flowed freely from their trunks. The people had only to collect it and drink their fill. Wenebojo, being lazy and greedy, drank so much that he became sick. Angrily believing the trees had tricked him, h
stories.title: The Origin of Maple Sugar (Wenebojo and the Maple Trees)

stories.name: The Origin of Sedna
stories.excerpt: Sedna, once a mortal girl, is betrayed by her father after fleeing a bird-husband. As she clings to the side of her father's kayak during a storm, he cuts off her fingers to save the boat. As her fingers fall into the sea, they transform into the first whales, seals, and walruses. Sedna sinks to the bottom of the ocean
stories.title: The Origin of Sedna

stories.name: The Origin of the Apsara Dancers
stories.excerpt: According to Khmer mythology, the Apsaras are celestial dancers born from the churning of the Ocean of Milk — a Hindu creation myth adopted and deeply embedded in Cambodian culture. The story tells of the devas (gods) and asuras (demons) who churned the cosmic ocean using Mount Mandara as a churning rod and the serpent
stories.title: The Origin of the Apsara Dancers

stories.name: The Origin of the Chaga People
stories.excerpt: According to Chaga tradition, the first Chaga people emerged from the sacred caves on the slopes of Kilimanjaro. Long ago, a great famine drove people from the surrounding plains to seek refuge on the mountain's fertile slopes. There, Ruwa led them to hidden caves where underground rivers flowed and the soil was eterna
stories.title: The Origin of the Chaga People

stories.name: The Origin of the Coconut Tree in the Maldives
stories.excerpt: Maldivian mythology explains the origin of the coconut tree — the nation's most vital resource — through a poignant legend. When the first settlers arrived on the barren coral islands of the Maldives, they found no plants and struggled to survive. Many died, and tragedy struck nearly every family. A sorcerer (fandita m
stories.title: The Origin of the Coconut Tree in the Maldives

stories.name: The Origin of the Horsehead Fiddle (Morin Khuur)
stories.excerpt: A shepherd named Namjil the Cuckoo from eastern Mongolia was drafted into military service on the western border. He sang so beautifully that people called him Namjil the Cuckoo. During his service, he fell in love with a local prince's daughter, who gave him a magical winged horse to cross the vast distances to meet h
stories.title: The Origin of the Horsehead Fiddle (Morin Khuur)

stories.name: The Origin of the Hummingbird
stories.excerpt: In the time of the Maya, before the great cities fell to jungle, there lived a young warrior named Utz that was the finest in his tribe—strong, swift, brave in battle.
stories.title: The Origin of the Hummingbird

stories.name: The Origin of the Medicine Pipe
stories.excerpt: A beautiful woman appeared to a Blackfoot man who had gone on a vision quest. She gave him a pipe decorated with eagle feathers and taught him the prayers and songs that went with it. She told him the pipe would be a mediator between the people and the spirit world. When he returned to camp, the elders recognized the p
stories.title: The Origin of the Medicine Pipe

stories.name: The Origin of the Stars
stories.excerpt: A myth explaining the placement of stars in the night sky. It describes a celestial event where fragments of a great spirit or cosmic object were scattered across the heavens. These stars serve as a map for the Inuit, linking the physical world to the ancestral realm and providing direction for navigation across the ic
stories.title: The Origin of the Stars

stories.name: The Origin of the Sun Dance (Cheyenne)
stories.excerpt: The Sun Dance was given to the Cheyenne by the culture heroes Sweet Medicine and Erect Horns. Sweet Medicine brought the Sacred Arrows and the structure of the Sun Dance from his journey to the Sacred Mountain. The Sun Dance is held each summer when the tribe gathers to renew their connection to Ma'heo'o. Dancers fast
stories.title: The Origin of the Sun Dance (Cheyenne)

stories.name: The Origin of the Thunderbird (Wabanaki)
stories.excerpt: In the Wabanaki tradition, the Thunderbird was once a great chief who loved his people so much that after his death, the Great Spirit transformed him into a giant bird whose wings make the thunder and whose eyes flash lightning. He was given dominion over the sky and tasked with hunting the great horned serpent Weewill
stories.title: The Origin of the Thunderbird (Wabanaki)

stories.name: The Origin of the Tiki
stories.excerpt: In the timeless era before the world was fully awakened, when the heavens and earth were still locked in a cold, silent embrace, there existed a longing for life.
stories.title: The Origin of the Tiki

stories.name: The Origin of Throat Singing (Khöömei)
stories.excerpt: The Tuvan legend explaining the origin of khöömei throat singing, the unique overtone singing technique of the Tuvan people recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. According to the myth, long ago a young Tuvan hunter became lost in the Sayan Mountains during a blizzard. Desperate and alone, he began to mi
stories.title: The Origin of Throat Singing (Khöömei)

stories.name: The Owl Husband (Passamaquoddy)
stories.excerpt: A beautiful young Passamaquoddy woman was visited each night by a mysterious man who came to her lodge after dark. He was kind and gentle, and she grew to love him, though she had never seen his face clearly. Her parents warned her to discover his identity. One night, she placed ashes near the doorway. When the man lef
stories.title: The Owl Husband (Passamaquoddy)

stories.name: The Owl Wife
stories.excerpt: A young hunter finds a beautiful woman sleeping under an owl skin, but when he steals the skin, she is trapped in human form — and the owls come looking for her.
stories.title: The Owl Wife

stories.name: The Painted Skin
stories.excerpt: In Taiyuan, during the Ming Dynasty, there lived a scholar named Wang. Centers on Demon, the concepts of absolute evil, temptation, and the consequences of moral failure..
stories.title: The Painted Skin

stories.name: The Pale Fox and the Divination Grid
stories.excerpt: Yurugu the Pale Fox (Ogo), the first being of Dogon creation born from Amma's flawed act, limps across the Sahel on uneven legs as the living embodiment of disorder. Despite his chaotic nature, Yurugu serves a vital purpose in Dogon society through divination. Each night, Dogon diviners draw a rectangular grid in fine
stories.title: The Pale Fox and the Divination Grid

stories.name: The Panchatantra: The Lion and the Rabbit
stories.excerpt: In a great forest of India, there lived a mighty lion named Dhandara. Centers on Gwyllion, mountain folklore. Causes disorientation and getting lost - represents dangerous mountain paths..
stories.title: The Panchatantra: The Lion and the Rabbit

stories.name: The Panther Deity of the Chaco
stories.excerpt: A black panther spirit guards the western Chaco, and the farmer who clears its land without offering will find his crops burned by invisible fire.
stories.title: The Panther Deity of the Chaco

stories.name: The Papa-Figo of Salvador
stories.excerpt: A ghoulish figure in a top hat devours the figs — the vital organs — of the living, and only the protection of the orixás can ward it off.
stories.title: The Papa-Figo of Salvador

stories.name: The Parikhan Lantern
stories.excerpt: A ghost who carries a lantern through the mountain fog is said to guide lost travelers home, though those who follow too eagerly may never find their way back.
stories.title: The Parikhan Lantern

stories.name: The Parson and the Clerk
stories.excerpt: A miserly parson who refuses charity disguises himself as a tramp to turn away beggars. The clever clerk, also in disguise, torments the parson all night by pretending his corn has been spilled and his cattle let loose, while impersonating the parson to his wife. The terrified parson reforms and becomes generous.
stories.title: The Parson and the Clerk

stories.name: The Patasola
stories.excerpt: A one-legged forest creature lures men into the jungle with the voice of their loved ones.
stories.title: The Patasola

stories.name: The Pathfinder — Aigin's Revenge
stories.excerpt: The famous Sámi legend adapted into the 1987 Oscar-nominated film. Circa 1000 AD in Finnmark, a young Sámi man named Aigin returns from hunting to find his family massacred by Chude raiders. He escapes to another Sámi community, but the Chudes follow. The noaidi Raste hides with Aigin but is tortured. Aigin reveals him
stories.title: The Pathfinder — Aigin's Revenge

stories.name: The Pawnee Capture of the Sacred Arrows
stories.excerpt: Around 1830, the Cheyenne attacked a Skidi Pawnee hunting party in central Nebraska, carrying their most sacred possession—the Maahótse (Four Sacred Arrows) bundle. During the battle, the Pawnee captured the sacred arrows, described as the greatest disaster in Cheyenne history. The Cheyenne made replica arrows and desp
stories.title: The Pawnee Capture of the Sacred Arrows

stories.name: The People Could Fly
stories.excerpt: In this beloved African American folktale collected by Virginia Hamilton, enslaved Africans secretly retained the magical ability to fly—a power brought from their homeland. One day, as an old man named Toby worked in the cotton fields under a cruel overseer's lash, he began to whisper ancient words in a language the o
stories.title: The People Could Fly

stories.name: The Peri (Fairy Spirits of Persian Myth)
stories.excerpt: Peris are beautiful, benevolent winged spirits in Persian mythology, originally fallen angels in Zoroastrian tradition who later became more benign in Islamic Persian folklore. They are depicted as exquisite beings who dwell in the lower heavens and enchant humans with their beauty. Peris are locked in eternal conflict
stories.title: The Peri (Fairy Spirits of Persian Myth)

stories.name: The Peri and the Poet
stories.excerpt: A grieving poet is visited by a Peri, a celestial spirit of Persian-Azerbaijani myth, who offers him a choice between forgetting his sorrow and learning its deeper meaning.
stories.title: The Peri and the Poet

stories.name: the Phujku, the Harvest Demon
stories.excerpt: A skeletal figure wrapped in dead corn husks stalks the fields at harvest time, draining the life from crops — and only the sound of bells and singing can drive it back to the earth.
stories.title: the Phujku, the Harvest Demon

stories.name: The Piath of the Baobab Grove
stories.excerpt: A monstrous Piath haunted the baobab grove near Renk, stealing children who wandered too far from the village, until a clever girl turned its own hunger against it and banished it to the dry wastes beyond the river.
stories.title: The Piath of the Baobab Grove

stories.name: The Pied Piper of Hamelin
stories.excerpt: In the year 1284, the German town of Hamelin suffered a plague unlike any other.
stories.title: The Pied Piper of Hamelin

stories.name: The Pig King
stories.excerpt: A princess must break the enchantment of a pig-like king, learning that true beauty lies within.
stories.title: The Pig King

stories.name: The Pipe of Peace Treaty
stories.excerpt: The sacred pipe given by White Buffalo Calf Woman serves as the ultimate symbol of peace among the Lakota. When two warring tribes wished to end hostilities, they would smoke the pipe together. The pipe bowl, made of red stone, represents the earth; the wooden stem represents all that grows upon the earth. The smoke ri
stories.title: The Pipe of Peace Treaty

stories.name: The Pishtaco of the Mountain
stories.excerpt: A white-skinned stranger with a silver knife appears in mountain villages at night, draining the fat from sleeping farmers — because fat, in Aymara belief, is the substance of the soul.
stories.title: The Pishtaco of the Mountain

stories.name: The Plague
stories.excerpt: In Swedish folk tradition, the devastating plagues were personified as a boy with a rake and a girl with a broom, wandering from village to village. Where the boy raked, some were spared; where the girl swept, death left an empty house. On Soller Island, the plague spirits strewed gold along the roads, but the treasure
stories.title: The Plague

stories.name: The Plat-Eye
stories.excerpt: The Plat-Eye is a malevolent, shapeshifting spirit in Gullah Geechee folklore, believed to be the restless ghost of a person who was wronged in life and died with unfinished business. The Plat-Eye takes various forms—an animal with one large glowing eye, a ball of light, or a shadowy figure—and haunts the place of its
stories.title: The Plat-Eye

stories.name: The Polar Bear Son
stories.excerpt: A woman, unable to have children, adopts a polar bear cub. As the cub grows, it develops human intelligence and speech, becoming a protector and companion to the woman. The story emphasizes unconventional family bonds and the deep respect the Inuit hold for the polar bear as a sentient being.
stories.title: The Polar Bear Son

stories.name: The Polkan at the Ridge
stories.excerpt: A shepherd boy encounters the Polkan shapeshifter on a mountain ridge and survives by offering it neither fear nor aggression, but a riddle it cannot answer without revealing its true form.
stories.title: The Polkan at the Ridge

stories.name: The Poludnitsa in the Wheat
stories.excerpt: A noonday spirit in a white dress haunts the wheat fields at midday, and the reaper who works through the heat will meet her and never work again.
stories.title: The Poludnitsa in the Wheat

stories.name: The Pond Spirit Who Danced
stories.excerpt: A water spirit who lives in a forest pond teaches a lonely boy to dance, and the dance becomes the boy's gift to the village.
stories.title: The Pond Spirit Who Danced

stories.name: the Pontianak of the Coast
stories.excerpt: A Pontianak who haunts the coastal roads of eastern Singapore, appearing as a woman with a baby, because in Singapore the sea and the dead are never far apart.
stories.title: the Pontianak of the Coast

stories.name: the Pontianak, the Vampire Bride
stories.excerpt: A beautiful woman in white who appears on lonely roads at night, her long black hair hiding a face that is not a face, because in Singapore beauty is the deadliest weapon.
stories.title: the Pontianak, the Vampire Bride

stories.name: The Poor Devil
stories.excerpt: When a peasant prays for his cow's protection, God and the Devil argue over who truly controls fate — leading to a wager that reveals the Devil's limitations and God's grace. This tale from Småland is at once humorous and philosophical.
stories.title: The Poor Devil

stories.name: The Poor Turkey Girl
stories.excerpt: A Zuni Cinderella-like story about a poor girl who was mistreated by her community and found companionship among the wild turkeys. The turkeys, taking pity on her, transformed her appearance with beautiful clothing and feathers so she could attend a sacred dance at the village. She danced beautifully and won the heart
stories.title: The Poor Turkey Girl

stories.name: The Porcupine and the Beaver (Tsimshian)
stories.excerpt: This Tsimshian myth from the William Beynon collection tells of a time when animals spoke like human beings and possessed great powers to change the weather. Porcupine and Beaver, two animal-people, had a contest of abilities that determined their roles in the world. Porcupine demonstrated his cleverness and defensive
stories.title: The Porcupine and the Beaver (Tsimshian)

stories.name: The Prairie-Dogs and Their Priest the Burrowing-Owl
stories.excerpt: A Zuni story about a village of Prairie-dogs who were suffering from a drought. They held a council and decided to ask their grandfather, the Burrowing-owl who lived on top of their mountain, for help. The Burrowing-owl, a powerful priest, agreed to intercede with the rain gods. He collected a foul-smelling beetle and
stories.title: The Prairie-Dogs and Their Priest the Burrowing-Owl

stories.name: The Prince and the Princess in the Forest
keywords: the prince and the princess in the forest
stories.excerpt: A romantic tale of two lovers separated by tragic circumstances and reunited through magic and enduring love in a mystical forest setting.
stories.title: The Prince and the Princess in the Forest

stories.name: The Princess and the Glass Mountain
stories.excerpt: A princess sits atop a treacherous glass mountain, and the man who can ride to the top wins her hand — a poor boy with a magic horse succeeds where knights fail. The princess is a relative of Brunhilde of Germanic heroic legend, and the tale is very popular across the North.
stories.title: The Princess and the Glass Mountain

stories.name: The Princess and the Pea
stories.excerpt: Once upon a time, in a kingdom of rolling green hills and turreted castles, there lived a prince who searched the world for a true princess to marry.
stories.title: The Princess and the Pea

stories.name: The Princess in the Chest
stories.excerpt: A tale of a princess hidden away in a chest for her safety, and the subsequent quest by a brave hero to find and rescue her.
stories.title: The Princess in the Chest

stories.name: The Princess on the Glass Hill
stories.excerpt: A determined young man seeks to win the hand of a princess who resides atop an impenetrable glass hill. Through his bravery, wit, and the help of magical entities, he overcomes the obstacles and ascends the hill to claim his bride.
stories.title: The Princess on the Glass Hill

stories.name: The Psoglav of the Unmarked Graves
stories.excerpt: A monstrous hound with a human face and a single eye in its forehead feeds on the forgotten dead buried without crosses, and those who hear its digging at night know which graves the village tried to erase.
stories.title: The Psoglav of the Unmarked Graves

stories.name: the Psoglav, the One-Eyed Dog
stories.excerpt: A creature with a dog's body, a human face, and a single eye in the center of its forehead that feeds on the dead in unmarked graves — because in Montenegro, some graves are unmarked for a reason.
stories.title: the Psoglav, the One-Eyed Dog

stories.name: The Pueblo Emergence from the Underworld
stories.excerpt: A central Pueblo creation theme across multiple Pueblo tribes (Acoma, Zuni, Hopi, Laguna, etc.) involves the emergence of the first people from the underworld through a sacred opening called the sipapu. In the beginning, the people lived in darkness beneath the earth. Guided by spirits, culture heroes, or twin war gods
stories.title: The Pueblo Emergence from the Underworld

stories.name: The Pueblo Hero Twins
stories.excerpt: In Pueblo mythology, the Twin War Gods (Masewi and Oyoyewi in some traditions) are the most important heroic figures. They were born to a virgin mother who conceived from the Sun, much like the Navajo Hero Twins. These twins are credited with creating the world and all living creatures, as well as slaying a giant monst
stories.title: The Pueblo Hero Twins

stories.name: The Qalupalik
stories.excerpt: A humanoid sea creature with green skin and long fingernails drags children who wander too close to the ice edge beneath the water.
stories.title: The Qalupalik

stories.name: The Queen
stories.excerpt: Queen Adelgunda possesses a remarkable gift: she can see into the hearts of men. This power makes her a wise and just ruler, but it also creates complications. When the noble Sigmund — whom the queen secretly loves — is accused of dishonorable intentions, the queen's gift suggests his guilt. To save Sigmund from the di
stories.title: The Queen

stories.name: The Queen Bee
stories.excerpt: Two kings' sons once set out on a grand adventure, but they fell into wild and reckless ways and never returned home.
stories.title: The Queen Bee

stories.name: The Queen's Necklace
stories.excerpt: The cruel King Hendrik possesses a necklace of one hundred perfect pearls. He forces his nephew to find him a wife, and the kind Blanzeflor is chosen. On their wedding day, the king fastens the pearls around her neck with a threat: the day she is found without them will be her last. Blanzeflor, trapped in a cold marria
stories.title: The Queen's Necklace

stories.name: The Quilting Party Ghost
stories.excerpt: A classic Gullah ghost story set in the Sea Islands of Georgia. A group of women gathered for a quilting party at an old cabin on St. Helena Island. As they worked on the quilt by lantern light, they told stories to pass the night. An old woman named Sarah, whose grandmother had been enslaved on the plantation before t
stories.title: The Quilting Party Ghost

stories.name: The Rabbit Trickster (Chickasaw)
stories.excerpt: Chukfi (or Chokfi), the Rabbit, is the trickster figure in Chickasaw folklore. Rabbit is clever, mischievous, and always getting into trouble, but he also uses his wits to benefit the people. In one story, Rabbit outwits the wolves by pretending to be dead and then escaping when they are not looking. In another, he tri
stories.title: The Rabbit Trickster (Chickasaw)

stories.name: The Rabbit Trickster of the Kongo
stories.excerpt: Among the Kongo, the rabbit (sometimes called Nsumunu) is the greatest of all tricksters, smaller than nearly every other creature but cleverer than them all. In the most famous tale, Rabbit grew tired of drinking from muddy puddles while the great elephant and hippo drank from the clear river. Rabbit challenged them t
stories.title: The Rabbit Trickster of the Kongo

stories.name: The Race of Good and Evil
stories.excerpt: After the world was made, Good and Evil existed as two brothers. Evil constantly spoiled Good's work, making stony places and poisonous fruits. Good decided to destroy Evil. He proposed a race, and each brother had to reveal his greatest fear. Evil feared buck's horns; Good feared braided Indian grass. Evil filled Good
stories.title: The Race of Good and Evil

stories.name: The Rain Princess of the Sotho
stories.excerpt: Sotho oral tradition tells of a rain princess who possessed the power to control the weather and bring fertility to the land. In times of drought, the Sotho people would perform ceremonies to honor the rain princess and her connection to Modimo, the supreme god. The princess was both a spiritual figure and a political
stories.title: The Rain Princess of the Sotho

stories.name: The Rainbow Serpent and the Creation of the Land
stories.excerpt: The Rainbow Serpent (known by many names across Australia including Julunggul, Kunmanggur, and Wagyl) is one of the most widespread and significant creator beings in Aboriginal Australian mythology. In the Dreamtime, the great Rainbow Serpent traveled across the land, creating rivers, gorges, mountains, and waterholes
stories.title: The Rainbow Serpent and the Creation of the Land

stories.name: The Rainbow Snake
stories.excerpt: The great creator serpent of Aboriginal Australian mythology who shaped the land and rivers.
stories.title: The Rainbow Snake

stories.name: The Rainmaker of the Kalahari
stories.excerpt: In the shimmering, amber expanses of the Kalahari, where the horizon trembles in the heat and the earth is a mosaic of cracked clay, rain is not merely weather—it is the difference between existence and extinction.
stories.title: The Rainmaker of the Kalahari

stories.name: The Raven and the Whale
stories.excerpt: A Chukchi story from the Kuutkh cycle describing how the Raven creator interacted with the primordial whale. In this tale, Kuutkh encounters a giant whale that threatens the newly created world. Through a combination of trickery and negotiation, the Raven convinces the whale to accept boundaries for its territory, esta
stories.title: The Raven and the Whale

stories.name: The Re-Creation of the Sacred Mountains
stories.excerpt: After emerging into the Fourth World, First Man, First Woman, Water Sprinkler, and Black God re-created the six sacred mountains from dirt First Man had brought from the Third World. They placed Sisnaajiní (Blanca Peak) in the East, decorated with white shells, white lightning, white corn, and dark clouds for male rain
stories.title: The Re-Creation of the Sacred Mountains

stories.name: The Red Cloak
stories.excerpt: In the old days of the Crusades, when Christian knights traveled to the Holy Land to fight what they were told were enemies of the faith, there was a knight of Brittany called Sir Guillaume le Rouge—William the Red.
stories.title: The Red Cloak

stories.name: The Red Headband of Grande Comore
stories.excerpt: A fisherman discovers that the forest spirits wear crimson headbands to mark those they have chosen to protect, and learns that the boundary between the human world and the spirit world is thinner than the strand of a fishing net.
stories.title: The Red Headband of Grande Comore

stories.name: The Red Robin of Wales
stories.excerpt: A small bird endures the fires of hell to bring comfort to suffering souls, becoming an eternal symbol of compassion and hope.
stories.title: The Red Robin of Wales

stories.name: The Red Shoes
stories.excerpt: There was once a little girl named Karen, pretty and delicate, but so poor that she wore wooden shoes in winter that chafed her ankles raw.
stories.title: The Red Shoes

stories.name: The Release of the Buffalo (Arapaho)
stories.excerpt: In the time before buffalo roamed the plains, all the buffalo were confined in a cave beneath a mountain, guarded by a powerful spirit. The Arapaho people had only small game and were often hungry. A young man on a vision quest learned from a mouse spirit that the buffalo were hidden underground. With the help of vario
stories.title: The Release of the Buffalo (Arapaho)

stories.name: The Release of the Wild Animals
stories.excerpt: In the beginning, all wild animals were confined in a great underground cavern by a spirit who wanted to protect them. The Comanche people had only dogs and horses. A brave warrior followed a trail to the cavern entrance and heard the stamping and snorting of many animals within. With the help of the wind spirit, he op
stories.title: The Release of the Wild Animals

stories.name: The Riddle of the Mountain Troll
stories.excerpt: A traveler is captured by a mountain troll who agrees to let him go only if he can solve three impossible riddles. The traveler uses his wit and knowledge of the natural world to outsmart the troll, proving that intelligence is more powerful than brute strength.
stories.title: The Riddle of the Mountain Troll

stories.name: The Ride of the Wild Hunt
stories.excerpt: During the darkest nights of winter, the sky is filled with the screams of the Wild Hunt. Led by a ghostly chieftain or Odin himself, the hunt consists of spirits and hounds that gallop across the clouds. Those caught in the path of the hunt are swept away to the spirit realm forever.
stories.title: The Ride of the Wild Hunt

stories.name: The Ring
stories.excerpt: A young prince rides out in the moonlight and finds a tiny ring by the shore — a delicate band with blue stones arranged like a forget-me-not flower. He picks it up and puts it in his pocket. The ring belongs to a captive princess who, as a child, was taken from her mountain castle when a foreign conqueror killed her f
stories.title: The Ring

stories.name: The Riri Yaksha and Suniyam Sorcery Legends
stories.excerpt: The Riri Yaksha (Blood Demon) is one of the most feared demonic figures in Sinhalese folklore, central to the Bali and Tovil exorcism traditions. According to legend, Riri Yaksha was born from the blood of a slain demon, possessing enormous power and an insatiable thirst. The Suniyam demon, associated with sorcery and
stories.title: The Riri Yaksha and Suniyam Sorcery Legends

stories.name: The Rise of the Kraken
stories.excerpt: Sailors in the north often reported seeing a massive island of skerries emerging from the sea. In reality, this was the Kraken, a colossal cephalopod. The creature creates massive whirlpools as it sinks back into the depths, dragging entire ships down with it in a swirl of tentacles and foam.
stories.title: The Rise of the Kraken

stories.name: The Rival Suitors
stories.excerpt: Several heroes of Kalevala, including Wainamoinen and Lemminkainen, compete for the hand of the Daughter of Pohjola. The competition is characterized by a mixture of physical strength and magical ingenuity, as each hero attempts to prove themselves the most worthy suitor.
stories.title: The Rival Suitors

stories.name: The River-Shutter of Delagoa
stories.excerpt: When a greedy fisherman begins taking more from the bay of Delagoa than he returns, the great water spirit Kambujanu rises to teach him the difference between harvest and theft.
stories.title: The River-Shutter of Delagoa

stories.name: The Roc
stories.excerpt: There are birds, and then there is the Roc. Centers on Roc, from Saudi Arabia mythology. Known for nature manipulation and animal communication and wind control..
stories.title: The Roc

stories.name: The Rolling Calf
stories.excerpt: One of Jamaica's most feared duppies, the Rolling Calf appears as a massive jet-black bull with blazing red eyes that gash fire, dragging heavy chains that clank and spark as it moves. It haunts lonely roads, bridle paths through cane fields, and crossroads at night. The Rolling Calf is believed to be the restless spir
stories.title: The Rolling Calf

stories.name: The Rolling Calf of St. Joseph
stories.excerpt: A monstrous bull with a chain of fire around its neck roams the roads at night, chasing down those who break their word or cruelty to animals.
stories.title: The Rolling Calf of St. Joseph

stories.name: The Rolling Stone Legend (Cheyenne)
stories.excerpt: A Cheyenne boy was left in camp while the adults went hunting. A mysterious rolling stone appeared and began chasing him. The boy ran for his life, but the stone rolled faster and faster, crushing everything in its path. The boy encountered various animals who tried to help—a magpie pecked at the stone, a badger dug a
stories.title: The Rolling Stone Legend (Cheyenne)

stories.name: The Rooster of Barcelinhos
stories.excerpt: On the West African coast, in the dense mangrove swamps and lagoons of Nigeria, there is a spirit that every fisherman knows.
stories.title: The Rooster of Barcelinhos

stories.name: The Rooster, the Hand-Mill and the Swarm of Hornets
stories.excerpt: A poor peasant trades a pig for three seemingly worthless gifts — a rooster, a hand-mill, and a hornets' nest — but each proves invaluable when he outwits a greedy innkeeper. The gold-laying rooster is a widely known international folktale motif.
stories.title: The Rooster, the Hand-Mill and the Swarm of Hornets

stories.name: The Rusalka of Lake Ilmen
stories.excerpt: A drowned maiden haunts the waters of Lake Ilmen, singing songs that lure fishermen to their deaths during the green weeks of spring.
stories.title: The Rusalka of Lake Ilmen

stories.name: The Russian Fortress of Bomarsund – A Cursed Ruin
stories.excerpt: The unfinished fortress of Bomarsund, built by Russia between 1832 and 1854, is one of Åland's most evocative historical sites. Local folklore holds that the fortress was cursed from the start — built on ground that was never meant to be fortified. Thousands of laborers, prisoners, and soldiers worked on the project, w
stories.title: The Russian Fortress of Bomarsund – A Cursed Ruin

stories.name: The Saci Who Stole the Wind
stories.excerpt: A one-legged trickster with a red cap steals the wind from a village, and only a clever grandmother with a pair of scissors can catch him.
stories.title: The Saci Who Stole the Wind

stories.name: The Sacred Drum of the Luba Realm
stories.excerpt: According to Luba tradition, the first sacred drum was given to the people by the spirit of the forest. It was said to have the voice of the ancestors, and its beat could be heard across the entire kingdom. The drum contained the soul of the Luba nation — as long as it beat, the kingdom would endure. The Luba kings (mu
stories.title: The Sacred Drum of the Luba Realm

stories.name: The Sacred Groves of the Chaga
stories.excerpt: The Chaga people maintain sacred groves (mshitu) on the slopes of Kilimanjaro, patches of virgin forest that are never cut or farmed. According to tradition, these groves are the dwelling places of the mountain spirits (warimu) who protect the Chaga people. The largest and most sacred grove is said to be where Ruwa him
stories.title: The Sacred Groves of the Chaga

stories.name: The Sacred Pipe (Blackfoot)
stories.excerpt: The Blackfoot believe the sacred pipe was given to them by the Thunder spirit, who taught them the songs and rituals for its use. A man once heard thunder and saw a lightning-struck tree. Where the lightning had struck, he found a beautifully carved pipe. The Thunder spirit spoke to him, instructing him to form a socie
stories.title: The Sacred Pipe (Blackfoot)

stories.name: The Sacred Sieidi Stones
stories.excerpt: Legends about sieidis—unusual rock formations considered sacred dwelling places of spirits. Each family had its local sieidi. Offerings of reindeer meat, antlers, and fish were made for hunting luck and protection. The Storjunkare were stones resembling humans or animals, set up on mountain tops. They had power over al
stories.title: The Sacred Sieidi Stones

stories.name: the Saka, the Possessing Spirit
stories.excerpt: A spirit that attaches itself to a family line, growing stronger with each generation, demanding offerings that escalate from flowers to blood, because in Singapore some debts are inherited.
stories.title: the Saka, the Possessing Spirit

stories.name: The Saltvik Runestone – Serpent of the Norse Sea
stories.excerpt: The Saltvik runestone is a second significant Viking-age monument on Åland, located in the Saltvik parish north of Mariehamn. Like the Jomala stone, it is carved with runic inscriptions in the Younger Futhark, its serpentine bands curling like waves around the ancient alphabet. The stone marks the connection between Ål
stories.title: The Saltvik Runestone – Serpent of the Norse Sea

stories.name: The Sampo Lost In the Sea
stories.excerpt: During the fierce struggle to escape Pohjola, the Sampo is broken into pieces and falls into the sea. While the main machine is lost, fragments of the Sampo wash ashore, continuing to bring wealth and luck to the land of Kalevala.
stories.title: The Sampo Lost In the Sea

stories.name: The Sand Jinn and the Lost Son
stories.excerpt: A young Soninke boy separated from his family during a sandstorm is found by a sand jinn who offers him safe passage in exchange for a piece of his memory.
stories.title: The Sand Jinn and the Lost Son

stories.name: The Sausage
stories.excerpt: A mysterious lady borrows a woman's brewing pan and grants her three wishes in return. Eager to please her hungry husband, the woman wishes for a sausage—then her angry husband wishes it stuck to her nose. Their last wish must be used to remove it.
stories.title: The Sausage

stories.name: The Sayona Who Watched from the River
stories.excerpt: A beautiful woman lures unfaithful men to the riverbank at dusk, then tears away her skin to reveal a white skeleton that demands they confess their sins before dawn.
stories.title: The Sayona Who Watched from the River

stories.name: The Scorpion Spirit of the Chokwe
stories.excerpt: A scorpion spirit punishes a greedy chief who hoards the harvest, teaching the Chokwe people that generosity is the price of leadership and sting is the cost of selfishness.
stories.title: The Scorpion Spirit of the Chokwe

stories.name: the Sea Beast of Raouche
stories.excerpt: A creature that lurks in the caves beneath the Raouche Rocks, emerging only during storms to pull fishermen beneath the waves — because Beirut's most famous landmark hides Beirut's most dangerous secret.
stories.title: the Sea Beast of Raouche

stories.name: The Sea Draugr – Ghost of Drowned Sailors
stories.excerpt: In the Nordic maritime tradition that extends to Åland, the draugr or sea draug is the restless spirit of a drowned sailor. It appears as a figure in oilskins with a head of seaweed, sailing in half a boat. The sea draugr serves as an omen of impending drowning: if a fisherman sees the draug or hears its cries, his own
stories.title: The Sea Draugr – Ghost of Drowned Sailors

stories.name: The Sea Draugr's Warning
stories.excerpt: The Sea Draugr is the spirit of a man who drowned at sea, appearing as a pale, bloated corpse with a head made of seaweed. He wanders the coastlines during storms, calling out to sailors and attempting to lure them into the surf to join him in the freezing depths of the ocean.
stories.title: The Sea Draugr's Warning

stories.name: The Sea Island Creation Frog
stories.excerpt: In Gullah Geechee creation folklore, the frog was one of the first creatures and played a crucial role in shaping the Sea Islands. The story tells that in the beginning, there was only water everywhere. The Creator needed someone to dive to the bottom and bring up mud to make land. All the big animals tried and failed—
stories.title: The Sea Island Creation Frog

stories.name: The Sea Nymph
stories.excerpt: One night on the northwest shores of the island of Gotland, fishermen sleeping in a hut see a white, dew-besprinkled woman's hand reaching through the door. They recognize it as a sea nymph seeking to destroy them, and pretend to be asleep. The next day, a young, newly married man from Kinnar in Lummelund joins them. H
stories.title: The Sea Nymph

stories.name: The Sea Spirit Tolk
stories.excerpt: A Nivkh legend about Tol (or Tolk), the powerful sea spirit who governs the waters around Sakhalin Island and the Sea of Okhotsk. Tolk is a massive creature that controls the movement of fish, the intensity of storms, and the success of sea mammal hunts. Before embarking on sea voyages, Nivkh hunters and fishermen woul
stories.title: The Sea Spirit Tolk

stories.name: The Sea Wolf (Wasgo) (Haida)
stories.excerpt: Wasgo the Sea Wolf is a powerful supernatural being in Haida mythology, a creature that combines the features of a wolf and a whale. He possesses the strength of both land and sea animals and serves as an important crest figure for Haida clans. In the narratives, Wasgo descends from a supernatural lineage and mediates
stories.title: The Sea Wolf (Wasgo) (Haida)

stories.name: The Secret World of the Huldufólk
stories.excerpt: The Huldufólk, or Hidden People, are a race of elegant and powerful beings who live inside the rocks and mountains. They are generally peaceful but can be vengeful if their homes are disturbed. Many roads in Iceland are diverted to avoid disturbing these unseen neighbors and their dwellings.
stories.title: The Secret World of the Huldufólk

stories.name: The Sedna Hunter's Wife
stories.excerpt: A Cree hunter's wife is taken by the wind and must navigate the spirit world to return home, aided by the animals she once cared for.
stories.title: The Sedna Hunter's Wife

stories.name: The Selkie Bride
stories.excerpt: A man steals the skin of a seal-woman to make her his wife, but learns that a love born of theft can never truly hold a spirit of the sea.
stories.title: The Selkie Bride

stories.name: The Selkie Wife
stories.excerpt: A solitary man captures a selkie's skin to force her into marriage, discovering that love built on captivity can never truly replace the pull of the ocean.
stories.title: The Selkie Wife

stories.name: The Selkie's Stolen Skin
stories.excerpt: A group of selkies, seal-people who can shed their skins to become human, visit the shore to dance. A man steals one of the skins, preventing a female selkie from returning to the sea. He forces her to marry him, and though she lives as a human for years, she eventually finds her skin and returns to the ocean.
stories.title: The Selkie's Stolen Skin

stories.name: The Separation of the Hmong Clans
stories.excerpt: According to Hmong oral tradition, in the earliest times all Hmong people belonged to a single clan and lived together in harmony. But as the population grew, disputes arose, and it became impossible for everyone to live under one roof. The ancestors sought divine guidance and were told in a vision that the people must
stories.title: The Separation of the Hmong Clans

stories.name: The Separation of Women and Men
stories.excerpt: In Navajo mythology, First Woman boasted that women could live without men, claiming she thanked her vagina for the deer First Man brought. Enraged, First Man led all men and the two hermaphrodite twins across the river to the north bank. For four years, the sexes lived apart. Women tried to satisfy themselves with bon
stories.title: The Separation of Women and Men

stories.name: The Seri Gumum Dragon of Tasik Chini
stories.excerpt: Malaysia's answer to the Loch Ness Monster: Seri Gumum is a legendary dragon (naga) said to dwell in the depths of Tasik Chini in Pahang, a pristine lake surrounded by ancient rainforest. According to Orang Asli legend, the dragon was once a princess transformed into a serpentine guardian of the lake's mystical waters.
stories.title: The Seri Gumum Dragon of Tasik Chini

stories.name: The Serpent of the Sea (Kolowisi)
stories.excerpt: A Zuni legend about Kolowisi, the great horned water serpent that lives in the sacred lake. A maiden from Zuni went to the lake and was seen by Kolowisi, who took her as his bride beneath the waters. She lived with the serpent in his underwater home, where there was no light but she was treated well and given abundance
stories.title: The Serpent of the Sea (Kolowisi)

stories.name: The Serpent Rainbow Ayida-Weddo (Fon/Dahomey)
stories.excerpt: Ayida-Weddo is the rainbow serpent, the androgynous cosmic serpent who supports the world. According to Fon cosmology, the universe is held up by Ayida-Weddo, who coils beneath the earth and stretches into the sky as the rainbow. When the serpent moves beneath the ocean, it causes earthquakes and tidal waves. Ayida-Wed
stories.title: The Serpent Rainbow Ayida-Weddo (Fon/Dahomey)

stories.name: The Seven Foals
stories.excerpt: Three brothers attempt to win a princess by watching seven magical foals for a day. While the elder brothers are lazy and fail, the youngest, Boots, discovers the foals' true identity as princes and helps them break a curse.
stories.title: The Seven Foals

stories.name: The Seven Hanging Poems (Mu'allaqat)
stories.excerpt: A collection of seven long pre-Islamic Arabic poems considered the finest examples of ancient Arabian poetry, traditionally said to have been written in gold on Coptic linen and hung from the Kaaba in Mecca. The seven poets are Imru' al-Qais, Tarafa, Zuhayr, Labid, Antarah, Amr ibn Kulthum, and Harith ibn Hilliza. Each
stories.title: The Seven Hanging Poems (Mu'allaqat)

stories.name: The Seven Reindeer of the Sky
stories.excerpt: A Nenets celestial myth about seven magical reindeer that traverse the sky, forming the constellation that guides Nenets reindeer herders on their seasonal migrations. According to the legend, the seven reindeer were originally earthly animals belonging to a great shaman who could fly. When the shaman ascended to the s
stories.title: The Seven Reindeer of the Sky

stories.name: The Seven Sacred Rites
stories.excerpt: White Buffalo Calf Woman gave the Lakota people the Seven Sacred Rites that would guide their spiritual life. The rites are: 1) Keeping of the Soul (preserving the spirit of the deceased for a year before release); 2) The Purification Rite (sweat lodge ceremony for cleansing); 3) Crying for a Vision (vision quest for g
stories.title: The Seven Sacred Rites

stories.name: The Seven Sisters (Pleiades) Dreaming
stories.excerpt: The Seven Sisters is a widespread Aboriginal Australian Dreaming story found across many language groups. The story tells of seven sisters who fled across the land and into the sky to escape a persistent pursuer, often a man named Wurrurrumbi or a hunter who wanted to take one of the sisters as his wife. As they fled,
stories.title: The Seven Sisters (Pleiades) Dreaming

stories.name: The Seven Wishes
stories.excerpt: Olle Niklasson is a thirteen-year-old boy who is exceptionally ugly, lazy, and stupid. His hair resembles a dried juniper bush, his cheeks like swollen fly agaric mushrooms, and he is so lazy he barely moves when he falls. Even the magpies laugh at him. One day in the forest, Olle sees a viper staring down a frog that
stories.title: The Seven Wishes

stories.name: The Shadow
stories.excerpt: A wise man lived in a northern land, and he was content with his life—except that he was always overshadowed by other men.
stories.title: The Shadow

stories.name: The Shaman's Canoe Journey to the Underworld
stories.excerpt: A Nanai shamanic epic describing a powerful shaman's journey in his spirit-canoe to the underworld (buni) to retrieve a dying person's soul. According to Nanai tradition, the underworld is a mirror of the world above but reversed — the rivers flow backward and the seasons are opposite. The shaman must navigate treacher
stories.title: The Shaman's Canoe Journey to the Underworld

stories.name: The Shaman's Journey to the Spirit World
stories.excerpt: Altai legend tells of the first shaman, named Jaangara, who was taught the art of kamlanie (shamanic journeying) by Erlik himself. According to the story, a nobleman fell ill and called upon Jaangara to heal him. As Jaangara drummed and entered a trance, his spirit traveled up the sacred tree Bay-Terek to the sky world
stories.title: The Shaman's Journey to the Spirit World

stories.name: The Shark as Provider
stories.excerpt: A mother and daughter are abandoned by their kin and left to starve. Their fortunes change when a dead seal washes ashore, followed by a talking shark that rises from the deep. The shark promises to protect and provide for them, eventually carrying them and all their possessions on its back to a safe, remote island to
stories.title: The Shark as Provider

stories.name: The Sheep and the Pig Who Set up House
stories.excerpt: A sheep and a pig decide to partner up and create a household. The story follows their comedic attempts at domestic management, showcasing the friction and eventual cooperation required to maintain a home.
stories.title: The Sheep and the Pig Who Set up House

stories.name: The Shipwrecked Sailor
stories.excerpt: An ancient Egyptian literary tale from the Middle Kingdom (c. 2000 BCE), the Shipwrecked Sailor tells of a sailor who survives a storm that sinks his ship, killing all his companions. He washes ashore on a magical island filled with food, fruit, and fish. After offering thanks to the gods, he hears a thunderous noise a
stories.title: The Shipwrecked Sailor

stories.name: The Shtriga: The Vampire Witch of Albanian Folklore
stories.excerpt: An ancient witch feeds on the life force of infants, escaping through keyholes in the form of a flying insect.
stories.title: The Shtriga: The Vampire Witch of Albanian Folklore

stories.name: The Siguanaba and the Lovesick Boy
stories.excerpt: A beautiful woman with a horse's face appears to young men walking alone at night, seducing them with her beauty before revealing her true monstrous form.
stories.title: The Siguanaba and the Lovesick Boy

stories.name: The Silversmith and the Moon
stories.excerpt: A beloved Hmong folktale tells the story of a master silversmith who created the most beautiful silver jewelry in all the land. His work was so exquisite that the Moon herself, looking down from the sky, fell in love with his craftsmanship. Each night, the Moon crept closer to earth to admire the silversmith's work. Th
stories.title: The Silversmith and the Moon

stories.name: The Simorgh and the Prince
stories.excerpt: A Persian prince is saved by a magical bird, the Simorgh, who teaches him the value of promises.
stories.title: The Simorgh and the Prince

stories.name: The Simurgh and the Burning Garden
stories.excerpt: The great Simurgh descends from Mount Qaf to heal a garden scorched by divine fire, teaching a village the difference between destruction and renewal.
stories.title: The Simurgh and the Burning Garden

stories.name: The Sipapu Emergence
stories.excerpt: In one version of the Hopi emergence story, the people of the Third World grew wicked and corrupt. With the help of Spider Grandmother or bird spirits, a hollow bamboo reed grew at the opening between the Third World and the Fourth World. This opening, called the sipapu, is traditionally located at the Grand Canyon. On
stories.title: The Sipapu Emergence

stories.name: the Sisimito of the Rainforest
stories.excerpt: A hairy ape-like creature that guards the deep rainforest, punishing those who hunt too greedily and rewarding those who respect the balance.
stories.title: the Sisimito of the Rainforest

stories.name: The Six Initiation Societies of the Bambara
stories.excerpt: Bambara spiritual life is organized through six initiatory societies: N'domo, Komo, Nama, Kono, Tyiwara, and Kore. Each society represents a stage of knowledge and spiritual development, guiding members from childhood through full spiritual maturity. The Komo society, one of the most powerful, preserves esoteric knowle
stories.title: The Six Initiation Societies of the Bambara

stories.name: The Six Servants
stories.excerpt: A prince travels with six extraordinary servants who each possess unique abilities (super hearing, super sight, super strength, etc.). Together they overcome impossible challenges to win a princess.
stories.title: The Six Servants

stories.name: The Six Swans
stories.excerpt: A silent princess endures hardship to save her brothers from a wicked enchantment.
stories.title: The Six Swans

stories.name: The Sjörå – Lady of the Baltic Sea
stories.excerpt: The sjörå (sea spirit) is a guardian entity of the Baltic waters surrounding the Åland archipelago. She appears as a beautiful woman, sometimes described as hollow-backed like the skogsrå, who can calm storms or raise tempests depending on how she is treated. Fishermen and sailors traditionally greeted her with respect
stories.title: The Sjörå – Lady of the Baltic Sea

stories.name: The Skalunda Giant
stories.excerpt: A giant who fled Skalunda mountain because of church bells meets shipwrecked sailors from his homeland, tests their blood with a red-hot iron bar, and sends a magical girdle home that uproots an oak tree.
stories.title: The Skalunda Giant

stories.name: The Skin Satchel
stories.excerpt: Hunger and need have fallen upon Niklas's village. He accidentally witnesses a troll take six grains from a leather satchel and in minutes grow an entire field of wheat. He resolves to obtain the magic satchel, but the treasure is hard to find and even harder to keep. The satchel can only be found at night but must be
stories.title: The Skin Satchel

stories.name: The Skitters
stories.excerpt: In the remote glens of Scotland, where the mist lingers between the hills and the old ways still hold sway, there are tales of creatures so small and so terrible that they make the bravest men tremble.
stories.title: The Skitters

stories.name: The Skogsrå and the Hunter
stories.excerpt: In the deep forests of Västmanland, where the trees grow so thick that summer days are dim, there lived a hunter named Erik who was the pride of his village.
stories.title: The Skogsrå and the Hunter

stories.name: The Skogsrå – Forest Spirit of Åland's Woodlands
stories.excerpt: The skogsrå (forest spirit) is a female nature spirit found throughout Swedish-speaking regions including Åland. She appears as a beautiful woman from the front, but seen from behind she has a hollow, rotten back and often a cow's tail or one horse foot. She lures men deep into the forests, leading them astray into swa
stories.title: The Skogsrå – Forest Spirit of Åland's Woodlands

stories.name: The Slave Who Became a Buzzard
stories.excerpt: A Gullah version of the Flying Africans legend, recorded by the Federal Writers' Project in the late 1930s. Wallace Quarterman, a Gullah man born in 1844 on Sapelo Island, Georgia, recounted that the Igbo people who drowned at Dunbar Creek did not die at all. According to the oral tradition passed down through generati
stories.title: The Slave Who Became a Buzzard

stories.name: The Slaying of Déélgééd the Horned Monster
stories.excerpt: After defeating Yéʼiitsoh, the Hero Twins faced Déélgééd, the Horned Monster, a creatures described as having one horn and living in the water. In some versions the monster was a giant water creature with a single horn. Monster Slayer and Child of the Water tracked it to its lair. Monster Slayer shot the creature multi
stories.title: The Slaying of Déélgééd the Horned Monster

stories.name: The Slaying of Yéʼiitsoh
stories.excerpt: Monster Slayer's greatest feat in Navajo tradition was killing Yéʼiitsoh, the Big Giant, who wore armor of flint knives on his legs. The Hero Twins approached him after their father the Sun had weakened the giant by striking him four times. Monster Slayer shot an arrow into the giant's leg armor but it shattered; a sec
stories.title: The Slaying of Yéʼiitsoh

stories.name: The Snatcher of the Dubai Alleyways
stories.excerpt: When children begin vanishing from the lanes of old Dubai, a grandmother traces the disappearances to Khattaf Rafai, the demon who steals children with whispered promises.
stories.title: The Snatcher of the Dubai Alleyways

stories.name: The Snegurochka Who Melted
stories.excerpt: A girl made of snow falls in love with a shepherd, but when she tries to kiss him, she melts into a puddle of spring water.
stories.title: The Snegurochka Who Melted

stories.name: The Snow Leopard of Mount Kailash
stories.excerpt: A wandering pilgrim lost on the slopes of Mount Kailash encounters a spectral snow leopard who guides him through a blizzard — but the path she chooses leads not to the monastery, but to the place within himself he has spent a lifetime avoiding.
stories.title: The Snow Leopard of Mount Kailash

stories.name: The Snow Queen
stories.excerpt: A courageous girl journeys to the frozen ends of the earth to rescue her friend from the Snow Queen's icy grip.
stories.title: The Snow Queen

stories.name: The Son of the Sun's Courting in the Land of the Giants
stories.excerpt: The epic origin myth of the Sámi people. Beaivvi bárdni (the Son of the Sun) sails beyond the easternmost star to the land of the giants to seek a bride. He wins the giant's daughter through strength and cunning. The giant's daughter ties three knots in the wind to help them escape her pursuing brothers—untying each kn
stories.title: The Son of the Sun's Courting in the Land of the Giants

stories.name: the Sonangi, the Rain Child
stories.excerpt: A child-shaped spirit that appears in the rain, following travelers on mountain paths — and if you turn to look at it, you will hear its voice calling your name until the rain stops.
stories.title: the Sonangi, the Rain Child

stories.name: The Song of the Forest Sprite
stories.excerpt: In the rare forests of the north, a sprite is said to play a flute that can put any human to sleep. Those who fall asleep to the melody enter a dream world where they are tempted with riches and power, but they can only wake up if they find the strength to ignore the sprite's promises.
stories.title: The Song of the Forest Sprite

stories.name: The Song of the Mermaids of Black Rocks
stories.excerpt: A young fisherman ignoring his grandmother's warnings sails past the Black Rocks at twilight and hears the mermaids' song, nearly meeting his doom on the volcanic stones.
stories.title: The Song of the Mermaids of Black Rocks

stories.name: The Sorceress of Oyndarfjørður
stories.excerpt: The Rinkusteinar legend in its more detailed form. Long ago, when Irish pirates attacked Fuglafjørður, they killed, robbed, and terrorized the village before setting sail for Oyndarfjørður. An old witch (sorceress) living in Oyndarfjørður saw them coming and rushed to the shore. She raised her arms and cast a powerful
stories.title: The Sorceress of Oyndarfjørður

stories.name: The Soucouyant of Chalky Mount
stories.excerpt: An old woman sheds her skin at night, becomes a ball of fire, and flies through the darkness to feed on the blood of infants, leaving telltale marks on their sleeping bodies.
stories.title: The Soucouyant of Chalky Mount

stories.name: The Soucouyant of Roseau
stories.excerpt: An old woman sheds her skin each night to become a fireball that preys on the blood of sleeping villagers, until a clever young woman discovers her secret.
stories.title: The Soucouyant of Roseau

stories.name: The Soucouyant of Vieux Fort
stories.excerpt: An old woman suspected of being a soucouyant is exposed when a clever girl discovers the jar of fire where the creature hides its skin at night.
stories.title: The Soucouyant of Vieux Fort

stories.name: The Soucouyant, the Vampire of Trinidad
stories.excerpt: The Soucouyant is one of the most feared beings in Trinidadian folklore — a vampire-like creature who appears by day as a harmless old woman living alone in a shack with shuttered windows. At midnight, she sheds her human skin, hiding it in a wooden mortar, and transforms into a searing ball of fire that slips through
stories.title: The Soucouyant, the Vampire of Trinidad

stories.name: The Soungoula and the Sleeping Children
stories.excerpt: A vampiric spirit called Soungoula slips into homes at night to drain the breath from sleeping children, leaving them pale and listless until a healer performs the right ceremony.
stories.title: The Soungoula and the Sleeping Children

stories.name: The Specter in Fjelkinge
stories.excerpt: An innocent man is wrongly executed, and his ghost appears to the true murderer night after night until justice is done and his soul can finally rest. The tale is founded on the ancient belief that innocent blood calls for atonement.
stories.title: The Specter in Fjelkinge

stories.name: The Spider Trickster and the Sugar Kings
stories.excerpt: When the sugar planters of Mauritius grew too wealthy and too cruel, the Spider Trickster wove a web of illusions that turned their fortune against them.
stories.title: The Spider Trickster and the Sugar Kings

stories.name: The Spirit of Kilimanjaro
stories.excerpt: A Chaga legend tells of a poor hunter named Mushi who lost his way in the dense forest on Kilimanjaro's slopes. After days of wandering, starving and exhausted, Mushi came upon a clearing where an old woman sat beside a fire. The old woman was the spirit of the mountain, though Mushi did not know it. She gave him food
stories.title: The Spirit of Kilimanjaro

stories.name: The Spirit of the Black Sands
stories.excerpt: On the shores of the south, a spirit is said to appear as a small child guiding travelers away from the dangerous sneaker waves. However, if the traveler is greedy or unkind, the spirit leads them directly into the crashing surf, where the ocean claims them as a sacrifice.
stories.title: The Spirit of the Black Sands

stories.name: The Spirit of the Great River
stories.excerpt: A young Fang hunter must navigate the secrets of the forest and appease the river spirits to save his village from a devastating drought.
stories.title: The Spirit of the Great River
